FortiManager version 7.6.8 trying to install ssl-ssh-profile settings that are not supported on 2GB FortiGate devices
topics.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps for installation failure in FortiManager version 7.6.8 due to the 'udp-not-quic' option under 'config firewall ssl-ssh-profile' when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory.ScopeFortiManager. SolutionIn version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation to fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS version 7.6.This behavior is due to a known issue, with ID 1352524.Workaround: Set 'udp-not-quic' to 'block' in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Set udp-not-quic to block in the https and dot sections of the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Go to Policy & Objects -> Advanced.Select the CLI Configurations tab.In the left pane, under firewall, select ssl-ssh-profile.Select the affected profile (for example, custom-deep-inspection), then select Edit.In the Edit firewall ssl-ssh-profile window, scroll to the https section and set udp-not-quic to block.Scroll to the dot section and set udp-not-quic to block.Select OK.Repeat steps 4 to 7 for each SSL/SSH profile that is used by the 2GB FortiGate devices.Install the policy package again.Note: Some models may not accept this setting. For example, a comment on this article reports 'Operation not supported. detail: object not support' on a FortiGate 50G. Contact Fortinet Support if the error persists.Fix: A fix is expected in FortiManager firmware versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.3.Related document:Known issues

topics.title: Administrator SSO authentication fails after upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionAfter upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login for FortiGate administrators with Entra ID acting as SAML IdP.Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP, for example see Configuring single-sign-on in the Security Fabric.Confirmed not affected:VPN user SSO authentication.Other FortiOS versions including FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2.Local administrator authentication.Remote administrator authentication using RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+.While access to the FortiGate from FortiManagement Cloud (FortiGate Cloud) is technically not affected, SSO authentication to the FortiGate is still not possible over this management path.Issue matching:To confirm the issue, check the FortiOS crashlog for a matching "FORTISM Violation" from the time of the access attempt. This can be done by accessing the FortiGate using a local administrator account and executing diagnose debug crashlog read | grep YYYY-MM-DD .FGT-A(Primary) # diagnose debug crashlog read | grep 2026-10-20 6545: 2026-10-20 11:09:52 domain=WEB_AUTH domainid=37 acl=write msg="[FORTISM Violation: pid-236, 6546: 2026-10-20 11:09:52 api-open_w(), path-/tmp/ftnt1_sp_metadata.xml]." 6547: 2026-10-20 11:10:24 domain=WEB_AUTH domainid=37 acl=write msg="[FORTISM Violation: pid-236, 6548: 2026-10-20 11:10:24 api-open_w(), path-/tmp/ftnt1_sp_metadata.xml]."The issue is under investigation and scheduled for fix in FortiOS 7.6.9.Workaround:At this time, the only available workaround is to use another administrator authentication method.If no suitable administrator account exists, console access to a physical device can be used to recover access, see Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console.If the device is centrally managed by FortiManager or a valid FortiManagement Cloud subscription, an administrator can be added. See Recover access to FortiGate via FortiManagement Cloud.Related article:Technical Tip: Create a 'break glass' admin account on the FortiGate as a backup for remote authentication/MFA (Recommendation)

topics.title: Flow-mode inspection drops the 2nd TCP segment of a post-quantum (X25519MLKEM768) TLS ClientHello when the client does not use TCP timestamps (Windows default)
topics.summary: Product: FortiGate-80F-POE, S/N FG80FPTK24000713 Firmware: FortiOS v7.6.8 build3744 (GA.M); IPS Engine 7.01200; AV Engine 7.00062 Severity: 3 (business impact, workaround available)SummarySince Windows clients started sending hybrid post-quantum key shares (OpenSSL 3.5+, Chrome/Edge), TLS 1.3 handshakes from Windows hosts through our FortiGate time out. The ClientHello (~1.5–2 KB) is split into two TCP segments. For sessions without the TCP timestamp option (Windows default timestamps=allowed), the FortiGate ACKs the second segment to the client on behalf of the server. It then retransmits that segment on wan1 about 6 times, and the server never acknowledges it. The handshake hangs until the client times out (FIN from server after ~15 s, or RST after ~35 s).macOS clients (TCP timestamps on) are unaffected through the same policy, with the same NAT IP and destination, and even with a byte-identical ClientHello split at the same offsets.This looks related to KB “ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR when using flow-based deep inspection due to ML-KEM” (known issue), but our IPS engine (7.01200) is already newer than the fixed build (7.1026). Our profile is certificate-inspection, not deep inspection, and the failure depends on the TCP timestamp option.PolicyPolicy 19 sw-ap-corp_to_WAN: inspection-mode flow, ssl-ssh-profile certificate-inspection, av-profile default, ips-sensor default, auto-asic-offload enable, NAT to wan1 interface IP.ReproductionWindows 11 client (TCP timestamps not sent in SYN). Python 3.14 / OpenSSL 3.5: ssl.create_default_context().wrap_socket(socket.create_connection(('104.18.188.228',443)), server_hostname='api.pipedrive.com')The handshake times out. Destination: Cloudflare (Pipedrive) 104.18.188.228 / 104.18.189.228.EvidenceFortiGate sniffer (diagnose sniffer packet any ... 6), failing Windows session:The client sends seq X (1250 and seq X+1250 (707 B, PSH). Both are forwarded on wan1 with identical payload and a valid checksum.The server ACKs only X+1250.The FortiGate sends the client an ACK for X+1957, which the server never sent.The FortiGate retransmits the 707 B segment on wan1 at +0.25 s, +0.9 s, +2 s, +4 s, +7.7 s and +14.7 s. The server never ACKs it and FINs at ~15 s with ack=X+1250.Client-side pcap (pktmon): the client receives ACK for the full ClientHello 20 ms after sending it. The server’s FIN carries ack=1251 with SACK only for the client’s FIN. Pcap available.Same host, Windows netsh int tcp set global timestamps=enabled: OK (TLS 1.3 in 0.1–0.2 s), even though the ClientHello is still split (1238 + 286 . ECN on/off makes no difference.Same host, temporary policy without UTM (no ssl-ssh-profile / AV / IPS): OK, 2/2.Component isolation (temporary policies above policy 19, same host, 2 attempts each):certificate-inspection + IPS (no AV): FAILcertificate-inspection + AV (no IPS): FAILcertificate-inspection only (no IPS, no AV): FAIL (16 s, 300 B received; same pattern as above)IPS + AV with no-inspection SSL profile: OK (1 s, full handshake)The trigger is the certificate-inspection SSL/SSH profile in flow mode. IPS and AV are not involved.Classic X25519 only (ClientHello ~500 B, one segment): OK.ExpectedThe FortiGate should not ACK client data on the server’s behalf in flow mode, or, if it does, should deliver it reliably. The handshake should complete regardless of the client’s TCP timestamp option.

Working: User attempts to log in. Username is checked locally; if present, it is forwarded to the TACACS+ server. Password is verified successfully, forwarded, and processed to verify the Trusted host list. The required profiles and resources are allowed for the user. topics.title: Explanation for BGP debug output '107-Transport endpoint is not connected'
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to manage the condition where the BGP neighborship remains in the Active state, and the BGP debug shows the message '107-Transport endpoint is not connected'.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionAssuming a scenario where a FortiGate is receiving no traffic, the first check to perform is to verify the presence of the necessary routes in the VDOM routing table using the command:get router info routing-table allIf the required route is missing and should be announced by a BGP neighbor, you need to check the neighbor state with the command:get router info bgp neighbors When a BGP neighbor remains in the Active state, and it is not possible to perform checks directly on the neighbor's configuration and status, it is important to first understand what this state indicates. StateMeaningIdleThe local FortiGate has not started the BGP process with the neighbor. For eBGP, this can be because the peer is multiple hops away and multihop is not enabled.ConnectThe BGP process has started but has not initiated a TCP connection, possibly due to improper routing.ActiveA TCP connection was initiated, but there is no response, a delivery, or a remote-peer response problem.Assuming the neighborship remains in the Active state, this indicates that the TCP 3-way handshake has not been completed. If collecting the BGP debug logs, as explained here:Technical Tip: Capture BGP debugs for a specific neighbor, the output contains the message:107-Transport endpoint is not connectedThis confirms that the 3-way handshake was never completed.Another similar error message that might be possible to find in the debug logs:104-Connection reset by peerThis means the handshake was interrupted due to a remote reset.These errors can be caused by several factors, including:Incorrect routing: for the IP address used by the FortiGate to establish the BGP peering.Asymmetric routing: resulting in TCP packets on port 179 never being received.A firewall in the path: dropping TCP port 179 packets sent by the neighbor, or ISP filters.Misconfigured BGP peer IP: for example, a neighbor group configured on the remote side with an IP that falls outside the subnet used by the FortiGate.BGP password mismatch (if configured).QoS misconfigurations.Other routing problems affecting TCP port 179 packets, such as a Layer 3 routing loop.IPsec Phase 2 selector mismatch: In the case of BGP running over an IPsec VPN tunnel.Related article: Technical Tip: FortiOS BGP Resource List

topics.title: Resolved: EAPPasswordError with IKEv2, EAP-TTLS and FortiAuthenticator 2FA
topics.summary: I recently encountered and resolved the following issue, and I am sharing the troubleshooting process because the FortiClient error did not immediately indicate the actual cause.EnvironmentFortiClient EMS: 7.4.8 FortiClient for Windows: 7.4.8 FortiAuthenticator: 6.6.9 FortiGate VM: FortiOS 7.4.13 VPN type: IKEv2 IPsec Authentication method: EAP-TTLS User source: LDAP/Active Directory Two-factor authentication: FortiToken managed through FortiAuthenticatorIssueWhen I tried to establish the VPN connection using a domain account, FortiClient returned the following error:EAPPasswordErrorThe authentication process failed, and the VPN connection could not be established.Since I was taking over an existing installation, I was not yet fully familiar with every step of the authentication flow between FortiClient, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, and the LDAP server.Troubleshooting performedI initially verified the following points: The FortiGate was reachable from the client’s public IP address. A direct LDAP authentication test from the FortiGate was successful for both connectivity and credential validation. EAP-TTLS was selected in the VPN profile distributed through FortiClient EMS. EAP-TTLS was enabled in the FortiAuthenticator RADIUS policy, while EAP-MSCHAPv2 was disabled. The default realm configured in the RADIUS policy was associated with the correct LDAP identity source. During an authentication test from FortiAuthenticator, I received an error indicating that the user could not be found in the imported users database. I also found an Access-Reject event containing the message “User Locked”, but I could not confirm whether it was related to the same VPN authentication attempt. Since the direct LDAP test was successful, I initially suspected that the authentication request was not being processed correctly at some point in the chain between IKEv2, EAP-TTLS, RADIUS, FortiAuthenticator, and LDAP.SolutionI eventually found that the problem was related to the way the second authentication factor had to be entered.When EAP-TTLS/PAP is used with two-factor authentication through FortiAuthenticator, FortiClient does not display a separate prompt for the FortiToken code.The LDAP password and the current OTP must be entered consecutively in the same password field:LDAP password + OTPFor example:MyPassword123456After entering the LDAP password followed immediately by the current OTP, the authentication completed successfully and the IKEv2 IPsec VPN connection was established.The behavior and solution are documented in the following Fortinet Technical Tips:Technical Tip: Multi-Factor Authentication support for Windows FortiClient with LDAP (EAP-TTLS)https://community.fortinet.com/fortigate-3/technical-tip-multi-factor-authentication-support-for-windows-forticlient-with-ldap-eap-ttls-212498Technical Tip: How to resolve the “EAP authentication failed due to missing token” error when using EAP-TTLS/PAP + 2FA Authenticationhttps://community.fortinet.com/fortiauthenticator-8/technical-tip-how-to-resolve-the-eap-authentication-failed-due-to-missing-token-error-when-using-eap-ttls-pap-2fa-authentication-216311?tid=216311&fid=8In my case, the issue was not related to LDAP connectivity or realm selection. It was caused by the way the second authentication factor had to be provided when using EAP-TTLS with FortiAuthenticator.The EAPPasswordError message did not immediately indicate the actual cause, and the successful direct LDAP test initially led me to investigate other parts of the authentication flow.Has anyone else encountered the same behavior or received a different FortiClient error in a similar configuration?I hope this information can help anyone troubleshooting the same issue.

topics.title: IPS Engine Crash after upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.12
topics.summary: DescriptionThe ipsengine daemon crashes frequently on FortiGate devices running FortiOS 7.4.x / 7.6.x when FortiSandBox scanning is enabled in AntiVirus profiles.ScopeFortiGate 7.4.x, 7.6.xipsengine 07.004.604 FortiSandBox FortiSandBox-Cloud.SolutionSymptomAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.x or 7.6.x, the ipsengine daemon has been observed to crash repeatedly.The crash logs indicate a segmentation fault (Signal 11). This behavior results in Intrusion Prevention System scanning failures, which may cause certain traffic sessions or websites to be blocked.The following command below allows you to check the latest ipsengine crashes that occurred:Note:When an AntiVirus profile is configured to use FortiSandBox scanning (either Cloud or On-Premises), this will trigger a crash in the ipsengine.diagnose debug crashlog read | grep ipsengine -A 1 15512: 2026-09-08 07:26:43 application ipsengine 07.004.604 15513: 2026-09-08 07:26:43 *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received *** ... 15587: 2026-09-08 07:30:26 application ipsengine 07.004.604 15588: 2026-09-08 07:30:26 *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received ***WorkaroundDisable the FortiSandBox scanning feature within all AntiVirus profiles used in Firewall policies. This allows other security profiles, such as SSL Inspection, Web Filtering, and IPS, to continue functioning without crashing the engine.Log in to the FortiGate GUI.Select Security Fabric -> AntiVirus.Edit the AntiVirus profiles used in the firewall policies.Under the APT Protection Option, set Send files to FortiSandbox for inspection to disabled.Select OK to save the changes.Alternatively, use the Command Line Interface (CLI) to disable the feature:config antivirus profile edit " " config http set fortisandbox disable end config ftp set fortisandbox disable end config imap set fortisandbox disable end config pop3 set fortisandbox disable end config smtp set fortisandbox disable end next endThe permanent fix for this Known Issue is already included in FortiOS 7.4.13, 7.6.7, and 8.0.0.Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 7.4.13 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 7.6.7 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 8.0.0 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Related article: FortiGate / FortiOS - Administration Guide - Using FortiSandbox inline scanning with antivirus

topics.title: Invalid image when upgrading FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to troubleshoot when an upgrade to FortiManager fails with an 'Invalid Image' error.ScopeFortiManager.SolutionFortiManager firmware upgrade may fail with the error message 'Invalid Image'. The following is the checklist and steps to troubleshoot and identify the issue.Check the upgrade path and ensure that the image has no intermediate images. Upgrade path tool can be used to check: Upgrade Path Tool.Check the image downloaded. The image is specific to the model and VM instance. To check the VM instance, the following command can be run:diagnose debug klogSnippet of the output: [0.000000] Hypervisor detected: KVMBased on the output, the Hypervisor is KVM, and the image used should match the hypervisor (example):FMG_VM64_KVM-v7.6.8.M-build3788-FORTINET.outThe same command provided in the previous steps can also be used to identify if there are issues in the disks. The following is an example of the error: [702415.444478] EXT4-fs (dm-0): failed to convert unwritten extents to written extents -- potential data loss! (inode 7864504, error-30)The output indicates there are issues and errors within the disk that should be resolved first. Note that the output may vary depending on the exact issue. Previous command output can be used to compare working and non-working boot-ups to identify the error.System resources need to meet the minimum system requirements, as not meeting the requirements may block the upgrade. The following command can be used to check the system resources:get system performanceThe minimum system requirements are explained in the following document: Minimum system requirements.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient VPN before logon fails to connect when using windows credentials
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiClient version 7.4 fails to establish a VPN connection before user logon using Windows credentials.ScopeFortiClient version 7.4.SolutionSymptoms.Users cannot connect to the SSL VPN or IPsec VPN using the VPN Before Logon feature after upgrading to FortiClient version 7.4. The connection fails at the Windows logon screen, and no logs are generated on the FortiGate.Root cause.In FortiClient version7.4, a change in behavior causes the client to check for credentials before initiating the connection. If the Prompt for Username setting is disabled, FortiClient may fail to retrieve the necessary credentials from Windows, causing the pre-logon connection to halt. This differs from FortiClient version 7.2, which attempted to start the connection even if credentials were not immediately found.Resolution.Workaround:To resolve this issue in FortiClient version 7.4, enable the prompt for usernames in the endpoint profile:Log in to the FortiClient EMS console.Select Endpoint Profiles -> System Settings.Select the profile applied to the affected endpoints and select Edit.Navigate to the VPN tunnel settings.Enable the prompt for username option.Save the changes and deploy the profile to the endpoints.Settings in SSL VPN tunnel configuration:Settings in IPsec VPN tunnel configuration:Permanent solution.This behavior is not present in FortiClient version 8.0.0 and above. Upgrade the FortiClient installation to FortiClient version 8.0.0 or above to restore the VPN Before Logon behavior without requiring the username prompt.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Configuring Agentless FSSO polling via IPsec VPN tunnel
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to configure Agentless FSSO Polling via an IPsec VPN tunnel between two FortiGates.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionIn the network diagram above, the AD server is only reachable by FGT-A by IPsec VPN tunnel to FGT-B. By using FSSO Agent, specify the source IP to reach FGT-B. However, there is no such option in Agentless FSSO polling.LDAP is configured to specify the source IP, but performing a sniffer on FGT-A on port 445 reveals it was being sent out using another source IP:config user ldap edit "AD" set server "10.125.1.11" set source-ip 10.149.1.21 set cnid "sAMAccountName" set dn "dc=ces,dc=com" set type regular set username "cn=Administrator,cn=Users,dc=ces,dc=com" next end FGT-A # diagnose sniffer packet any 'port 445' 4 interfaces=nany] filters=oport 445] 0.624513 VPN-AtoB out 2.2.2.2.11209 -> 10.125.1.11.445: syn 2524384594 4.636167 VPN-AtoB out 2.2.2.2.11209 -> 10.125.1.11.445: syn 2524384594 25.233656 VPN-AtoB out 2.2.2.2.11211 -> 10.125.1.11.445: syn 2949233177 26.224879 VPN-AtoB out 2.2.2.2.11211 -> 10.125.1.11.445: syn 29492331772.2.2.2 is the public IP of FGT-A and it is not supposed to be traversing through the IPsec VPN tunnel VPN-AtoB; thus traffic will be dropped by the remote FortiGate.Resolution:By configuring IP address on the IPsec VPN tunnel, force the FSSO traffic to use the VPN tunnel IP address instead of the lowest-index IP address as the source IP.By default, FortiGate will use the lowest-index interface IP address as the source IP to initiate the traffic; the index list can be found in the command output below.diagnose ip address list IP=10.56.241.136->10.56.241.136/255.255.252.0 index=3 devname=port1 IP=10.56.1.136->10.56.1.136/255.255.252.0 index=4 devname=port2 IP=10.68.1.136->10.68.1.136/255.255.240.0 index=5 devname=port3 IP=10.69.1.136->10.69.1.136/255.255.240.0 index=6 devname=port4 IP=127.0.0.1->127.0.0.1/255.0.0.0 index=14 devname=root IP=10.255.1.1->10.255.1.1/255.255.255.0 index=18 devname=fortilink IP=127.0.0.1->127.0.0.1/255.0.0.0 index=23 devname=vsys_ha IP=127.0.0.1->127.0.0.1/255.0.0.0 index=25 devname=vsys_fgfmFGT-A # diagnose sniffer packet any 'port 445' 4 interfaces=nany] filters=oport 445] 7.309059 VPN-AtoB out 172.16.1.2.21873 -> 10.125.1.11.445: syn 751818537 7.310877 VPN-AtoB in 10.125.1.11.445 -> 172.16.1.2.21873: syn 1602721448 ack 751818538 7.310938 VPN-AtoB out 172.16.1.2.21873 -> 10.125.1.11.445: ack 1602721449 7.327293 VPN-AtoB out 172.16.1.2.21873 -> 10.125.1.11.445: psh 751818538 ack 1602721449 7.328787 VPN-AtoB in 10.125.1.11.445 -> 172.16.1.2.21873: psh 1602721449 ack 751818732 7.328816 VPN-AtoB out 172.16.1.2.21873 -> 10.125.1.11.445: ack 1602721658 7.329148 VPN-AtoB out 172.16.1.2.21873 -> 10.125.1.11.445: psh 751818732 ack 1602721658 7.330492 VPN-AtoB in 10.125.1.11.445 -> 172.16.1.2.21873: psh 1602721658 ack 751818902 7.330673 VPN-AtoB out 172.16.1.2.21873 -> 10.125.1.11.445: psh 751818902 ack 1602722080FGT-A is now using the VPN interface IP 172.16.1.2 to send the FSSO packet. On the remote FGT-B, the route 172.16.1.2 is now a directly connected route via IPsec VPN tunnel VPN-BtoA, therefore, it knows how to route the traffic back to FGT-A. FGTB # get router info routing-table all Routing table for VRF=0 Codes: K - kernel, C - connected, S - static, R - RIP, B - BGP O - OSPF, IA - OSPF inter area N1 - OSPF NSSA external type 1, N2 - OSPF NSSA external type 2 E1 - OSPF external type 1, E2 - OSPF external type 2 i - IS-IS, L1 - IS-IS level-1, L2 - IS-IS level-2, ia - IS-IS inter area * - candidate default S* 0.0.0.0/0 10/0] via 2.2.2.254, port1 C 10.47.0.0/22 is directly connected, port1 S 10.125.0.0/23 r10/0] via 172.16.1.1, VPN-BtoA C 10.149.0.0/23 is directly connected, port2 C 172.16.1.0/30 is directly connected, VPN-BtoA C 172.16.1.2/32 is directly connected, VPN-BtoAHence, the agentless FSSO polling is now working as expected:FGT-A # diagnose debug fsso-polling detail 1 AD Server Status(connected): ID=1, name(10.125.1.11),ip=10.125.1.11,source(security),users(0) port=auto username=Administrator read log eof=1, latest logon timestamp: Sun May 27 16:41:54 2018 polling frequency: every 10 second(s) success(508), fail(0) LDAP query: success(0), fail(0) LDAP max group query period(seconds): 0 LDAP status: connectedRelated articles:Technical Tip: Self-originating traffic over IPSec VPN (for example, ping)Technical Tip: tracert/traceroute behavior over IPsec VPN tunnel

topics.title: Why does FortiGate send self-signed Root CA Certificate in IKEv2 CERT payload?
topics.summary: Irrespective whether the FortiGate server certificate is directly issued by a Root CA or by an Intermediate CA, the Root CA is always sent to the IPsec VPN client in the CERT payload of the IKE_AUTH response. This doesn't make any sense since no peer is going to trust a self-signed certificate received via an untrusted channel. Omitting the unnecessary Root CA certificate would help to reduce the number of IKEv2 fragments needed to transmit the huge IKE_AUTH response.

topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAuthenticator ZTNA certificate error on FortiGate. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Zero trust tunnels FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 This article assumes that the initial setup for this feature has been completed: Setting up a zero trust tunnel If the ZTNA tunnel is failing on the FortiGate, check the ZTNA traffic logs on FortiGate: Log & Report -> ZTNA Traffic. After confirming the CA certificate, configure the following option through the FortiGate CLI: config authentication setting set user-cert-ca end Note: The authentication rule and scheme settings should also be configured as described in the documentation below: Configuring certificate authentication for FortiAuthenticator After confirming the CA certificate has been selected, re-attempt the ZTNA connection and check the ZTNA traffic logs again to verify it is successful: Related Articles: Configuring certificate authentication for FortiAuthenticator Setting up a zero trust tunnel What's new FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4

topics.title: Technical Tip: Enable Security Event logging on policy with Security Fabric enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to enable Security Event logging when Security Fabric is enabled.It applies to both Fabric root and subordinate FortiGates.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionBy design and by default, all firewall policies (except for the implicit deny policy) log all sessions after Security Fabric has been enabled.Users cannot directly change the logging configuration on downstream (i.e. non-root) FortiGates as the option is greyed out as shown below: When the info indication highlighted above is hovered over, it shows: 'Security fabric is enabled so logging will exempt traffic from downstream FortiGates'.Although it is possible to change the logtraffic option manually in FortiGate CLI, this change will not be reflected in the GUI, and the session will continue to log all traffic.For example, the following configuration change would cause only security events to be logged if the FortiGate was not part of a security fabric, but is ignored for fabric FortiGates:config firewall policy edit set logtraffic utm next endThis behavior is by design to avoid unnecessary changes to firewall policy configuration when enabling or disabling Security Fabric.In FortiOS version 8.0.1 and above, the following warning shows when changing the 'logtraffic' setting:FortiGate-60F(Primary) # config firewall policy FortiGate-60F(Primary) (policy) # edit 10 FortiGate-60F(Primary) (10) # set logtraffic disable WARNING: Security Fabric is enabled. Traffic from downstream devices will still be logged.Customizing Downstream FortiGate logging behavior.This is done on the downstream FortiGate using the Security Fabric 'configuration-sync' setting. Set configuration-sync to 'local' instead of 'default' in the downstream FortiGate CLI Security Fabric settings as shown below:config system csf set configuration-sync local endAfter making the change, the logging level can be changed on the firewall policy in CLI or GUI:Note: In some cases, even after applying 'set configuration-sync local' in CLI, the logging option will still be greyed out and will not permit change; this is generally a browser issue. To resolve it, either refresh the GUI browser page or log out of the admin account and log back in again. The GUI should now allow to update the Logging Options.Note: There are 2 options that configuration-sync can be set to, which are:Default: Synchronize configuration for FortiAnalyzer, FortiSandbox, and Central Management to the root node.Local: Do not synchronize configuration with the root node. As mentioned, setting it to local will prevent the device from synchronizing the configuration with the root node.Note: The 'set configuration-sync local' command is effective only on a downstream FortiGate; in a root FortiGate, it is not used, and therefore the command has been removed for FortiGates serving as a fabric root in FortiOS 7.6.1 and onwards.Customizing fabric root FortiGate logging behavior.This is done using the 'log-unification' setting on the root FortiGate.The fabric root FortiGate will log all sessions matching all configured firewall policies by default, even if the 'logtraffic' setting is changed.For example, the following firewall policy will still generate traffic logs:config firewall policy edit 10 set name "Explicit LAN block outbound" set srcintf "lan" set dstintf "any" set srcaddr "lan_net" set dstaddr "grp_LAN_explicit_block" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" set logtraffic disable next endMatching traffic log:eventtime=2110839462597492736 tz="+0600" logid="0000000013" type="traffic" subtype="forward" level="notice" vd="root" srcip=172.16.10.10 srcport=53467 srcintf="lan" srcintfrole="undefined" dstip=198.51.100.10 dstport=443 dstintf="wan" dstintfrole="undefined" srccountry="United States" dstcountry="United States" sessionid=12345678 proto=6 action="deny" policyid=10 policytype="policy" poluuid="6af9be38-cdf4-51ef-f217-317f2d7e77a3" policyname="Explicit LAN block outbound" service="HTTPS" trandisp="noop" appcat="unscanned" duration=0 sentbyte=0 rcvdbyte=0 sentpkt=0 rcvdpkt=0 crscore=30 craction=131072 crlevel="high"If needed, log-unification can be disabled for the fabric in the root FortiGate's configuration as follows:config system csf set status enable set log-unification disable endThis disables multiple security fabric features, including the 'log all sessions' behavior and fabric device MAC discovery broadcasts.An alternative option is to configure an explicit granular logging filter matching a specific policyid and traffic subtype; see Technical Tip: Configuring advanced syslog free-style filters.Related documents:Optimizations for physical FortiGate devices with 2 GB RAMTechnical Tip: The impact of 'set configuration-sync local' on the Security Fabric

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tips: Admin is logged out of the GUI immediately after login (login must be entered twice) on FortiGate version 7.6.7
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue on FortiOS version 7.6.7: some administrators are kicked back to the login page right after a successful GUI login; it is necessary to enter credentials a second time before the dashboard loads. In other cases, the first attempt shows a blank/white page, and a later attempt loads normally. The login may be recorded in the event log together with an HTTPS connection error, even though authentication itself succeeds.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.7.SolutionSymptoms:After entering the username and password, the login page reappears instead of the dashboard. Entering the credentials a second time succeeds and the GUI loads.The issue affects GUI (HTTPS) logins only, SSH sessions are not affected. It may be seen across Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, and sometimes in /private mode as well.An 'HTTPS connection error' may be logged in the event log.Root cause:When signing in through a web browser, the page loads a large number of small resources all at once (far more than in earlier releases). The web interface's activity monitor mistakes this normal burst of activity for a brief attack and interrupts the login, dropping back to the login page, even though the username and password were already accepted.This is why the login can appear in the event log as successful while the page still sends back: authentication succeeds, but the session is cut before the dashboard finishes loading.Related known issues in the 7.6.7 release notes:Bug ID 1300025 – Admin session termination (especially Chrome/Edge). Workaround: clear browser cache/cookies.Bug ID 1306049 – Blank page after upgrade to 7.6.7. Workaround involves disabling HTTP rate-limiter settings.Resolution:Fixed in FortiOS version 7.6.8 (and above version 8.0.1). The fix scopes the unauthenticated request-body monitor to body-carrying methods only, raises the unauthenticated request timeout from 1 s to 10 s, and reworks the rate-limiter token pricing and refund logic so a normal GUI bootstrap is not mistaken for an attack and killed.Upgrade to FortiOS version 7.6.8 or above to resolve the issue.Workaround (until upgrade):Until the upgrade can be performed, one of the following avoids the problem:Clear the browser cache and cookies associated with the FortiGate, then log in again.Access the GUI in the browser's Incognito/InPrivate mode.Simply log in a second time; the second attempt loads the dashboard normally.Diagnostic Commands:Useful while reproducing the issue:diagnose debug resetdiagnose debug console timestamp enablediagnose debug application httpsd -1diagnose debug application node -1diagnose debug application http_authd -1 # or http_authdiagnose debug enableStop with:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset

topics.title: BGP VPNv4 routes received but not installed in the VRF routing table
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen a BGP VPNv4 route(s) are received, the route(s) fail to be installed in the VRF routing-table when an extended community value is missing.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionIn an MPLS L3VPN environment integrating FortiGate firewalls, MP-BGP VPNv4 routes and VRF route-tagging mechanisms help maintain routing separation between customer networks while controlling route exchange across the provider backbone. By combining FortiGate routing policies and VRF-based segmentation with appropriate BGP route-target import/export policies and route-tag controls, service providers can reduce unintended route propagation and strengthen customer traffic isolation.This article focuses on the route installation issue. The configuration part is assumed to be working, and BGP neighborship between FW-01 and FW-02 is established.In this scenario, FW-01 receives the route 10.115.1.0/24 from Customer-A on VRF 115. FW-01 advertises this route to FW-02. The same route must be installed to FW-02 VRF 115 routing table.10.100.223.9 - FW-01 BGP router ID10.100.223.10 - FW-02 BGP router ID10.100.228.5 & 10.100.228.6 - Customer A BGP router IDFW-01 is advertising the route to neighbor 10.100.223.9 (FW-02).FW-01 # get router info bgp neighbors 10.100.223.10 advertised-routes vpnv4 | grep 10.115.1.0 *> 10.115.1.0/24 10.100.223.9 0 0 64902 64902 64902 64902 64901 64900 ? On FW-02, the route is received from FW-01. However, the route is not installed in the routing-table.FW-02 # get router info bgp neighbors 10.100.223.9 received-routes vpnv4 | grep 10.115.1.0 *> 10.115.1.0/24 10.100.223.9 0 0 64902 64902 64902 64902 64902 64901 64900 ? The required Extended Community (RT) Route Target for VRF 115 is 64600:115.First, look at the BGP route information for 10.115.1.0/24 on FW-01 VRF 115. This route is received from Customer-A via two BGP neighborship, 10.100.228.5 and 10.100.228.6. Notice that Extended Community field is empty.FW-01 # get router info bgp network 10.115.2.0/24 VRF 115 BGP routing table entry for 10.115.2.0/24 Paths: (2 available, best #2, table Default-IP-Routing-Table) Advertised to non peer-group peers: 10.100.228.5 10.100.228.6 Original VRF 115 local 64901 64900 10.100.228.6 from 10.100.228.6 (10.100.228.6) Origin incomplete distance 20 metric 0, localpref 100, valid, external, best Extended Community: Advertised Path ID: 2 Last update: Mon Aug 10 23:37:14 2026 Original VRF 115 local 64901 64900 10.100.228.5 from 10.100.228.5 (10.100.228.5) Origin incomplete distance 20 metric 0, localpref 100, valid, external, best Extended Community: Advertised Path ID: 1 Last update: Mon Aug 10 23:37:14 2026When FW-01 advertises this route to FW-02, the extended community value is empty.Take a look at a working subnet 10.107.1.0/24, which is advertised with the extended community value 64600:115. This attribute is requirement for VRF 115 route installation. As a result, this route is successfully installed in the FW-02 VRF 115 route table.Despite adding a route-map out to include the extended community route target, FW-01 still advertises 10.115.1.0/24 without any route target attribute. For more information about extended community route targets, refer to Matching BGP extended community route targets in route maps.ResolutionTo mitigate this, the required route target attribute must be added before the route is installed on FW-01 VRF 115 route table. To achieve this, a route-map-in must be configured under the BGP neighbor configuration between FW-01 and Customer-A.Configure the route-map rule.FW-01# config router route-map edit "VRF115-RT-Inbound" config rule edit 1 set set-extcommunity-rt 64600:115 next end next endThen apply the route-map inbound under BGP neighbor configuration on FW-01.FW-01# config router bgp config neighbor edit "10.100.228.5" set route-map-in ""VRF115-RT-Inbound" next end endOnce this is applied, the route installed on FW-01 VRF 115 will now show the required extended community route target attribute of 64600:115.FW-01 # get router info bgp network 10.115.2.0/24 VRF 115 BGP routing table entry for 10.115.2.0/24 Paths: (2 available, best #2, table Default-IP-Routing-Table) Advertised to non peer-group peers: 10.100.228.5 10.100.228.6 Original VRF 115 local 64901 64900 10.100.228.6 from 10.100.228.6 (10.100.228.6) Origin incomplete distance 20 metric 0, localpref 100, valid, external, best Extended Community: RT:64600:115 Advertised Path ID: 2 Last update: Thu Oct 15 22:46:36 2026 Original VRF 115 local 64901 64900 10.100.228.5 from 10.100.228.5 (10.100.228.5) Origin incomplete distance 20 metric 0, localpref 100, valid, external, best Extended Community: RT:64600:115 Advertised Path ID: 1 Last update: Thu Oct 15 22:46:42 2026On FW-02, the route is now installed in VRF 115 with the required extended community route tag attribute.FW-02 # get router info bgp network 10.115.2.0/24 VRF 115 BGP routing table entry for 10.115.2.0/24 Paths: (1 available, best #1, table Default-IP-Routing-Table) Advertised to non peer-gr

topics.title: Dial-up IPsec VPN clients assigned duplicate IP addresses
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to prevent remote users connecting via dial-up IPsec VPN from being assigned IP addresses already in use by other active sessions, leading to connectivity drops and authentication failures.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient/EMS.SolutionSymptomsUsers connecting to a dial-up IPsec VPN configured with "net-device disable" experience connection drops immediately after completing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Logs indicate that the IP address assigned to a new user is already linked to another active VPN session.The issue occurs when the system reassigns IP addresses too quickly after a session ends or when the tunnel configuration does not properly manage the IP pool reuse interval. This can lead to IP address conflicts where multiple users are assigned the same address from the configured range.ResolutionTo resolve IP address duplication and improve connection stability, perform the following steps:Configure IP address reuse delay:Increase the time the FortiGate waits before reusing an IP address from the pool. This prevents a new user from receiving an IP that is still associated with a recently disconnected session.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set ip-delay-interval 240 next endOptimize tunnel configuration:Follow these best practices to ensure tunnel stability and performance:Upon experiencing this issue, limit the number of characters in the IPsec VPN phase 1 name to avoid potential processing issues (must be below 13 characters), even when net device is disabled. See Technical Tip: IPsec VPN phase1 interface name characters limitation best practice.Disable reauthentication on the tunnel to prevent unexpected drops during active sessions.Enable the net-device setting if the environment requires specific network device handling for the tunnel.To enable the net-device setting, run the following commands:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set net-device enable next endVerify and troubleshoot:If the issue persists, use the following commands to monitor IP assignments and tunnel status:diagnose vpn ike gateway list diagnose vpn tunnel list diagnose vpn ipsec status get vpn ike gateway get vpn ipsec tunnel details get vpn ipsec state tunnelTo capture detailed debug logs for the IKE process and authentication, use these commands:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug disable diagnose vpn ike log filter name diagnose vpn ike log filter rem-addr4 diagnose debug application ike -1 diagnose debug application eap_proxy -1 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug enable diagnose debug application fnbamd -1After, open a TAC support case with this evidence: Customer Service Tip: How to create a ticket for Fortinet TAC.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving stale FSSO TS-gent sessions retained by Collector Agent
topics.summary: DescriptionIn environments utilizing Fortinet Single Sign-On (FSSO) Terminal Server Agent (TS Agent), if a host running the TS Agent service is decommissioned, shut down, or has the TS Agent software uninstalled, its assigned port-range logon sessions (type fsso_citrix) may persist indefinitely on the Collector Agent and continue to be advertised to FortiGate firewalls.Symptoms:Stale TS-Agent sessions persist indefinitely in the Collector Agent (show logon users) after the TS Agent service is stopped or uninstalled.Stale TS-Agent sessions coexist with fresh standard logons (such as EventLog polling or DC Agent) for the same IP address.User traffic using outbound source ports outside the assigned range fails identity-based firewall policies.Cause:Aging timer exclusions: Standard Collector Agent aging timers (Dead Entry Timeout, Workstation Verification, and DNS verification) are architected for single-user endpoints and deliberately exempt multi-user TS-Agent sessions.Silent service shutdown: When the TS Agent service stops or is uninstalled, it terminates without transmitting a logoff or disconnect notification to the Collector Agent.Session coexistence: TS-Agent sessions are indexed by server session ID rather than workstation name, allowing them to coexist alongside standard logons (EventLog or DC Agent) on the same IP address.Keepalive validation disabled by default: The Collector Agent background keepalive health check (tsagent_alive_check) is disabled by default (0).Security consideration: DHCP IP reuse:If a machine with an active TS Agent session releases its IP address back to a DHCP pool without a clean logoff, and a new client device subsequently leases that same IP address, any outbound traffic generated by the new device using source ports within the stale port range will inherit the previous user's FSSO identity and group permissions on the FortiGate. Enabling keepalive checking mitigates this identity-spoofing exposure.ScopeFSSO Collector Agent: All supported versions.FSSO Terminal Server Agent (TS Agent): All supported versions.Operating System: Microsoft Windows Server.SolutionTo enable automatic detection and cleanup of abandoned TS-Agent sessions, configure the tsagent_alive_check registry values on all Collector Agents.Step 1: Open Registry Editor.Launch regedit.exe on each Collector Agent server with administrative privileges.Step 2: Navigate to the correct registry key.The Collector Agent service queries the registry using the KEY_WOW64_32KEY flag. On 64-bit Windows installations, the values must reside under the 32-bit registry hive (WOW6432Node).64-bit Windows: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Fortinet\FSAE\CollectorAgent32-bit Windows:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Fortinet\FSAE\CollectorAgentStep 3: Create or update DWORD values.Create or modify the following DWORD (32-bit) Value entries:NameTypeRecommended ValueDescriptiontsagent_alive_checkREG_DWORD1Enables Timer 6 to monitor TS Agent keepalives. (Default is 0 - Disabled).tsagent_alive_check_periodREG_DWORD7200 (Decimal)Timeout period in seconds. Once a TS Agent host stops sending keepalives for longer than this period, all sessions for that host IP are purged.Recommended timeout guidelines:Production Environments with regular maintenance: 7200 seconds (2 hours) is recommended to prevent premature session purges during routine Windows patching or server reboots.Fast cleanup / Lab environments: 300 seconds (5 minutes) can be used for rapid session cleanup.Step 4: Restart the service.A service restart is mandatory because the timer 6 evaluation thread is only initialized during service startup:Open Windows Services (services.msc).Restart the Fortinet Single Sign On Agent service (Fortinet_FSAE):Verification.In the Collector Agent GUI, navigate to the log level settings and set the log level to debug.Open CollectorAgent.log located under C:\Program Files (x86)\Fortinet\FSAE\.Verify that Timer 6 starts:Periodic keepalive checks log as TSAgentAliveCheck.When an abandoned host exceeds the timeout period, the log records:[UPDATE_LOGON_LIST] action:remove_entry ...In the Collector Agent GUI under Show Logon Users, confirm that the stale TS-Agent entry has been removed and only the active user session remains.

topics.title: Isolation network failure in FortiNAC v7.6.7 operating in Layer 2 mode
topics.summary: DescriptionUpgrading FortiNAC from version 7.6.6 to 7.6.7 may cause Layer 2 isolation and remediation interfaces to lose their IP addresses, resulting in DHCP and captive portal failures.ScopeFortiNAC-F v7.6.7.SolutionSymptoms.After upgrading FortiNAC from version 7.6.6 to 7.6.7, the following issues occur in Layer 2 isolation mode:The Configuration Wizard Summary displays the message "No isolation networks configured" even when isolation is correctly configured.Isolation and remediation interfaces lose their assigned IP addresses.DHCP services and the captive portal on these networks stop responding.The DHCP service may become inactive.Verify the DHCP service status using the following command:execute service status kea-dhcp6The output shows the service as Active: inactive (dead).Applying the config wizard displays the following result:Results 2026/10/13 15:04:56 Successful Configuration, scroll down for details. You will need to reboot your FortiNAC-CA. Results are written to the following file: /bsc/campusMgr/config/results.html File /bsc/campusMgr/bin/.cm_config written successfully Configuring DHCP Server... No isolation networks configured <====== (EVEN THOUGH ISOLATION IS CONFIGURED AND NO CHANGES HAVE BEEN MADE) DHCP Server configuration updated successfully Successful write to file /etc/hosts using /bsc/campusMgr/config/templates/hosts_Server.template Root cause.A problem in the configuration script in FortiNAC version 7.6.7 causes Layer 2 isolation and remediation VLAN interfaces to be omitted. As a result, these networks are silently discarded.Resolution.This issue is resolved in the upcoming FortiNAC version 7.6.8. To resolve the problem, perform the following steps:Take a virtual machine snapshot and perform a full system and database backup of the current environment.Upgrade FortiNAC to version 7.6.8 during a scheduled maintenance window.Verify that the isolation and remediation interfaces have the correct IP addresses assigned.Run the Configuration Wizard to ensure the summary no longer displays 'No isolation networks configured'.

topics.title: How to configure EMS connector for a specific VDOM using FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiManager allows administrators to configure an EMS connector at the ADOM level. By default, the configured EMS connector is pushed to all FortiGate devices within the ADOM. For FortiGate devices operating in multi-VDOM mode, this configuration is applied at the Global level.However, in a multi-VDOM environment, individual VDOMs can override the Global EMS configuration to connect to their own EMS servers. VDOMs that do not enable the override continue to inherit the Global EMS configuration.ScopeFortiManager 7.4, 7.6, 8.0.SolutionBackgroundThe EMS connector can be configured in FortiManager under Fabric View -> Fabric connector -> Enable EMS.When configured at the ADOM database level, the EMS connector is intended to be distributed to the FortiGate devices managed by that ADOM. In multi-VDOM mode, the configuration is applied at the Global level.FortiGate also supports configuring an EMS connector override at the VDOM level. When the override is enabled, the VDOM can use its own EMS configuration instead of inheriting the Global configuration.The VDOM-level EMS configuration is stored in the FMG Device Database. Therefore, configuring an EMS connector in the ADOM database does not override an existing VDOM-level EMS configuration.Configuring the EMS connector in the FortiManager ADOM database remains necessary when FortiManager needs to import tags from the EMS server.SetupFollow the steps below to configure an EMS connector override for a specific VDOM on a FortiGate operating in multi-VDOM mode.Step 1: Enable endpoint-control settings for the VDOMNavigate to Device Manager -> Device & Groups.Select the required FortiGate VDOM.Navigate to CLI Configuration -> endpoint-control settings -> Enable it.Step 2: Install the VDOM device settings.Step 3: Retrieve the configuration: Technical Tip: Retrieve configuration file using GUI or CLI from a FortiManager.Step 4: Configure the VDOM-level EMS connector.Navigate to Device Manager -> Device & Groups.Select the required FortiGate VDOM.Navigate to CLI Configuration -> fctems-override -> Configure the EMS connector required per-VDOM and enable it.Install the configuration to the FortiGate.SummaryAfter the configuration is installed successfully:The specified VDOM uses its own EMS configuration.VDOMs without the override enabled continue to inherit the Global EMS configuration.The EMS connector configured in the ADOM database remains available for FortiManager's EMS tag-import functionality.

topics.title: FortiGate IPoE Setup Guide NTT Docomo Business Corporation FixedIP
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article is written based on the FortiGate-60F. The WAN configuration with multiple VNE interfaces requires FortiOS 7.6.1 or later. If required to use multiple VNE interface features, make sure to upgrade FortiGate in advance. For information on the firmware upgrade path and how to upgrade, please refer to the release notes or manuals.ScopeFortiGate 7.6.1 and later.SolutionWAN 1 Interface IPv6config system interface edit "wan1" set vdom "root" set mode dhcp set allowaccess ping set type physical set role wan set snmp-index 1 config ipv6 set dhcp6-information-request enable set autoconf enable set unique-autoconf-addr enable end next end VNE configurationconfig system vne-interface edit "vne.wan1" set interface "wan1" next end IPv4 Default Routeconfig router static edit 1 set device "vne.wan1" next end IPv4 firewall policyconfig firewall policy edit 1 set name "internal-vne.wan1" set srcintf "internal" set dstintf "vne.wan1" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" set logtraffic all set nat enable set tcp-mss-sender 1420 set tcp-mss-receiver 1420 next end DHCPv4 server settingsconfig system dhcp server edit 1 set dns-service default set default-gateway 192.168.101.254 set netmask 255.255.255.0 set interface "internal" config ip-range edit 1 set start-ip 192.168.101.101 set end-ip 192.168.101.200 next end next endChecking the IPv6 addressWAN1 and the IPv6 address for the IPv4 over IPv6 tunnel generated by the obtained MAP rules are both configured. These IPv6 addresses are automatically generated based on the settings so far. If these IPv6 addresses are not set, it could be a misconfiguration or an environmental factor. In that case, verify the settings and investigate the environment.FortiGate-60F # diagnose ipv6 address list dev=5 devname=wan1 flag=P scope=0 prefix=128 addr=XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX: :0 preferred=4294967295 valid=4294967295 cstamp=72883 tstamp=72883 dev=5 devname=wan1 flag= scope=0 prefix=64 addr=XXXX:XXXX:XXXXX:XXXX: preferred=14281 valid=2591881 cstamp=71960 tstamp=672570 (omitted)Checking the IPv4 over IPv6 tunnelMake sure that the IPv4 over IPv6 tunnel with the IPv6 tunnel endpoint is properly established. The IPv6 addresses for the IPv4 over IPv6 tunnel created by the MAP rule are shown in the blue box, and the IPv6 address of the IPv6 tunnel endpoint is shown in the orange box.FortiGate-60F # diagnose ipv6 ipv6-tunnel list devname=vne.wan1 devindex=5 ifindex=27 vfid=0000 rpdb=0 ref=0 laddr=XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX: raddr=XXXX:XXXX:XXXX::X 192.0.2.1/255.255.255.255 index=27 devname=vne.wan1Once the above items are verified, make sure that user can access the internet via IPv4 from the LAN-side device.Related Articles:config system vne-tunnel (FortiOS 7.4.X and earlier) NP6 session fast path requirements

topics.title: HA cluster firmware upgrade stuck after the Secondary unit is upgraded successfully
topics.summary: DescriptionA firmware upgrade behavior issue observed in a High Availability (HA) cluster. In an HA cluster, when the FGCP Multi-Version Cluster (MVC) upgrade mode is enabled using set uninterruptible-upgrade enable, the upgrade behavior will upgrade the Secondary unit first followed by the Primary unit.However, there are cases where the firmware upgrade may not proceed to the Primary unit even after the Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded.For example:The Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded to firmware version 7.6.7.However, the Primary unit remains on firmware version 7.4.11.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionRecommended action:Do not reboot the Primary unit or initiate a failover.Re-run the firmware upgrade from the Primary unit to trigger the upgrade process again.This approach will usually resolve the issue and allow the firmware upgrade to proceed as expected.

topics.title: No allowed logs in FortiAnalyzer
topics.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps to take when there are no allowed web-filter logs in the FortiAnalyzer.ScopeFortiAnalyzer, FortiGate.SolutionWhen checking the FortiAnalyzer Analytics logs, it is possible to see there are no Allow web-filter logs:First thing needs to do is to verify if there are any Allowed traffic log in the Archived logs. Navigate to FortiView -> Log Browse -> Traffic logs of the selected device.If there are no allowed logs, it means the FortiGate itself does not generate the logs. Note that FortiAnalyzer can only process what is being received from the logging devices and does not generate the logs.To address this, FortiGate needs to generate the logs. The following article can be referred to on how to configure for all logs for traffic:Technical Tip: How to see all visited website URLs under web filter security logIf there are necessary archive logs, but no analytics logs, capture the following debug output:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug app fazsvcd 255 diagnose debug enableAfter debugging is enabled, start querying analytics logs to generate output.If the CLI shows there are Allowed traffic logs, it means the issue is on the GUI rather than the database. Further debug and troubleshooting steps can refer to the following documents:Technical Tip: How to debug GUI issues in FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer.If the output from the previous steps shows no Allowed logs, the issue may be on the database itself. At this stage, a database rebuild can be considered:execute sql-local rebuild-dbIf the issue still observes after all 3 steps have been verified. There could be a hardware/hypervisor issue or underlying issue within the system.Reach out to the Technical Support team to assist and verify if there are issues within the system/hardware. topics.title: One-arm sniffer option visible on interface with WAN role
topics.summary: DescriptionThe one-arm sniffer addressing mode remains visible in the GUI when an interface role is set to WAN.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionThe one-arm sniffer addressing mode should not be visible in the GUI when the interface role is set to WAN as mentioned in the document: One-arm sniffer.This only means that the one-arm sniffer mode is hidden on the GUI level: not on the functionality level. When the one-arm sniffer mode is selected before the role of an interface is set to "WAN", or when the one-arm sniffer is enabled via CLI, the option will remain visible in the interface GUI. The firmware does not restrict the users to set the addressing mode to one-arm sniffer in the interfaces with a role WAN. It only attempts to hide the option from the GUI.Two methods to enable the one-arm sniffer on a WAN interface:Using the Command Line Interface (CLI) below on an interface with the "WAN" role:config system interface edit set ips-sniffer-mode enable next end2. Using the Graphical User Interface (GUI):Select Network -> Interfaces -> Edit an interface(port1 for this example image).Select the interface and change the role from "WAN" to "LAN" or "Undefined". (Example image is port1.)Select "One-Arm Sniffer" as the addressing mode.Select OK to save the changes.Edit the Same InterfaceChange the interface role back to "WAN". On this part, the one-arm sniffer mode will not disappear in the GUI.Select OK to save the changes.To hide the One-arm sniffer option from the GUI while the role is set to "WAN":Edit the interface with "WAN" role.Change the Addressing mode to a different option like" Manual" or "DHCP".Select OK to save the changes.

topics.title: FortiClient Web Filter browser extension fails to uninstall during an on-fabric to off-fabric transition
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen the Web Filter extension is not uninstalled when the endpoint moves from on-fabric to off-fabric while 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled and 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering' is enabled.ScopeFortiClient Endpoint version 8.0.0, FortiClient Windows.SolutionIssue scenario: FortiClient v8.0.0.0103 GA.Enable the Web Filter profile.Disable 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric'.Enable 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering'.Verify the extension is installed while on-fabric.Move the endpoint to off-fabric and observe that the extension is not uninstalled. Issue resolved In: FortiClient version 8.0.1. Solution description:Fixed a bug where the policy watchdog unconditionally re-added the browser extension force-install policy. The fix ensures that when 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled, the policy is removed during the transition to an inactive filtering state (including on-fabric to off-fabric). Both the periodic policy-check and extended-keepalive-absence paths now respect the policy gate to prevent the extension from being resurrected. Additionally, SafeSearch hosts-file enforcement was updated to align with actual extension presence.

topics.title: FortiGate Single Sign-On users logged off when Enforce Kerberos is enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionUsers are automatically logged off from FortiGate Single Sign-On after enabling the Enforce Kerberos setting in the Collector Agent.ScopeFortiGate, FSSO Collector AgentSolutionA known issue exists where the workstation check fails when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled. Users are de-authenticated when the workstation check fails after the dead entry timeout.Upgrade the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent to version 5.0.0335 or later. This version addresses WMI workstation check failures when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled by adding reverse DNS lookup to resolve workstation IP addresses to hostnames.Download the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent version 5.0.0335 from the Fortinet Support Portal.Install the updated Collector Agent on the server.Enable the "Enforce Kerberos" setting in the Collector Agent configuration.Monitor the user sessions to verify that they are no longer automatically logged off after one hour.Related article:Technical Tip: FortiGate FSSO Collector Agent v5.0.0323 and earlier do not support Windows Server 2025 with default polling mode

topics.title: rxqid default value was changed after upgrade
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter an upgrade from versions 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4 to versions 7.0.15, 7.2.9, and 7.4.5, the rxqid value was changed and may cause RX drops on the interface.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionSymptomsUnder system 'affinity-packet-redistribution ' is the rxqid setting. It is the ID of the receive queue on an interface used to perform packet redistribution across multiple CPU cores. The value is from to .In 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4, the default value is 0. After upgrading FortiOS to 7.0.15, 7.2.9, 7.4.5, and above, the default value is changed to 255. topics.title: Technical Tip: Recovering a policy block rule that was changed directly on the FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains how to restore a policy block rule that was edited, disabled or deleted directly on a FortiGate. It also explains the two warnings that the Import Configuration wizard shows for a policy package that uses a policy block, and what not to do.ScopeIt applies to firewall rules that FortiManager installs from a policy block and that were then changed directly on the FortiGate. It does not cover changes made to the block in FortiManager itself.SolutionWhich way to go: if the change made on the FortiGate is unwanted, install the policy package to that device (section 3). If the change is wanted, make it in the policy block in FortiManager (section 4). Do not use Import Configuration for either case (section 5).How a policy block rule appears on the FortiGate.A policy package stores only a reference to the policy block. At install, FortiManager expands the block into normal firewall policies. The FortiGate has no policy block concept and shows the rules as ordinary policies.The expanded rules have large, block-derived policy IDs.These IDs come from a range that FortiManager reserves. A FortiGate accepts policy IDs from 0 to 4294967294, but FortiManager supports policy IDs only up to 1071741824 for policies it imports or creates, and it reserves IDs from 1071741825 upward for internal use. The range 1071741825-1072741824 is reserved for policy blocks. See Appendix B - Policy ID support in the Administration Guide.What FortiManager shows after a change on the FortiGate.When a block rule is edited, disabled or deleted directly on the FortiGate, FortiManager pulls the change into the Device DB of that device (auto-update). The same pattern appeared in the lab for all three changes:In Device Manager, Config Status of the device and of the VDOM shows Auto-update, and the policy package of that VDOM shows the red Out-of-Sync icon. Other VDOMs and other devices stay green.The device Revision History gets a new revision named AutoUpdate with the comment 'Auto update from device'.The policy block and the policy package are unchanged and still list the block. Other devices that use the block are not affected.Restore the original rule.The policy package defines the block rules, so installing the package to the affected device restores them. A Device Revert is not needed.In Device Manager, open Install Preview for the device. To see which rule differs, right-click the VDOM and choose Policy Package Diff.Install the policy package to that device only. Use Install Wizard (Install Policy Package & Device Settings), or right-click the VDOM and choose Re-install Policy. Re-install Policy opens a two-step wizard with the device and the package already selected and an Install Preview button on page 1. In that wizard, Next starts the install, so review the preview first.Open the install log. It lists only the commands from the preview.On the FortiGate, run show firewall policy with the rule ID to confirm the rule. In Device Manager, Config Status returns to Synchronized and the package to Installed.Before installing: The install sends every difference between the package and the device, not only the rule changed. If the preview shows anything else, find out why before continuing.Other devices that use the block are not touched by this install.Keeping the change instead.If the change made on the FortiGate must stay, make it in the policy block in FortiManager. Do not import it.Open the policy block and use Where Used to list every policy package that references it.Edit the rule in the block. If you edit it from inside a device package, FortiManager shows Confirm Policy Block Edit and changes the shared block, not only that package.Run Install Preview for each device and install the devices that should receive the change.A change in the policy block reaches every package that references it. Until a device is installed, it keeps the old value, so check each device.The two Import warnings, and what not to do.Import Configuration reads the configuration of the device into FortiManager. It is not the way to accept or undo a change to a block rule, because the wizard does not bring the block rules back as a policy block. On page 2 (Interface Mapping & Policy) it shows one of two red warnings, depending on the package name:Package name in the wizardWarning shown in the labWhat it meansAn existing package nameThe policy package will be overwritten and 1 policy block will be removed from the existing policy package.Continuing would replace the package and remove the policy block from it.A new package namePolicy Block policies installed from FortiManager will not be imported. Please add back Policy Block after import.The new package would not contain the block rules. The block would have to be added back by hand.Both warnings appeared for a device that was in sync and for a device that was never edited on the FortiGate, so they do not mean that the block link is already broken. In both cases, select Cancel and use

topics.title: How to interpret FIB and policy-route version changes on FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains how to monitor FIB and policy-route version changes on FortiGate and correlate them with SD-WAN events, session revalidation, NPU offload changes, and high softirq CPU usage.ScopeFortiGate.FortiOS 7.x and later.SolutionFortiGate can perform additional route lookups when routing information changes during the life of an existing session. Depending on the session-dirty configuration, affected sessions may be marked dirty and revalidated.The following command can be used to monitor routing-version activity:diagnose sys vd listExample:system fib version=8167 name=root/root fib_ver=26237 rpdb_ver=3185Relevant fields:system fib version: System-level FIB version indicator.fib_ver: Per-VDOM FIB version. It changes when relevant routing information changes.rpdb_ver: Per-VDOM policy-route version. It can be used to identify policy-routing database activity.Important:These are version/generation counters.For example:fib_ver: 26237 -> 26874 rpdb_ver: 3185 -> 3776Does NOT mean that 637 routes and 591 policy routes changed.It means that the corresponding routing versions changed repeatedly during the observation window.The counters confirm routing activity, but do not identify by themselves which route or feature caused the change.Establish a baselineRun several samples while the FortiGate is operating normally:execute time diagnose sys vd list | grep fibExample:fib_ver=30482 rpdb_ver=6375If repeated samples remain unchanged, no FIB or policy-route version churn was observed during that collection window.Detect routing churnDuring the issue, repeat:execute time diagnose sys vd list | grep fibIf fib_ver or rpdb_ver increase rapidly, correlate the timestamps with the routing subsystems in use.For SD-WAN environments, collect:diagnose sys sdwan member diagnose sys sdwan health-check diagnose sys sdwan service4 diagnose firewall proute listAdditionally, review the routing table when required:get router info routing-table all diagnose ip route listIf BGP or IPsec dynamically influences routing, additional useful commands include:get router info bgp summary get vpn ipsec tunnel summaryCorrelate with session revalidationCheck the configured behavior:show full-configuration system settings | grep firewall-session-dirtyFor example:set firewall-session-dirty check-allWith check-all, affected existing sessions can be marked dirty and revalidated following relevant routing or policy changes.Check session state:diagnose sys session full-statRelevant fields include:session_count= npu_session_count= nturbo_session_count= session walkers:If required, dirty sessions can also be checked:diagnose sys session list | grep \ dirty -c diagnose sys session list | grep =dirty -cCaution:Walking or grepping a very large session table can be expensive. Avoid running these commands continuously during severe CPU saturation.Correlate with CPU and offloadExample incident pattern:fib_ver: 26237 -> 26874 rpdb_ver: 3185 -> 3776 dirty sessions: 147586 session walkers: active=1 vf increasing npu_session_count: 90849 -> 40724 nturbo_session_count: 37211 -> 22508 CPU softirq: 95-97%If these events occur in the same time window, the evidence is consistent with large-scale session revalidation and temporary de-offload occurring while routing/session state is changing.This establishes correlation, not root cause.The next step is to identify which SD-WAN member, route, policy route, tunnel, or routing protocol changed at the same timestamp.Stable-state comparisonExample stable capture:fib_ver=30482 rpdb_ver=6375Repeated samples:fib_ver unchanged rpdb_ver unchanged dirty sessions = 0 session walker inactive/stable NPU/nTurbo stable CPU normalA stable comparison is useful, but it should not be considered a controlled A/B test if traffic load, topology, active links, or application placement also changed.Recommended troubleshooting workflowCPU/session collection:execute time get system performance status diagnose sys vd list | grep fib diagnose sys session full-statRouting/SD-WAN collection:execute time diagnose sys vd list | grep fib diagnose sys sdwan member diagnose sys sdwan health-check diagnose sys sdwan service4 diagnose firewall proute listFollow the flow of baseline -> problem -> recovery.Always record:Incident timestamp.Timezone.Observed symptom.Traffic impact.Management impact.SD-WAN/link changes.Configuration changes made during the test.Interpretationfib_ver changes rapidly, rpdb_ver stable: FIB/routing activity is present. topics.title: FortiGate GUI unreachable due to ACME interface configuration
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue where the administrative web interface (httpsd) becomes unreachable when the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is down, such as an IPsec tunnel.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsThe FortiGate GUI is not reachable, and users receive a 500 error when attempting to load the administration page. The httpsd process may not be running or fails to start. This issue can affect both the primary and secondary units in a High Availability cluster.Root CauseThe FortiGate management web server (httpsd) hosts the ACME client used for Let's Encrypt certificate challenges. If the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is currently down (for example, an IPsec tunnel), the web server cannot bind its listener to that interface. This causes the httpsd process to shut down, which blocks all administrative web access, including access via the management port.ResolutionWorkaroundRemove the interface binding from the ACME configuration to allow the web server to start.Connect to the FortiGate via the Command Line Interface (CLI).Run the following commands to unset the ACME interface:config system acme unset interface endThe GUI should become accessible immediately after removing the interface setting.Permanent SolutionUpgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS 7.4.13 or later. This version includes a fix for a defect where the ACME module can crash the web server during certificate renewal.

topics.title: FortiSwitch port remains active and does not generate logs when learning-limit-action shutdown is set
topics.summary: DescriptionConfiguring set learning-limit-action shutdown on a FortiSwitch port does not disable the port or generate event logs when the dynamically learned MAC address limit is exceeded.ScopeFortiSwitch standalone or managed by FortiGate (FortiLink).SolutionBy default, the mac-violation-timer parameter is set to 0, which disables the shutdown action. Additionally, MAC limit violation logging is disabled by default, preventing event logs from generating when a limit violation occurs.To enforce the shutdown behavior and record violations, set a non-zero value for mac-violation-timer and enable MAC limit violation logging globally. If the FortiSwitch is managed by FortiGate through FortiLink, you can use config system custom-command to ensure these settings persist across configuration synchronizations.Step 1: Configure global settingsConfigure logging and define the port shutdown duration (in seconds) applied after a violation:config switch global set log-mac-limit-violations enable set mac-violation-timer 180 endStep 2: Configure the port learning limitApply the learning limit, the shutdown action, and event logging to the target interface:config switch interface edit "port1" set learning-limit 1 set learning-limit-action shutdown set log-mac-event enable next endStep 3: Verify the configurationUse the following commands to inspect the port state and detect violation events:Check for active violations across all interfaces:FortiSwitch# get switch mac-limit-violations all Port VLAN ID MAC Address Timestamp Action port1* 1000 d8:93:d4:0d:88:b3 2026-09-24 19:00:21 disableCheck the physical port status:FortiSwitch# diagnose switch physical-ports list port1 Port(port1) is HW Admin down, SW Admin down, line protocol is downView system event logs for violation details:FortiSwitch# execute log display 8: 2026-09-24 19:00:21 log_id=0100001401 tz=-0600 type=event subtype=link pri=notice vd=root action="port-down" user="ctrld" unit="primary" switch.physical-port="port1" status="down" msg="primary switch port port1 has gone down" 9: 2026-09-24 19:00:21 log_id=0103042004 tz=-0600 type=event subtype=system pri=notice vd=root user="llvd" switch.interface="port1" msg="Interface MAC learning limit exceeded, MAC d8:93:d4:0d:88:b3 on port1 (Packet VID: 1000)."Static MAC addresses do not count toward the learning limit; only dynamically learned MAC addresses are evaluated.Related articleDynamic MAC address learning
