topics.title: FortiGate HA cluster out of sync due to obsolete internet-service-name
topics.summary: DescriptionA FortiGate High Availability cluster remains out of sync because of obsolete Internet Service Database entries referenced in firewall policies.ScopeFortiGate, FortiGuard.SolutionSymptomsThe secondary unit in a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster shows an "out-of-sync" status. Standard synchronization commands such as execute ha synchronize start do not resolve the issue, and the global configuration checksums between the primary and secondary units remain different.Root CauseHigh Availability (HA) synchronization failure is caused by obsolete Internet Service Database (ISDB) entries referenced in the configuration. When the primary unit contains references to ISDB objects that are no longer valid or have been updated in the database, the secondary unit cannot synchronize these obsolete entries, leading to a checksum mismatch.ResolutionIdentify obsolete services:Run the following command on the secondary unit to check for configuration errors related to obsolete internet services:diagnose debug config-error-log readLook for log entries indicating that an internet-service-name is obsolete. For example:>> internet-service-name Microsoft-Teams.Published.Worldwide.Allow(id=327992) is now obsolete. Please change the configuration(s) containing this service name.Remove obsolete references:Identify all firewall policies, local-in policies, or traffic shaping policies that reference the obsolete service IDs found in the previous step.On the primary unit, remove the obsolete internet services from those policies.Save the configuration changes.Verify synchronization:Restart the secondary unit to trigger a fresh synchronization.Verify the HA status on the primary unit using the following commands:get system ha status diagnose sys ha checksum clusterConfirm that the status for all units is now "in-sync" and that the global checksums match.

topics.title: Management interface access blocked when virtual patch and VRF are enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate blocks GUI access to the management interface when virtual patching is enabled on a local-in policy and the management interface is configured with a VRF.This behavior exists in 7.6.6 and earlier versions.FGT_A # show sys interface port1 config system interface edit "port1" set vdom "vd1" set vrf 1 set ip 172.16.10.10 255.255.255.0 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp http telnet set type physical set device-identification enable set device-user-identification disable set snmp-index 3 config ipv6 set ip6-allowaccess ping https ssh snmp end next end FGT_A # shshow firewall local-in-policy config firewall local-in-policy edit 1 set uuid 7c2f91b4-86e5-43a7-9d02-6135b8e4f0a6 set intf "port1" set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set action accept set service "ALL" set schedule "always" set virtual-patch enable next endScopeFortiGate.SolutionAfter disabling virtual-patch, GUI access will work immediately.FGT_A # config firewall local-in-policy FGT_A (local-in-policy) # edit 1 FGT_A (1) # set virtual-patch disable FGT_A (1) # endIf you unset VRF and then enable virtual-patch, GUI access can work as well:FGT_A # config sys interface FGT_A (interface) # edit port1 FGT_A (port1) # sh config system interface edit "port1" set vdom "vd1" set vrf 1 set ip 172.16.10.10 255.255.255.0 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp http telnet set type physical set device-identification enable set device-user-identification disable set snmp-index 3 config ipv6 set ip6-allowaccess ping https ssh snmp end next end FGT_A (port1) # unset vrf FGT_A (port1) # end FGT_A # config firewall local-in-policy FGT_A (local-in-policy) # edit 1 FGT_A (1) # set virtual-patch enable FGT_A (1) # endThis behavior has a fix planned for FortiOS 8.0.3.

topics.title: Enabling a routing lookup (strict) for source verification for reply packets
topics.summary: DescriptionA new feature enables a routing lookup (strict) for reply packets.ScopeFortiGate v7.6.7, v8.0.0 and later.SolutionThe command set strict-src-check enable to enable strict Reverse Path Forwarding (RPF) checks does not cover the case of matching an existing session in the reply direction. The new command was introduced in FortiOS versions 7.6.7 and 8.0.0:config system settings set src-check-reply enable endenable: Enable source verification for reply packets.disable: Disable source verification for reply packets.The command src-check-reply helps prevent spoofed reply packets on FortiGate.

topics.title: CSRF validation error, SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains
topics.summary: Description An issue where users encounter a CSRF validation error when authenticating via SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains, such as Microsoft 365. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution When a user attempts to authenticate using a federated domain (for example, Microsoft 365) via the FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP Proxy, the process fails. The user is redirected from the identity provider back to the FortiAuthenticator endpoint /saml-idp-proxy/ and receives the following error message: Request failed CSRF validation: CSRF cookie not set. Refresh your browser and try again. This is a known issue in FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10 and 8.0.3 which causes the system to fail to set the required CSRF token cookie during the SAML redirection process. When the browser performs the subsequent POST request to the login endpoint, the validation fails because the expected CSRF cookie is missing from the request headers. Resolution is to upgrade FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.11, 8.0.4 or higher. This issue is resolved in firmware version 6.6.11 and 8.0.4. Internal engineering ticket ID is 1325777. topics.title: FortiSASE secure edge tunnel stays down after a FortiOS upgrade because of a Diffie-Hellman group mismatch
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate secure edge tunnel to FortiSASE stops negotiating after the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5, why the tunnel comes up when the Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups are set to 5 and 14 and then drops again with the groups back at 20 and 21, and how to fix the condition permanently.This article also explains why the tunnel settings on FortiManager are not the source of truth for this tunnel, and how to make the workaround persist on FortiOS builds that do not contain the code fix.ScopeFortiGate configured as a FortiSASE secure edge, FortiOS 7.6.5 and 7.6.6. FortiSASE. FortiManager used as the management station for the FortiGate. FortiOS 7.6.7 and later are not affected.SolutionSymptomA FortiGate operating as a FortiSASE secure edge has a VDOM, commonly named SASE, configured for LAN extension. The tunnel to the FortiSASE edge service is not created by an administrator. FortiOS creates and maintains it automatically, under a phase 1 interface named with the prefix ul-, for example ul-npu0_vlink1, and the interface carries the description "[fgconn] Do NOT edit. Automatically generated by extension controller".After the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5 or 7.6.6, the tunnel no longer establishes. The VPN logs show a large number of IKEv2 phase 1 proposals sent to the FortiSASE peer with no answer, each cycle ending in a negotiation timeout. The responder cookie in those log entries is all zeroes, which means the peer never replied. See the following logs for examples of Fortinet Tunnel ID, local IP, and interface names.date=2026-10-12 time=23:10:55 type=VPN subtype=tunnel action=tunnel-down vd=SASE vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" duration=28678 locip=172.16.10.90 remip=192.0.2.10 remport=4500 locport=4500 version="IKEv2" role="initiator" date=2026-10-12 time=23:17:46 type=VPN subtype=phase1 logid=0101037127 action=SA_INIT vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" status="success" locip=172.16.10.90 locport=4500 remip=192.0.2.10 remport=4500 outintf="npu0_vlink1" cookies="2999982861c3180a/0000000000000000" version="IKEv2" role="initiator" date=2026-10-12 time=23:18:03 type=VPN subtype=phase1 logid=0101037124 action=negotiate vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" status="fail" error="ike negotiation timeout" duration=15 date=2026-10-12 time=23:18:16 type=VPN subtype=tunnel logid=0101037142 action=auto_transport_switch vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" msg="switch auto transport from udp to tcp"The three entries repeat on a short cycle. In one hour of logs, a single FortiGate sent 109 IKEv2 phase 1 proposals to 192.0.2.10 and received no reply, and the same FortiGate logged 54 transport switches from UDP to TCP. No tunnel-up event appears after the initial drop.The second part of the symptom is the temporary fix. Setting the DH groups on the FortiGate to 5 and 14 brings the tunnel up. Some time later the tunnel drops, and the DH groups read 20 and 21 again. The FortiGate is not losing the change at random, as explained under "Why the configuration reverts".Root causeFortiOS 7.6.5 changed the default phase 1 and phase 2 DH group list from 14 and 5 to 20 and 21. The change is documented in the FortiOS 7.6.5 Release Notes, section Changes in default behavior. The FortiGate administration guide states the current default: by default, FortiGate uses DH group 20 and 21 when a VPN is configured from the GUI or CLI.FortiSASE continues to use DH groups 14 and 5 for this tunnel type, as documented in the FortiSASE deployment guides, section IPsec configuration. The tunnel created by the extension controller inherits the FortiOS default, which on FortiOS 7.6.5 and 7.6.6 is 20 and 21 with no other group in the list.The two ends therefore share no DH group. The FortiGate sends an IKEv2 IKE_SA_INIT proposal offering groups 20 and 21, the peer has no matching group, and the exchange never completes. The proposal payload in the IKE debug of an affected FortiGate contains the DH group values 0x14 (20) and 0x15 (21) only.The transport setting adds a second delay on top of the mismatch. These tunnels are created with transport set to auto. When the UDP attempt fails, FortiOS opens a TCP session to the peer on port 4500, and that session also fails, so each negotiation window is consumed before the FortiGate returns to UDP. The log entries with action auto_transport_switch and the IKE debug line 'auto transport timeout, use tcp port 4500' identify this behavior.Why the configuration revertsThe tunnel is an object owned by the FortiSASE connection controller on the FortiGate. When the controller re-creates the tunnel, it applies the FortiOS default DH group list, which replaces any manual change and any value that came from FortiManager. A tunnel reset on the FortiSASE side is enough to trigger that rebuild. This is why the tunnel comes up after the DH groups are set to 5 and 14, works for a period, and then drops with the groups back at 20 and 21.This also explains a common source of confusion when the FortiGate is managed by FortiManager. topics.title: Information required for FortiAppSec Cloud troubleshooting

Providing the information outlined below helps Fortinet Support understand the issue, identify its scope, and investigate it more efficiently.ScopeFortiAppSec Cloud.SolutionRequired information.When opening a FortiAppSec Cloud support case, provide the following information:Application information.Application name.Application domain/FQDN.Affected URL(s) or specific application endpoints.Issue description.A clear and detailed description of the issue.Expected behavior and actual behavior.Exact error message or HTTP status code, if applicable.Date and time when the issue occurred.Scope and impact.Number of affected users (single user or multiple users).Impact across users, including whether all users or only specific users are affected.Scope of the issue, such as the entire application or specific pages, URLs, or functionalities.Frequency of occurrence (consistent or intermittent).Previous working status.Previous operational status of the application.Date and time when the issue was first observed.Application deployment status (newly onboarded application or existing application).Recent changes to the application, origin server, DNS, network, or FortiAppSec Cloud configuration before the issue started.Testing and reproduction.Steps required to reproduce the issue.Reproducibility results, including whether the issue occurs consistently or intermittently.Testing results from different browsers, devices, or networks, if available.Additional evidence.Depending on the nature of the issue, provide the following information and supporting evidence:Connectivity or performance issues: HAR files captured from both working and non-working scenarios, if available.Application errors: Screenshots and exact error messages displayed.Other issues: Relevant logs, screenshots, timestamps, or additional information that may help with the investigation.Note: HAR files may contain sensitive information, including session cookies, authentication tokens, and other credentials. topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to resolve the "Failed to save changes" error encountered when saving a custom Application Control signature.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionA syntax error can occur when saving a custom Application Control signature if the signature definition contains line breaks or formatting that prevents the parser from correctly interpreting the opening and closing parentheses.When attempting to save a custom Application Control signature, the GUI displays the error "Failed to save changes".To investigate the issue, run the following commands.diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug cli 8 diagnose debug cmdb-trace diagnose debug enableThe CLI and CMDB trace debug output indicates that the closing or opening parenthesis cannot be identified. This can occur when the signature definition is formatted across multiple lines in a way that the parser cannot recognize.kvm42 # 0: config application custom 0: edit "OutboundTSTServerCommunication" 0: set comment '' 0: set signature "F-SBID( 0: --attack_id 9901; 0: --name \"Outbound.TST.Server.Communication\"; 0: --default_action drop_session; 0: --service HTTP; 0: --protocol tcp; 0: --app_cat 25; 0: --flow from_client; 0: --pattern \"/.well-known/tst.json\"; 0: --context uri; 0: --no_case; 0: --weight 40; 0: )" 0: unset protocol 0: unset technology 0: unset behavior 0: unset vendor [error] line 1 offset 8: F-SBID( ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 2 offset 18: --attack_id 9901; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 3 offset 44: rver.Communication"; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 4 offset 31: action drop_session; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 5 offset 16: --service HTTP; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 6 offset 16: --protocol tcp; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 7 offset 14: --app_cat 25; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 8 offset 20: --flow from_client; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 9 offset 35: ell-known/mcp.json"; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 10 offset 15: --context uri; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 11 offset 11: --no_case; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 12 offset 13: --weight 40; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 13 offset 1: ) ^^^ open bracet not found -2: end The debug output reports syntax errors, including closing round bracket not found and open bracket not found. topics.title: FortiManager firmware upgrade preview shows "No record found" even with an assigned device
topics.summary: DescriptionAn explanation for a "No record found" message occurring in the Firmware Upgrade Preview of a Firmware Template in FortiManager even when a device is assigned to the template. Steps to resolve it are provided.ScopeFortiManager.FortiGate.SolutionThe Firmware Upgrade Preview only lists devices that match the platform selected in the template. If the template platform is different from the platform of the assigned device, the preview has nothing to calculate and shows "No record found". No other error is shown, and the device still appears under "Assigned to Device/Group".This is easy to miss with virtual FortiGates, because several platform names look similar (for example FortiGate-VM64 and FortiGate-VM64-KVM).The device platform shows in the FortiGate CLI:FGT-SPOKE # get sys status Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.9,build2829,250924 (GA.M) First GA patch build date: 230509 Current Security Level: High Firmware Signature: certified Virus-DB: 1.00000(2018-04-09 18:07) Extended DB: 1.00000(2018-04-09 18:07) ....................... ............... .........The template platform is FortiGate-VM64, which does not match FortiGate-VM64-KVM.To avoid this, set the template Platform to "GA Versions" instead of a specific platform. The template is then not tied to one platform, and the Firmware Upgrade Preview selects the correct FortiGate platform for each assigned device.Go to Device Manager -> Firmware Templates and edit the template.In "Edit Upgrade Firmware", set Platform to "GA Versions".Select the target version under "Upgrade to".Save the template and open the Upgrade Preview.Related article:Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to select Setup Firmware Upgrade for FortiGate

topics.title: High packet drops occur during traffic bursts on a FortiGate VM hosted in Google Cloud Platform
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the case when a FortiGate VM hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experiences significant packet loss and latency during high bursts of traffic. While interface-level counters do not show RX drops, the internal RX queue statistics indicate drops.ScopeFortiGate VM, GCP.SolutionThe issue is caused by RX queue buffer exhaustion. When the GCP instance presents only one RX queue, the ring buffer descriptors are exhausted during traffic bursts, leading to packet drops. This occurs even if the CPU utilization is not high, as the bottleneck is at the NIC descriptor level rather than the CPU processing level.The following command will list the interface counters. Notice that all the RX drops are zero.diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic port1 Name: port1 Driver: gve Version: 1.3.0 Bus: 0000:00:04.0 HWaddr: 42:01:0a:5c:1a:02 State: up Link: up Mtu: 1460 Supported: Advertised: Speed: 32000half Auto: disabled Rx packets: 14891007 Rx bytes: 1101897774 Rx compressed: 0 Rx dropped: 0 Rx errors: 0 Rx Length err: 0 Use the command below to get more detailed interface stats; it lists the drops on the RX queue.diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic-stats port1 port1 statistics: rx_packets: 1833537831 tx_packets: 1329988458 rx_bytes: 1997339306123 tx_bytes: 1541708454631 -- output trimmed--- rx_queue_drop_cnt[0]: 1716637 rx_no_buffers_posted[0]: 1716637 rx_drops_packet_over_mru[0]: 0 rx_drops_invalid_checksum[0]: 0A non-zero and incrementing values of the counters (rx_queue_drop_cnt and rx_no_buffers_posted) indicate that packets are being dropped at the queue level as the NIC has run out of available descriptors.To resolve the buffer exhaustion, increase the number of RX queues. This provides more descriptors and allows multiple CPUs to process packets in parallel. In Google Cloud Platform, this is achieved by changing the VM instance type to a supported machine series that provides multiple queues.It is possible to notice more queue indexes ([0], [1]) when RX queues are increased.diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic-stats port1 ---output clipped--- Rx dropped: 0 Tx dropped: 0 rx_dropped: 0 tx_dropped: 0 rx_desc_err_dropped_pkt: 0 rx_dropped_pkt[0]: 0 <-- rx_queue_drop_cnt[0]: 0 rx_drops_packet_over_mru[0]: 0 rx_drops_invalid_checksum[0]: 0 rx_dropped_pkt[1]: 0 <-- rx_queue_drop_cnt[1]: 0 rx_drops_packet_over_mru[1]: 0 rx_drops_invalid_checksum[1]: 0

topics.title: How to disable the HTTP TRACE method on FortiClient EMS for Linux
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to disable the HTTP TRACE method on FortiClient EMS for Linux when vulnerability scanners report that the Apache web server accepts HTTP TRACE requests.ScopeFortiClient EMS.SolutionThe Apache web server used by FortiClient EMS may allow HTTP TRACE requests depending on the underlying Linux distribution and its default Apache configuration.On some RHEL deployments, HTTP TRACE requests may return HTTP 200 OK and echo the original request. On Debian/Ubuntu deployments, Apache may reject these requests by default.To disable the HTTP TRACE method, follow these steps.Verify the HTTP TRACE behavior.From a Windows machine with connectivity to EMS, open PowerShell and execute the following:curl.exe -ki -X TRACE https:// /When TRACE is enabled, the server may return the following:HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: Apache Content-Type: message/http TRACE / HTTP/1.1 Host: Modify the Apache configuration.Access the underlying Linux operating system with administrative privileges.For RHEL, edit:/etc/httpd/conf/httpd.confFor Debian/Ubuntu, edit the following:/etc/apache2/apache2.confAdd the following directive to the Apache configuration:TraceEnable OffValidate the configuration and restart Apache.For RHEL:sudo httpd -t sudo systemctl restart httpd sudo systemctl status httpdFor Debian/Ubuntu:sudo apache2ctl configtest sudo systemctl restart apache2 sudo systemctl status apache2Ensure the configuration validation completes successfully before restarting the service.Note: Restarting Apache may temporarily interrupt EMS web services. Perform the change during a maintenance window.Verify that HTTP TRACE is disabled.Repeat the TRACE request:curl.exe -ki -X TRACE https:// /The expected response is:HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not AllowedThe server should no longer return HTTP 200 OK with the original TRACE request echoed in the response body.For FortiClient EMS HA deployments, apply the configuration change and verify the results on each EMS application server.

topics.title: Understanding FortiPortal policy package installation flow in FortiManager JSON API debug
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the JSON API flow between FortiPortal and FortiManager when a firewall policy is modified from FortiPortal and the policy package is installed.The FortiManager JSON API debug can be used to identify the configuration sent by FortiPortal, the installation preview process, and the final policy package installation task.ScopeFortiPortal, FortiManager.SolutionThe following debug commands can be used on FortiManager to capture the JSON API requests sent from FortiPortal:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug service sys 255 diagnose debug service main 255 diagnose debug enableWhen a firewall policy is modified from FortiPortal, FortiPortal sends an API update request to the corresponding policy object in the FortiManager policy package.In the following example, firewall policy ID 2 in policy package FGT-1 was modified from FortiPortal.The FortiPortal IP address has been replaced with in the debug output.Policy configuration topics.title: FortiManager user session disconnection issues when using Cloudflare ZTNA
topics.summary: Description When administrators access the FortiManager GUI via Cloudflare ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access), the login session may automatically terminate or disconnect roughly 30 seconds after logging in. This typically occurs because proxy routing, load-balancing, or edge POP switches cause minor fluctuations in the client's apparent source IP address, triggering session security validation failures on the FortiManager side. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer Solution To resolve this issue, you need to configure FortiManager to bypass strict source IP validation checks for active sessions. Log in to the FortiManager CLI as an administrator and execute the following commands: config system global set skip-ip-check-in-session enable end Once this setting is enabled, FortiManager will ignore intermediate source IP modifications or fluctuations during an active session, allowing Cloudflare ZTNA users to maintain a stable, uninterrupted connection to the GUI. FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number
topics.summary: Description FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices. Scope FortiPAM, FortiClient EMS. Solution Devices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number. Root Cause FortiPAM retrieves the default tenant serial number instead of the specific tenant serial number in multi-tenant FortiClient EMS environments. This is identified as BUG 1343587. Permanent Fix Update FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.9 or later. Workaround Perform the following steps to clear the invalid tags and refresh the synchronization: Clear the invalid tags associated with the incorrect serial number by running the following command on FortiPAM: diagnose endpoint tags remove-by-sn Restart the fabric connector daemon to refresh the data: diag test app fcnacd 99 Verify that the tags are synchronized with the correct serial number using the following commands: diagnose test application fcnacd 2 diagnose test application fcnacd 7 Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Automation Stitch for collecting debug log when HA failover
topics.summary:
DescriptionHow to use Automation Stitch to collect debug logs when a FortiGate high availability failover occurs.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionCreate the auto-script:When an HA member loss occurs, one of the common root causes is high CPU utilization. If the CPU is overloaded, the FortiGate may fail to process HA heartbeat packets in a timely manner, triggering a false-positive or actual cluster split/failure. To investigate whether high CPU usage contributed to the HA member drop, use the troubleshooting command below to capture the CPU usage at the time of the issue.config system auto-script edit "Collect logs" set script "get system status get system performance status get system ha status diagnose sys top 1 200 1 diagnose sys top-mem 200" next endCreate an automation action:In this example, the FTP server IP address is 10.207.2.82, the username is 'admin', and the password is 'password'. The FTP server can be changed to a TFTP server, and a username and password are not required for TFTP.The first action is the action to run the auto-script.The second action is the action to send the output to FTP server.config system automation-action edit "Run collect logs" set action-type cli-script set script "execute auto-script start "Collect logs"" set accprofile "super_admin" next edit "Send to FTP server" set action-type cli-script set script "execute auto-script backup ftp "Collect logs" 10.207.2.82:21 admin password" set accprofile "super_admin" next endCreate an automation trigger to trigger when a Heartbeat packet is lost:config system automation-trigger edit "Heartbeat packet lost" set event-type event-log set logid 37910 next endCreate an automation stitch:A 3-second delay was added to handle scenarios where the script output is extensive, ensuring sufficient time to transmit the completed results to the FTP server.config system automation-stitch edit "HA peer lost" set trigger "Heartbeat packet lost" config actions edit 1 set action "Run collect logs" set required enable next edit 2 set action "Send to FTP server" set delay 3 set required enable next end next endThe result on the FTP server:Below is an example of the debug log when the script runs normally:FGVM020000108306(Primary) # diagnose debug application autod -1 Debug messages will be on for 30 minutes. topics.title: GUI inaccessible after upgrading to FortiSOAR version 8.0.0 due to nginx failure
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to restore GUI access when nginx fails to start after upgrading FortiSOAR to version 8.0.0.ScopeFortiSOAR.SolutionAfter the upgrade, the FortiSOAR web portal is inaccessible, and the nginx service fails to start. The nginx error logs display the following message:[emerg] unknown directive "ssl" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf:217This occurs when /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf contains the standalone ssl on; directive. Previous nginx versions accepted this directive with a warning. nginx version 1.26.3, used in FortiSOAR 8.0.0, rejects it, preventing the service from starting.To correct the configuration and restore web portal access:Create a backup of the configuration file:sudo cp -p /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.conf.before-fixOpen the configuration file:sudo vi /etc/nginx/conf.d/cyops-api.confLocate and remove the obsolete standalone directive:ssl on;If the ssl_protocols directive contains a duplicate TLSv1.3 value:ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 TLSv1.3;Replace it with:ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;In each /auth/ and /websocket/ location block, remove duplicate occurrences so that the following directive appears only once per block:proxy_ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;Ensure the following directive appears only once within the same server block:ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m;Save the file and exit the editor. Validate the configuration:sudo nginx -tConfirm the output reports that the configuration syntax is correct and the test is successful. If errors remain, resolve them before restarting nginx.Restart the nginx service:sudo systemctl restart nginxVerify the service status:sudo systemctl status nginx --no-pager -lConfirm the service shows as active (running), then verify that the FortiSOAR GUI is accessible.

topics.title: Customer Service Note: Email interaction when working tickets with Fortinet Support
topics.summary: Description This article describes a feature deployed in January 2019. The 'Email Interaction' feature allows the choice of whether ticket updates can be handled via email. This avoids the need to log into the Support Portal to read the latest ticket comments which have been added by the Fortinet engineer, or to provide updates to the engineer. When this feature is enabled the effects are that: (1) When a Fortinet engineer adds notes to a ticket, the entire content of the latest update will be sent via email to all of the contacts named on that ticket. The 3 most recent ticket comments will also be included in this mail. File attachments that are added to the ticket will also appear in this mail. (2) Upon receipt by email of a ticket update, it is possible choose to simply reply to the email and the reply will be added to the ticket notes. This reply may include file attachments. The ticket will then be placed into a "Received Customer Feedback" status. Email is not a secure, guaranteed delivery method. If the ticket update or file attachment contains private or sensitive information then the recommended approach is to update the ticket via the Support Portal rather than by using email. Scope Customer Service. Solution How do I reply to an email to update my ticket: The format of the email received when a Fortinet engineer updates a ticket is shown below: From: ticket_update@fortinet.com To: andy.kemp@abc.com Subject: Re: Ticket No. xxxxxxx Ticket Title: FortiGate configuration *** The following update has been added to your ticket *** Please provide more information of the problem you have reported ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- You may provide an update and add attachments to this ticket by replying to this email. Do not modify the content of this received email as it will not be added to the ticket. Alternatively, to provide an update to this ticket, add attachments or verify the status, please click here. If you have any urgent questions or require further assistance, please contact your regional Customer Services and Support team who will be happy to assist you. For Support Center contact information please visit http://www.fortinet.com/support/contact_support.html If you wish to provide feedback on your support experience, please visit https://support.fortinet.com/survey/Survey.aspx?ticketid=xxxxxxxx Best Regards, Fortinet Customer Services and Support *** The most recent updates to this tickets are given below *** Simply reply to this email. It is recommended to not alter the content of the subject line. Do not alter the text in the body of the received email (the section which contains the update from the Fortinet engineer) as this section will not be added to the ticket. How quickly will the reply be added to the ticket: The reply will normally be added to the ticket within 15 minutes. It will then be visible through the Support Portal. How can the 'Email Interaction' feature be enabled / disabled: This feature is enabled at the level of the entire support account and applies to the main account and all additional users. Select 'Edit' and then set the 'Allow ticket processing by email' option to either Yes (Enabled) or No (Disabled). A value of 'Undefined' may be displayed for some accounts. This means that the account owner has not expressed a preference and in this case the feature will be disabled. If the feature is Enabled/Disabled when will the change take effect: The change will take effect immediately. For example, if there is an open ticket and the feature is enabled, then the very next outbound comment sent by Fortinet could be replied to via email. How can I find the owner of the support account that I use: Contact Fortinet Customer Services by creating a ticket, using the Chat service, or calling on one of the telephone numbers given here. They will be able to give the name of the owner of the support account. Which email accounts are used by Fortinet to send email relating to tickets: Ticket updates for technical assistance tickets will be sent from the ticket_update@fortinet.com email address. For other types of support requests the reply may come from one of cs@fortinet.com, fsa_submit@fortinet.com, submitapp@fortinet.com, submitvirus@fortinet.com, vulnwatch@fortinet.com. If a reply to an update cannot be processed then a rejection will be sent from noreply@fortinet.com, replies should not be sent to this address as the mailbox is unattended. topics.title: Slow downloads through the explicit web proxy when tcp-option is disabled
topics.summary: DescriptionLarge downloads through the explicit web proxy may be slow when tcp-option is disabled.In this example, downloads stayed at about 650 KB/s with a server round-trip time of 100 ms. A faster internet connection made no difference.Enabling tcp-option allows TCP window scaling, which removes this limit.ScopeFortiOS 8.0.x, FortiOS 7.6.x, FortiOS 7.4.x.SolutionWhen tcp-option is disabled, FortiGate removes all TCP options except MSS from the handshake, including window scaling. This limits the TCP receive window to 65,535 bytes. The sender fills the window, then waits for an acknowledgement before sending more data. With a round-trip time of 100 ms, downloads stay at around 600–650 KB/s, even on a faster link. The connection starts normally, with no packet loss or resets. The longer the round-trip time, the lower the download speed.The capture below shows the connection between the client and the proxy. The client requests window scaling, SACK, and timestamps. The proxy replies with MSS only.No. Time Source Destination Proto Len Info 3307 0.000000 TCP 74 48718 → 8080 0SYN] Seq=0 Win=64240 Len=0 MSS=1460 SACK_PERM TSval=3372514582 TSecr=0 WS=16384 3308 0.000043 TCP 58 8080 → 48718 4SYN, ACK] Seq=0 Ack=1 Win=29200 Len=0 MSS=1460 3311 0.000307 TCP 54 48718 → 8080 �ACK] Seq=1 Ack=1 Win=64240 Len=0The second capture is between the FortiGate and the server. The FortiGate's own SYN has MSS only, so the server cannot use window scale either.The time from SYN to SYN-ACK is about 100 ms.No. Time Source Destination Proto Len Info 24663 0.000000 TCP 58 21274 → 443 4SYN] Seq=0 Win=29200 Len=0 MSS=1460 24715 0.100115 TCP 58 443 → 21274 3SYN, ACK] Seq=0 Ack=1 Win=64240 Len=0 MSS=1380 24716 0.100142 TCP 54 21274 → 443 2ACK] Seq=1 Ack=1 Win=29200 Len=0To fix the issue, enable tcp-option.In a multi-VDOM environment, enter config global first.config global config system global set tcp-option enable end Start a new download after the change. Window scaling is negotiated during the SYN and SYN-ACK exchange, so existing connections will keep their original settings.Related documents:Prevent FortiGate from responding with TCP timestamp

topics.title: FortiNAC-F: Captive portal User SAML SSO redirect loop caused by SP URL/Portal FQDN mismatch
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a captive portal redirect loop with User SAML SSO, and how to fix it. The user authenticates successfully at the IdP and is returned to the FortiNAC-F portal, but the device is never registered. The cause is a hostname mismatch: the SP URL of the User SAML SSO service connector is different from the captive portal Fully-Qualified Host Name set in Portal -> Portal SSL.ScopeFortiNAC-F 7.6.3 and later (User SAML SSO service connector). Observed on 7.6.7 build 0976.FortiAuthenticator as SAML IdP, including IdP proxy to Microsoft Entra ID. The same applies to any SAML IdP.Standalone and High Availability (1+1) deployments, L2 or L3 isolation.SolutionSymptoms:The rogue host is placed in the Registration VLAN and opens the captive portal.USER login redirects to the IdP. Authentication succeeds, the browser returns to FortiNAC-F, then lands back on the portal start page. Every new attempt repeats the cycle.The host stays Rogue, no SSO user record is created, and no CoA is sent to the controller.FortiAuthenticator shows the IdP side as successful, repeated on every attempt: Logging -> Log Access -> Logs, Log Type 20502 (SAML IdP SP_Request OK), Status Success, message "SAML assertion request from SP ' ', send back response for user ' '."Common trigger: the portal FQDN or the connector SP URL was changed, for example during HA testing or troubleshooting, and the other value was not changed to match.Cause:FortiNAC-F builds every SP value (SP Entity ID, ACS URL, SLS URL, SP metadata) from the connector's SP URL. The captive portal itself is served under the Fully-Qualified Host Name set in Portal > Portal SSL. When the two hostnames differ:The portal starts SSO. The AuthnRequest sends the SP ACS URL on the SP URL host, for example https://nacportal.example.com/registration/saml/ /acs.The IdP authenticates the user and the browser POSTs a valid, signed SAMLResponse to that ACS URL.That hostname is not the portal FQDN. FortiNAC-F answers the POST with its generic portal redirect (302 to https:// /registration/), the same response it sends to OS captive-probe URLs. The SAMLResponse is never handed to SAML processing.The portal session is still unauthenticated, so the portal offers the login again, and the cycle repeats.The ACS POST lands on the wrong host, so login loops:FortiNAC's SAML SSO guide states that for User SAML SSO in HA the "Captive Portal URL must remain consistent". The redirect behaviour in step 3 is not described in the documentation; it was confirmed from the FortiNAC-F logs and the browser capture in a support case.Not the cause in this condition: the IdP or Entra ID configuration, the IdP certificate, attribute mapping, NTP, MAB or RADIUS, and HA failover itself. Known issue 1208434 ("Users cannot register through the captive portal with SAML SSO authentication because of redirects") is resolved in FortiNAC-F 7.6.7 and is a separate condition.How to identify:Compare the connector's SP hostname with the portal hostname, then confirm in the logs that the ACS POST was redirected rather than processed. All values below are examples.Compare the two hostnames.FortiNAC-F: Network -> Service Connectors -> -> Service Provider Settings -> SP URL. The SP Entity ID, SP ACS (Login) URL, and SP SLS (Logout) URL are all built from this value.FortiNAC-F: Portal -> Portal SSL -> Fully-Qualified Host Name. This is the hostname the captive portal is served under.In the screenshot below, the SP URL is nacportal.example.com, while the portal is served as secureportal.example.com.FortiAuthenticator holds the same SP values, taken from the imported SP metadata: Authentication -> SAML IdP -> Service Providers -> -> SP Metadata.Check FortiAuthenticator. The IdP returns a successful assertion on every attempt: Log Type 20502, Status Success, repeated each time the user retries.Check the browser capture (HAR or SAML-tracer). The AuthnRequest names the ACS URL on the SP URL host. The POST of the SAMLResponse to that URL returns a generic redirect to the portal start page:AuthnRequest AssertionConsumerServiceURL="https://nacportal.example.com/registration/saml/FAC_SAML/acs" POST https://nacportal.example.com/registration/saml/FAC_SAML/acs (RelayState=&SAMLResponse=...) -> 302 Found Server: Apache Location: https://secureportal.example.com/registration/ Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1 Content-Length: 228The browser then loads the portal start page again, with the host still unregistered:Check the FortiNAC-F logs (node in control). Use grab-log-snapshot, or tail live with diagnose tail -F output.nessus.access_log: the ACS POST gets the same generic 302 as OS captive-probe URLs (/connecttest.txt, /generate_204):192.168.67.25 - - [25/Oct/2026:10:17:11 +0000] "POST /registration/saml/FAC_SAML/acs HTTP/1.1" 302 228 192.168.67.25 - - [25/Oct/2026:10:13:01 +0000] "GET /connecttest.txt HTTP/1.1" 302 227output.nessus: SSO is started, but no SAML processing is logged for the ACS POST:INFO yams - c

topics.title: Technical Tip: RMA procedure for FortiGates with a single HA license (Single FortiGuard License)
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to perform an RMA for FortiGates that have a single HA license (Single FortiGuard license).ScopeFortiGate.SolutionWhen dealing with failures involving a FortiGate with a single license shared among Cluster/HA members, the license transfer procedure during an RMA differs significantly from the procedure used for a FortiGate with a conventional license. As multiple FortiGate units are covered by the same license, the new FortiGate provided through the RMA cannot be added to the existing single license when the standard RMA process is followed.In this case, when opening a ticket with Fortinet Support, indicate that the firewall has a license shared across the Cluster to prevent automatic license transfer.For instructions on creating a support ticket, refer to Customer Service Tip: How to create a ticket for Fortinet TAC.After opening the ticket and confirming the firewall failure, when transferring the license, follow the steps below:Access Fortinet Support:After logging in, go to Services and select Asset Management.Under Product, select Product List and search for the HA serial number instead of the serial number of the faulty firewall.Select the device and go to RMA Transfer.Select the faulty firewall, either Device 1 or Device 2. Then enter the serial number of the replacement firewall and click Replace. Verify all information and complete the transfer.The license transfer has been completed successfully, allowing the new FortiGate to be added to the cluster and share the same license. For questions regarding this process, contact the FortiCare Support: Customer Service.Related articles:Technical Tip: The HA Cluster license requirementsTechnical Tip: Additional Info regarding Single FortiGuard license for FortiGate A-P HA cluster featureTechnical Tip: FortiGate Models and FortiOS support for HA LicensesTechnical Tip: How to restore a FortiGate HA cluster after RMA

topics.title: How to check and clear the firmware upgrade profile database (scheduled upgrade tasks) on FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionInstructions to check the firmware upgrade profile database on FortiManager with the diagnose fwmanager profile commands. It also describes how to clear the stored profile entries.ScopeFortiManager 7.2.3, 7.4.0, 7.6.0, 8.0.0 and later.SolutionFortiManager stores the firmware upgrade profiles of each ADOM (the enforced firmware version and the upgrade schedule used for scheduled firmware upgrade tasks) in an internal profile database. Since FortiManager 7.2.3, 7.4.0, 7.6.0 and 8.0.0, the following CLI commands are available to list this database and to clear it.Check the firmware upgrade profile databaseTo list the firmware upgrade profiles of all ADOMs, run the following command in the FortiManager CLI:diagnose fwmanager profile listExample output:fwm profile files in adom root(3): adom3_aaa: { "adom_oid": 3, "data": { "checksum": "1790596055-0417879535", "description": null, "enforced version": null, "image-source": null, "schedule-day": null, "schedule-end-time": null, "schedule-start-time": null, "schedule-type": 0 }, "name": "aaa", "oid": 6293 } adom3_AAA: { "adom_oid": 3, "data": { "checksum": "1790594072-0058378931", "description": null, "enforced version": [ { "flags": 104, "platform": "FortiGate-601F", "product": 1, "upgrade-path": 1, "version": "7.6.7-b3704" } ], "image-source": null, "schedule-day": null, "schedule-end-time": null, "schedule-start-time": null, "schedule-type": 0 }, "name": "AAA", "oid": 6288 } fwm profile files in adom FortiCarrier(104): fwm profile files in adom A74(169): fwm profile files in adom ADOMTEST(493): fwm profile files in adom AAA(591): adom591_FOS-upgrade: { "adom_oid": 591, "data": { "checksum": "1793048616-0646891765", "description": "7.4.12", "enforced version": [ { "flags": 104, "platform": "FGT-Default", "product": 1, "upgrade-path": 1, "version": "7.4.12-b2902" } ], "image-source": null, "schedule-day": null, "schedule-end-time": null, "schedule-start-time": null, "schedule-type": 0 }, "name": "FOS-upgrade", "oid": 6632 }The output is grouped by ADOM. The name and ID of each ADOM are shown in the header line (for example, adom root(3)). An ADOM with no profiles has an empty list.The main fields of each profile are:FieldDescriptionadom_oidObject ID of the ADOM that the profile belongs tonameName of the firmware upgrade profiledescriptionDescription of the profile (for example, the target firmware version)enforced versionTarget firmware for the profile: platform and version/build. null if no version is setschedule-type, schedule-day, schedule-start-time, schedule-end-timeUpgrade schedule of the profile. null if no schedule is configured.image-sourceSource of the firmware image. null if not set.checksumChecksum of the profile dataoidObject ID of the profileClear the firmware upgrade profile database.To clear the firmware upgrade profiles of a specific ADOM, run:diagnose fwmanager profile clear If no ADOM name is specified, the profiles of all ADOMs are cleared:diagnose fwmanager profile clearExample output:clearing fwm profile in adom root(3):... remove adom3_aaa remove adom3_AAA clearing fwm profile in adom FortiCarrier(104):... clearing fwm profile in adom A74(169):... clearing fwm profile in adom ADOMTEST(493):... clearing fwm profile in adom AAA(591):... remove adom591_FOS-upgradeEach remove line shows a profile entry that was removed from the database.Note:The commands are available only in FortiManager 7.2.3, 7.4.0, 7.6.0, 8.0.0 and later. They are not available in earlier builds.Run diagnose fwmanager profile list before and after diagnose fwmanager profile clear to confirm which entries were removed.Running the clear command without an ADOM name affects all ADOMs. Specify the ADOM name to limit the change to one ADOM.

topics.title: Slow dynamic VLAN assignment when using 802.1X and MAC authentication bypass
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an Access-Reject response.In comparison, when the RADIUS server returns an Access-Accept response, authentication and network access are typically completed much faster.Root CauseThe delay may be related to the authentication priority configured in the 802.1X security policy. When the priority is set to "legacy", the switch may take longer to process the authentication sequence and transition to the Guest VLAN following an authentication failure.ResolutionStep 1: Update the Authentication Priority.Log in to the FortiGate CLI and change the authentication priority from "legacy" to "dot1x-mab" in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set auth-priority dot1x-mab next endReplace with the name of the applicable 802.1X security policy.This setting prioritizes 802.1X and MAB authentication according to the configured authentication sequence and may reduce the time required to transition to the Guest VLAN after an authentication failure.Step 2: Review the Guest VLAN and Authentication Timeout Settings.Verify that MAB and Guest VLAN assignment are enabled and that the appropriate VLAN is configured in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set mac-auth-bypass enable set guest-vlan enable set guest-vlan-id " " next endIf the environment requires a VLAN assignment when the RADIUS server times out, review the authentication server timeout VLAN settings supported by the FortiOS version in use. Configure these settings only when the intended behavior is to assign the designated VLAN following a server timeout.Step 3: Review Re-authentication Settings.If the delay persists, review the FortiSwitch 802.1X re-authentication settings. The maximum number of re-authentication attempts can be configured as follows:config switch-controller 802-1X-settings set max-reauth-attempt 0 endStep 4: Verify the configuration.After applying the changes, perform the following checks:Connect a test device that is not authorized for 802.1X authentication to the FortiSwitch port.Check the RADIUS server logs and confirm that the authentication request receives an Access-Reject response.Verify whether MAB authentication is attempted according to the configured authentication sequence and timeout settings.Confirm that the port transitions to the configured Guest VLAN.Verify that the transition time has improved and that authorized devices continue to authenticate and obtain network access as expected.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Explaining 'diagnose traffictest' command limitation on FortiOS
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the limitations of the 'diagnose traffictest' command and how to properly test hardware throughput trafficScopeAll FortiGate models.SolutionIPERF is a tool used for active measurements of the maximum achievable bandwidth on IP networks. FortiGate does have the command 'diagnose traffictest' which is a reduced implementation of IPERF on FortiOS as described in Technical Tip: Use cases for the diagnose traffictest command. The fact that IPERF implementation on FortiGate was reduced can affect the result of bandwidth and throughput tests when they were started from the FortiGate interface instead of having IPERF traffic crossing the FortiGate device. Using a Virtual Machine with Win10 Pro and a NIC of 10Gbps behind the FortiGate 100F for example, that has 2x 10Gbps ports (x1 and x2), is possible to reach ~9Gbps of throughput. Checking the widget of bandwidth on FortiGate for interfaces x1 and x2. Checking IPERF results on VM. Now using the FortiGate 100F x1 interface as the source of the IPERF traffic (IPERF traffic is not crossing the FortiGate), the results are not the same. Checking the widget of bandwidth on FortiGate for interfaces x1 and x2 and IPERF output while the test is still running. The 10Gbps interface x1 cannot reach more than ~900Mbps not because of the hardware throughput, but because of the IPERF reduced implementation on FortiGate. Conclusion: To validate the actual FortiGate throughput and set up the upload and download speed baseline, an external server and client are required to test the throughput with FortiGate in between as the first network diagram presented in this article.Note:The iPerf3 server on the FortiGate cannot be used as a full-featured iPerf3 server.It can be used only for the interface tests between FortiGate ports or as a client towards a server. For tests where an iPerf3 server is required, use a Windows or Linux machine with iPerf3 configured as a server. Related article:Technical Tip: Setting up iperf server and client

The device status displays 'Online - Upgrade failed', and the Upgrade Status displays 'Upgrade failed'. In some instances, the device status may show 'Rebooting with new firmware', while the Upgrade Status displays 'Firmware info unavailable'.Check the console output and observe the following messages:Image verification OK! Failed to get the image encryption key!Retry the firmware upgrade by manually uploading the FortiOS v8.0.2 firmware image through the GUI. The upgrade fails again.Verify that the device remains on FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245.Workaround: Upgrade the firmware using TFTP via the CLI. topics.title: FortiManager policy package import error "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device". Scope FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following: The Download Import Report shows as following: "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-BlockURL_IP_Group1, oid=2636, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" What happened is FortiManager being unable to copy the password from system external-resource due to it being encrypted. To solve the issue, disable the "private-data-encrytion" in Device Manager -> Device & Groups -> select the FortiGate -> CLI Configurations -> System -> Global. After changing the setting, FortiManager's Import Configuration does not fail anymore. topics.title: How to save a FortiManager API session as a variable in Postman and reuse it in other API requests
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to save and reuse API sessions in Postman without having to copy and paste them every time.ScopeFortiManager, FortiAnalyzer.SolutionWhen using Postman to send API requests to FortiManager, you may need to copy and paste the session ID to other requests. This process can be time-consuming, especially if there are many requests in Postman. To solve this, you can use scripts in Postman to save the session as a variable every time a login API request is sent to FortiManager. First, create an Environment in Postman to store the variable(s): Next, create the POST request for API login to FortiManager in Postman: In the same request page, click on the Scripts tab, then select Post-response: You can then enter the following JavaScript code:let session = pm.response.json().session; pm.environment.set("session", session); The first line of the code reads the “session” attribute from the API response.The second line of the code saves it as a variable in the Environment. When you run the request, Postman will save the session ID into the Environment.Before request: After request:This variable can now be referenced and used in other requests in Postman using the following variable format: {{session}}Related Articles:Technical Tip: Using FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer API

topics.title: LDAPS authentication fails due to an incorrect member-attr configuration
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to resolve an issue when users fail to authenticate via LDAPS because the member-attr is incorrectly set to tokenGroups, preventing the FortiGate from matching users to their assigned groups.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionUsers cannot authenticate via LDAPS even though the LDAP server returns a success response. The authentication fails during the group matching phase.The FortiGate is configured to use the tokenGroups attribute to retrieve group memberships. If the Active Directory environment does not populate this attribute or if it is not the correct attribute for the environment, the FortiGate finds zero values and skips group matching, resulting in an authentication failure for the user.Verify the issue via debug:Run the following commands to analyze the authentication process:diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug application fnbamd -1 diagnose debug enableIn the output, the following 2 lines show the attribute that FortiGate read and how many values it found:get_member_of_groups- attr='tokenGroups', found 0 values find_matched_usr_grps-Skipped group matchingattr='tokenGroups' - found 0 values: This indicates the FortiGate is looking for group memberships in the tokenGroups attribute but finding none.find_matched_usr_grps-Skipped group matching: This confirms that because no attributes were found, the user cannot be matched to any group.Correct the member-attr configuration:If tokenGroups is not required by the Active Directory configuration, revert the attribute to the default memberOf.Enter the CLI and navigate to the LDAP server configuration:config user ldap edit set member-attr "memberOf" next endVerify that the user group on the FortiGate references the correct LDAP server and that the LDAP group Distinguished Name (DN) matches the actual group in Active Directory.Additional LDAPS recommendations:When migrating from LDAP to LDAPS, ensure the following:The FortiGate has the appropriate CA certificate installed to validate the LDAP server certificate.The communication is configured over TCP port 636.Server Identity Check is enabled to ensure the certificate matches the configured LDAP server name or IP address.

topics.title: FortiManager 7.6.8 trying to install ssl-ssh-profile settings that are not supported on 2GB FortiGate devices
topics.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps for install failure in FortiManager 7.6.8 due to a "udp-not-quic" option under "config firewall ssl-ssh-profile" when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory.ScopeFortiManager. SolutionIn version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS 7.6.This behavior is due to known issue, with ID 1352524.Workaround: Set "udp-not-quic" to "block" in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Related document:Known issues

topics.title: Using FortiAnalyzer to detect activities related to the PHP2Shell RCE Vulnerabilities
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to use a custom event handler in FortiAnalyzer to raise alerts for incident response related to attacks that attempt to leverage the PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619). A report is also provided to gain historical visibility into the logs. Note that this article provides alpha files, which are automatically generated. The article will be continually updated as more information becomes available. Scope This article contains the files necessary to load an event handler and report into the FortiAnalyzer for either a Fabric ADOM or a FortiGate ADOM. The Fabric report and event handler leverage logs from other Fortinet products that can be used to detect the attack in addition to FortiGate logs. For more information about this attack, see the following FortiGuard Outbreak Alert: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities Solution What is included in Fortinet_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities.zip: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json: This event handler helps identify PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities detected by FortiGate and other Fortinet products. This event handler is configured for Fabric ADOMs. PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report.dat: This report displays the findings on PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities from FortiGate and other Fortinet products. It is configured for Fabric ADOMs. fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json: The event handler for FortiGate ADOMs is configured for FortiGate logs only. fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report.dat: The FortiGate ADOMs report includes only FortiGate charts. Detections included: Product Detection type ID FortiGate IPS signature (attack ID) 62657, 62658 FortiGate OT virtual patch 10009977, 10009978 FortiWeb Signature ID 1090502648 Steps: Download the Fortinet_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities.zip file (contains 4 files). Unzip Fortinet_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities.zip. Import PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json or fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_event-handler.json event handler: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may be of the Fabric or FortiGate type. Go to the Event Handlers module. Select the Import option under More. Select the appropriate event handler depending on the ADOM type. Result: The event handler is enabled and will be triggered if the appropriate logs are received following the import of the event handler. Edit the event handler to customize the notification section. Import PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report.dat or fgt_PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report.dat to Reports: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may be of the Fabric or FortiGate type. Go to the Report module. Select the Import option under More. Select the appropriate file for the ADOM type to add the report to the ADOM. Result: The PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities_report can be run anytime, as determined by an admin user.

topics.title: Manage Device Blueprints using JSON API
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to list, create, update, and delete FortiManager Device Blueprints using the JSON API, and how to use blueprints to add model devices and model HA clusters.ScopeFortiManager.SolutionDevice Blueprints define settings used when adding model devices, including the platform, firmware, device groups, policy package, and provisioning templates. Refer to Using device blueprints for model devices.Authentication uses the Creating administrators for the FortiManager API (Bearer token) against the /jsonrpc endpoint. List existing Device Blueprints:{ "id": 1, "method": "get", "verbose": 1, "params": { "url": "/pm/config/adom/{{ADOM}}/obj/fmg/device/blueprint" } ] }To retrieve a specific blueprint, append its name to the URL:/pm/config/adom/{{ADOM}}/obj/fmg/device/blueprint/ Create a Device Blueprint:Use the add method. The following example creates a blueprint named TEST_01 for the FortiGate-81F platform:{ "id": 2, "method": "add", "params": { "url": "/pm/config/adom/{{ADOM}}/obj/fmg/device/blueprint", "data": { "name": "TEST_01", "platform": "FortiGate-81F", "prefer-img-ver": " -b |8", "dev-group": "Group_01" ], "folder": "/", "prerun-cliprof": "prerun_temp" ], "pkg": "PP_Folder/package_01", "prov-type": "templates", "templates": "1__system_temp", "5__sdwan_tmp" ], "cliprofs": "hostname_temp" ], "auth-template": "test" ], "linked-to-model": "enable", "enforce-device-config": "enable", "ha-config": "enable", "ha-monitor": "a" ], "ha-password": " " ], "ha-hbdev": "b", "1" ], "split-switch-port": "disable", "vm-log-disk": "disable", "vdom-provision": "disable", "sdwan-management": "enable" } ] } ] }The referenced device groups, templates, and policy package must exist in the target ADOM. Remove any optional settings that are not required.Key fields:FieldNotesprefer-img-verReplace and with a valid firmware version and build for the selected platform. The '|8' suffix represents Let Device Download Image from FortiGuard.folder'/' is the default when device folders are not used.pkgPolicy package, including its folder path when applicable.prov-typeSet to templates for individual templates, or template-group when using a template group (then specify 'template-group': 'Tmp_Grp_Name' instead of the templates array).templatesProvisioning templates, identified by their type prefix and name.Refer: Technical Tip: How to create template group using JSON API.cliprofsCLI templates.auth-templateFabirc Authorization templatesha-hbdevArray of fheartbeat-interface, priority].Note: Blueprint fields vary by FortiManager version. Refer to this link, fmgr_fmg_device_blueprint – Fmg device blueprint, when adapting the example to another version.Update an existing Device Blueprint:Use the update method and specify the existing blueprint name. The following example changes the policy package and CLI template assignments:{ "id": 3, "method": "update", "params": r { "url": "/pm/config/adom/{{ADOM}}/obj/fmg/device/blueprint", "data": d { "name": " ", "pkg": "PP_Folder/package_02", "templates": a "1__system_temp" ], "cliprofs": r "hostname_temp" ] } ] } ] }Retrieve metadata variable information for a blueprint:{ "id": 4, "method": "get", "params": r { "url": "/pm/config/adom/{{ADOM}}/_blueprint/info/", "data": { "name": n " " ] } } ] } Delete a Blueprint:{ "id": 5, "method": "delete", "params": a { "url": "/pm/config/adom/{{ADOM}}/obj/fmg/device/blueprint/ " } ] }To add a model device or a model HA Cluster using a Blueprint via API, refer to: Technical Tip: How to add a model device to FortiManager using the API.Troubleshooting:The following commands can be used on the FortiManager CLI to debug the API calls:diagnose debug enable diagnose debug service sys 255 diagnose debug service main 255Other common issues are a platform mismatch between the blueprint and the serial number, or metadata variables required by the blueprint that were not supplied in meta variables.Postman API Collection for quick use: Blueprint. topics.title: Technical Tip: Extended support for v7.0 FIPS-CC Certified/CVE-Patched firmware
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article discusses the v7.0 specialty builds for FIPS-CC certification and the technical support period offered by Fortinet.ScopeFortiGate, FIPS-CC.Solutionv7.0 has passed its End of Engineering Support date (EoES) of 2024-03-30 and will soon be approaching End of Support (EoS) as of 2025-09-30. At the same time, Fortinet only has FIPS-CC Certified/CVE-Patched firmware available for v7.0, as work is still ongoing to have builds for v7.2 and v7.4 certified for FIPS-CC and FIPS 140-3 (see also: NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program - Modules In Process list). Important Updates:2025-10-10: Fortinet has released a candidate build for FortiOS v7.2 FIPS-CC and has made it available for download on the Fortinet Support site. The firmware may be found under the following firmware download section: /FortiGate/v7.00/7.2/FIPS-CC-Certification-Pending/7.2.8-FIPS-CC/FIPS-Candidate.2026-01-19: FortiOS v7.2 FIPS-CC has been certified and has been made available for download on the Fortinet Support site. available for download under section: /FortiGate/v7.00/7.2/FIPS-CC-Certified/7.2.8-FIPS-CC.2025-11-27: Fortinet has also released a candidate build for FortiOS v7.4 FIPS-CC and has made it available for download on the Fortinet Support site. The firmware may be found under the following firmware download section: /FortiGate/v7.00/7.2/FIPS-CC-Certification-Pending/7.4.4-FIPS-CC/FIPS-Candidate.Users currently running the latest FortiOS FIPS-CC v7.0 CVE-Patched build (FIPS-CC-70-21) can upgrade directly to the latest 7.2 FIPS-CC candidate build (FIPS-CC-72-5, at the time of this writing), with no additional upgrade path required.Users who want to upgrade to the latest v7.4 FIPS-CC candidate build should first upgrade from the latest v7.0 FIPS-CC CVE-Patched build to the latest v7.2 FIPS-CC candidate build, then upgrade once again from v7.2 FIPS-CC to v7.4 FIPS-CC.Please note that at the time of this writing, v7.4 has not completed full certification and is still pending final review by NIST. Fully review the ReadMe file in the firmware download folders before installing the firmware in production environments. The original article regarding FortiOS 7.0 FIPS-CC continues below: Fortinet is providing Extended Support specifically for the v7.0 FIPS-CC specialty firmware branch, which includes the original Certified firmware (FIPS-CC-70-6) as well as the subsequent CVE-Patched builds, such as FIPS-CC-70-21 and similar. The following are the key conditions for this Extended Support:Fortinet TAC will continue to offer technical support for clients using the FortiOS v7.0 FIPS-CC specialty firmware, but there will not be extended support for regular v7.0 GA firmware (in the GA case, administrators must upgrade their firmware to a supported release ahead of the EoS date).The Fortinet development team will be specifically providing vulnerability patch support for high- and critical-severity CVEs applicable to v7.0 FIPS for at least the next 12 months, but there will not be any extended support for non-CVE-related bug fixes.Regarding FortiGate Cloud and its enforcement of EoS dates for FortiGate firmware (see also: Requirements):For no-subscription clients, FortiGate Cloud waives the EoS enforcement for FortiGates running in FIPS-CC mode (both for GA firmware as well as the specialty FIPS-CC Certified/CVE-Patched firmware), so users of v7.0 FIPS-CC will retain the ability to integrate with FortiGate Cloud.For subscription clients, EoS enforcement is automatically waived (i.e., subscription users may use any firmware branch regardless of EoS date as long as it is still supported by FortiGate Cloud in general). For further inquiries on the matter, reach out to a regional Fortinet Sales Engineer or contacts within the Fortinet Account team. At the time of this writing, support will currently be extended beyond the v7.0 EoS date by at least 12 months (September 2026).Related article:Technical Tip: How to enable FIPS-CC mode

topics.title: LDAPS configuration erased after FortiManager upgrade
topics.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps for an issue where LDAPS configurations are erased after a FortiManager upgrade when a 'ca-cert' is not configured.ScopeFortiManager.DescriptionFortiManager currently permits omitting the 'ca-cert' field when configuring LDAPS.These LDAPS configurations, where LDAPS is configured but the 'ca-cert' field is not set, will be automatically deleted during the upgrade to FortiManager versions 7.4.12 GA and 7.6.8 GA.config system admin ldap edit "LDAP" set server "x.x.x.x" set cnid "sAMAccountName" set port 636 set dn "dc=fortinet,dc=lab" set type regular set username "fortinet" set password ENC XXX set secure ldaps set ca-cert "Fortinet_CA" nextWorkaround: Assign a temporary ca-cert before upgrading FortiManager to keep the configurations during the upgrade. Disable it if necessary once the FortiManager has been upgraded. Note: This behavior applies to RADIUS over TLS and TACACS+ configuration as well, where the 'ca-cert' field must be configured with a valid CA certificate. If no CA certificate is assigned, the corresponding remote authentication server configuration will be lost after upgrading FortiManager to version 7.4.12 or 7.6.8.

topics.title: IPsec VPN SAML SSO authentication with FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes troubleshooting steps for IPsec IKEv2 VPN connections that use SAML single sign-on with FortiGate as the service provider and FortiAuthenticator as the identity provider. It covers troubleshooting listener connectivity, HTTP 403 responses, SAML attributes, and EAP authentication failures. Optional Fortinet Single Sign-On checks are included for deployments that also collect Active Directory logon events.ScopeFortiGate running FortiOS 7.4.11, FortiAuthenticator 6.6.9, and FortiClient 7.4.7 on Windows. The reference lab also used Windows Server 2019 Active Directory and a Windows 10 domain client. Commands and menu paths refer to these versions. Hostnames, usernames, addresses, and object names below are examples.SolutionSymptomsThe lab troubleshooting included the following observations:IKE_SA_INIT and gateway validation completed, but EAP later timed out. The authentication exchange reached a username and candidate group before returning FNBAM_ERROR, with an empty EAP response.After ike-saml-server was configured on the incoming FortiGate interface, the TCP 11443 test succeeded and the FortiClient error changed from Network Error to 403 Forbidden.The second observation establishes progress to an HTTP response. It does not establish successful SAML authentication, completion of EAP, or an operational IPsec tunnel.SolutionIdentify the failing authentication stageFortiClient first reaches the FortiGate IKE SAML listener over HTTPS. The browser is redirected to FortiAuthenticator, which authenticates the user against the configured directory and returns a SAML response to FortiGate. FortiGate then completes the VPN authentication and IKEv2 negotiation. The browser path and the IPsec transport require separate checks.ConnectionPurposeFortiClient to FortiGate TCP 11443Example HTTPS listener for IPsec SAML authenticationClient browser to FortiAuthenticator HTTPSIdentity provider login and SAML exchangeFortiAuthenticator to Active DirectoryDirectory authentication and group lookupFortiClient to FortiGate UDP 500 and 4500IKEv2 and NAT traversal in the reference UDP deploymentVerify DNS reachability and certificates.Run the following PowerShell commands from the affected endpoint before connecting the VPN:Resolve-DnsName vpn.example.com Resolve-DnsName idp.example.com Test-NetConnection vpn.example.com -Port 11443 Test-NetConnection idp.example.com -Port 443Confirm that both names resolve to addresses reachable before VPN establishment.Verify the browser can reach the identity provider over HTTPS.Verify the FortiGate listener certificate covers vpn.example.com, and the FortiAuthenticator HTTPS certificate covers idp.example.com.The endpoint must trust their issuing certificate authorities.Check certificate validity and time synchronization on the endpoint, FortiGate, and FortiAuthenticator.The HTTPS server certificate and the SAML identity provider signing certificate serve different purposes. Verify both independently; a successful TCP connection does not validate either certificate.Verify the FortiGate IKE SAML listener.Review the listener port, interface binding, and authentication certificate:show full-configuration system global | grep auth-ike-saml-port show full-configuration system interface port1 show full-configuration user setting | grep auth-cert show user samlThe SAML object must already exist. If the listener or interface binding is missing, apply the relevant correction. The following example uses TCP 11443 and an existing local certificate:config system global set auth-ike-saml-port 11443 end config system interface edit "port1" set ike-saml-server "FAC-SAML" next end config user setting set auth-cert "Fortinet_Factory" endBind the SAML server to the interface receiving the FortiClient authentication request.Administrative HTTPS access on that interface is a separate service and does not replace the IKE SAML binding.Verify the FortiClient SSO port and the FortiGate service provider URLs also use 11443.If TcpTestSucceeded (Test-NetConnection result) remains False, check endpoint routing, upstream filtering, FortiGate local-in restrictions, and competing services on the selected port.Capture the request while repeating the connection test:diagnose sniffer packet any 'host and tcp port 11443' 4 0 lUse the client source address as observed by FortiGate, including any upstream NAT translation. Repeated SYN packets without a SYN-ACK require transport or listener investigation. A completed TCP handshake followed by an HTTP denial requires the SAML and web-service checks below.Isolate HTTP 403 response.Record the hostname and path that return a 403 Forbidden error. A response from the FortiGate endpoint and a response from FortiAuthenticator identify different processing points. Correlate the failed request with FortiGate SAML debugging and FortiAuthenticator authentication and web-service logs.On FortiAuthenticator, verify that the SAML identity provider service is enabled o
