topics.title: Rx Discards increase on access FortiSwitch uplink ports when fortilink-neighbor-detect is set to FortiLink
topics.summary: DescriptionThe Rx Discards counter increases on the uplink ports of an access FortiSwitch when the FortiGate FortiLink interface uses fortilink-neighbor-detect fortilink. Also, how to stop the increase by changing the setting to LLDP.ScopeFortiGate and FortiSwitch units managed over FortiLink, with fortilink-neighbor-detect set to FortiLink.SolutionSymptoms:The Rx Discards counter increases steadily on the uplink ports of the access FortiSwitch. These are the ports that connect to the distribution or core FortiSwitch.The Rx Discards counter does not increase on the access (downlink) ports.The uplink ports show no CRC, input, or output errors.The Rx Discards counter stops increasing after setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to LLDP on the FortiGate.Cause:When setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to FortiLink, the FortiGate and FortiSwitch units exchange proprietary FortiLink protocol frames over the FortiLink and ISL trunks. The access FortiSwitch receives these frames on its uplink ports, handles them itself instead of forwarding them, and adds them to the Rx Discards counter.When setting fortilink-neighbor-detect to LLDP, the FortiGate and FortiSwitch units use standard LLDP frames for neighbor detection. The FortiSwitch does not add these frames to the Rx Discards counter.Verification:On the FortiGate, check which neighbor detection method the FortiLink interface uses:show full system interface | grep neighborOn the access FortiSwitch, find the uplink trunk and its member ports:diagnose switch trunk summary show switch trunkOn the access FortiSwitch, reset the counters on each uplink port, wait a few minutes, and check the counters again:diagnose switch physical-ports set-counter-zero diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list Rx Discards: diagnose switch physical-ports list drops Rx Discards: drops set lldp-reception enable set lldp-transmission enable set fortilink-neighbor-detect lldp next endOn the access FortiSwitch, reset the counters on each uplink port and confirm that the Rx Discards counter either stops increasing or no longer increases at the same rate as before the change:diagnose switch physical-ports set-counter-zero diagnose switch physical-ports port-stats list diagnose switch physical-ports list Notes:The increase in the Rx Discards counter does not disrupt production traffic.Changing fortilink-neighbor-detect can briefly interrupt traffic, so plan the change for a maintenance window.Enable LLDP before you change the detection method. If changing the method without enabling LLDP, the managed FortiSwitch units go offline.A FortiLink interface based on a hardware switch does not offer the fortilink-neighbor-detect option.Related Article:Troubleshooting Tip: How to interpret RX drops on FortiSwitch devices

topics.title: Understanding and managing frequent HA audit log 0108035018
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.13, you may observe frequent event logs on a FortiGate High Availability (HA) cluster with log ID 0108035018.A sample log message appears as follows:date=2026-10-23 time=10:33:00 logid="0108035018" type="event" subtype="ha" level="information" vd="root" logdesc="HA secondary received CLI commands" user="FGT_ha_admin" ui="ha_daemon" msg="Received CMD from ip:169.254.0.1 vdom:vsys_ha type:1, msg_type:66"In FortiOS 7.4.13, security audit logging was added to record commands exchanged between HA cluster members across the internal heartbeat channel.Before FortiOS 7.4.13, these internal exchanges occurred silently. In FortiOS 7.4.13, each received command generates an informational event log.ScopeFortiOS 7.4.13.SolutionThese logs are purely informational. They do not cause packet loss, do not trigger failovers, and do not indicate a configuration defect.You can confirm that your cluster is healthy, or configure a log filter to exclude this message if you prefer not to retain it.Confirm HA Cluster SynchronizationTo verify that the cluster is healthy and in sync, run the following commands on the primary FortiGate:get system ha status diagnose sys ha statusVerify that both cluster members show an in-sync state and that the secondary node is reachable over all configured heartbeat interfaces.Filter the Log from Local Disk Storage (Optional)If your FortiGate has an onboard disk and you wish to stop recording this informational log to disk, configure a free-style exclusion filter in the CLI:config log disk filter config free-style edit 1 set category event set filter "(logid 0108035018)" set filter-type exclude next end endFilter the Log from FortiAnalyzer (Optional)If you send logs to FortiAnalyzer and wish to exclude this message, apply a free-style filter on the FortiGate:config log fortianalyzer filter config free-style edit 1 set category event set filter "(logid 0108035018)" set filter-type exclude next end end

topics.title: Metadata variables in CLI scripts use global or default values instead of mapped (per-device/VDOM) values
topics.summary: Description How metadata variables works in a CLI script. Scope FortiManager. Solution Metadata variables referenced inside CLI scripts in FortiManager do not resolve to a device‑specific mapped value when the script is executed on the Device Database. The script applies the value defined for the global context, or the default value if no global value is set — not the value mapped for a specific device or VDOM. Scenario A metadata variable is created with a default value and a per‑device mapped value (e.g. mapped for a root or named VDOM). If used inside a firewall object (e.g. an Address), the variable correctly resolves to the device's mapped value. The same variable used inside a CLI script run on the Device Database resolves to the global value — or the default value when no global value exists — instead of the per‑device/VDOM mapped value. This is an expected behavior. Metadata variables used in CLI scripts executed on the Device Database only support the global context or the default value. VDOM‑context (per‑device/VDOM) mapped values are not resolved within CLI scripts. Below a practical example. This is the metadata variable: FMG_Test # execute fmpolicy print-adom-object 179 3200 test_metadataDump object ttest_metadata] of category dfmg variable] in adom vTEST]:---------------config fmg variableedit "test_metadata"set value "1"config dynamic_mappingedit "Test_Firewall"-"global"set value "5"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"SDWAN"set value "12"nextedit "Test_Firewall"-"root"set value "9"nextendnextend Script: config vdomedit SDWANconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router static edit 1 set gateway 1.$(test_metadata).$(test_metadata).4 nextendend This script is run on the Device DB on Test_Firewall. Note that the "global" value was used. The values assigned to "root" or "SDWAN" were not used. View the log of script Test: running on device Test_Firewall (Test)-------Executing time: Thu Oct 22 15:33:07 2026-----------Starting log (Run on database)config vdomedit SDWANconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4nextendendconfig vdomedit rootconfig router staticedit 2set gateway 1.5.5.4 nextendendRunning script(Test) on DB success

topics.title: Prevent unnecessary FortiLink frames on FortiSwitch edge ports
topics.summary: DescriptionThe reasons why Managed FortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile may forward unnecessary FortiLink protocol frames (EtherType 0x88FF) to connected end devices. Devices that do not support or process these frames may discard them, resulting in rapidly increasing packet discard counters and unnecessary network traffic.ScopeFortiSwitch.SolutionFortiSwitch ports configured with the default-auto-isl LLDP profile by default.This profile supports automatic Inter-Switch Link (ISL) formation, allowing FortiSwitches to discover each other and establish inter-switch trunks.When this profile is applied to ports connected to end devices that do not require automatic ISL formation, FortiLink protocol frames with EtherType 0x88FF may reach those devices.The receiving devices may discard these frames because the EtherType is unsupported, causing unnecessary increases in packet discard counters.SolutionChange the LLDP profile on affected edge ports from default-auto-isl to default.Important: Do not apply this change indiscriminately to ports connected to other FortiSwitches that rely on automatic ISL formation.Configuration via FortiGate CLIIdentify the FortiSwitch and its connected edge ports.Verify that the ports do not require automatic ISL formation.Apply the following configuration:config switch-controller managed-switch edit config ports edit set lldp-profile "default" next end next endExpected resultUnnecessary FortiLink protocol frames are prevented from reaching connected devices on the affected ports, reducing avoidable frame discards and preventing servers from receiving a flood of unnecessary Ethernet frames.

topics.title: FortiAppSec Cookie Security causing HTTP 403 Forbidden errors
topics.summary: DescriptionEnabling the Set HttpOnly Cookie feature in FortiWeb Cloud may cause applications to return HTTP 403 Forbidden errors if the application relies on JavaScript to read CSRF tokens from cookies.ScopeFortiAppSec Cloud.SolutionSymptomsUsers encounter HTTP 403 Forbidden (Authentication Error) responses on various application pages after a successful login. These errors occur specifically when Cookie Security features are enabled in FortiWeb Cloud. No corresponding security violations or blocks appear in the Web Application Firewall (WAF) event logs, even when the policy is set to Alert mode.Root CauseThe issue is caused by the Set HttpOnly Cookie setting. When this feature is enabled, FortiWeb Cloud adds the HttpOnly flag to cookies passed to the browser. This flag prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie.If the application is designed to read a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token from a cookie using JavaScript, the browser cannot access the token. Consequently, the application receives a request with a missing or empty CSRF token and returns an HTTP 403 Access Denied response. Because this is an application-level authentication failure and not a WAF security block, no events are logged in the FortiWeb Cloud WAF logs.ResolutionDisable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option while maintaining other security settings.Log in to the FortiWeb Cloud console.Navigate to the Cookie Security settings for the affected policy.Disable the Set HttpOnly Cookie option.Keep the Set Secure Cookie option enabled if the application supports it.Save the configuration and test the application functionality.

topics.title: How to create a CLI script that runs automatically after every policy package or device settings installation on FortiManager
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to create a CLI script on FortiManager and configure it to run automatically on the FortiGate after every device install (policy package or device settings installation).ScopeFortiManager 7.x and 8.x.SolutionSome settings are changed or reverted by an install from FortiManager, or cannot be managed from the policy package or device database. A CLI script that runs directly on the FortiGate after each install can restore the required configuration without a manual step.For this, create a script with the target "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)", then enable "Automatic execute after each device install" in the script schedule.Step 1: Create the scriptGo to "Device Manager" -> Script.Select "Create New".Enter a name for the script (for example, "post-install-script").Set "Type" to "CLI Script".Set "Run script on" to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)".In "Script Detail", enter the CLI commands to run on the FortiGate. For example, for a FortiGate with VDOMs enabled:config vdom edit root config set end next endFor a FortiGate without VDOMs, enter the commands without the "config vdom" and "edit root" lines:config set endSelect "OK".Step 2: Run the script automatically after every installEnable the scheduled and automatic script options in the FortiManager CLI:config system admin setting set show_automatic_script enable set show_schedule_script enable endGo to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts".Right-click the CLI script and select "Schedule Script".Select the FortiGate devices that the script will run on.Select "Enable Automatic execute after each device install".Select "OK".Once enabled, the script runs on the selected FortiGate devices after each install, including every policy package installation and device settings installation. No manual step is needed.VerificationInstall a policy package or the device settings to one of the selected FortiGate devices.When the installation finishes, go to "Device Manager" -> "Scripts" and open the script execution history ("Script Log") to check that the script ran on the device.On the FortiGate CLI, check that the configuration was applied. For example:show full | grep Note:"Automatic execute after each device install" is only available when "Run script on" is set to "Remote FortiGate Directly (via CLI)". It cannot be used with scripts that target "Policy Package" or "ADOM Database".When "Automatic execute after each device install" is enabled, a time-based schedule (one time, daily, weekly, monthly) cannot be configured for the same script.A script that runs directly on the FortiGate triggers an automatic retrieve back to FortiManager. The policy package status may temporarily show "Unknown".The script runs after the install, so the change is applied on the FortiGate but does not become part of the policy package or the device database in FortiManager. The next install can overwrite it, which is why the script runs after every install.Related documents:Troubleshooting Tip: Useful workaround when FortiManager does not install configuration as expectedTechnical Tip: CLI Script behavior to run in FortiManager

topics.title: FortiManager Policy Package install fails with verification error due to "antiphish: max-body-len" parameter
topics.summary: Description An issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the " antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles. Scope FortiManager and FortiProxy 7.4.9 and higher, FortiProxy 7.6.1 and higher Solution When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification report install failed The same message may be reported for multiple webfilter profiles. The root cause is a difference in the default value of the max-body-len parameter between FortiProxy and FortiManager. Starting with FortiProxy 7.4.9 and 7.6.1, the default value of max-body-len was changed from 65535 to 1024 . However, FortiManager continues to use 65535 as the default value for this parameter. This difference in default values can result in installation verification failure in FortiManager. To work around the issue, configure FortiManager to use the optimal installation verification mode: config system dm set verify-install optimal end Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Technical Tip: Retrieve configuration file using GUI or CLI from a FortiManager
topics.summary: Description This article describes how the configuration file of a FortiGate can be retrieved by a FortiManager through the GUI or the CLI. Retrieving the configuration file using CLI can be used to gather more debug information if the retrieval process fails in the GUI. Scope FortiManager. Solution Via GUI: From: Device Manager -> Device & Group, as shown below: Select the managed FortiGate for which it is necessary to retrieve the configuration. Scroll down until the section: Configuration and Installation is visible; Click the button to the right of the Total Revision number called: Revision history. In the section that appears on the right, there is the Retrieve config button. Via CLI: Use the following debug to retrieve the OID of the device in question: diagnose dvm device list Once the OID value is known, the following command can be executed to retrieve the configuration file of the device in question: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf <----- OID value from the previous step. Sample Configuration: diagnose dvm device list --- There are currently 2 devices/vdoms managed --- TYPE OID SN HA IP NAME ADOM IPS FIRMWARE fmg/faz enabled 158 FGVM0X00000XXXX - 10.5.60.3 FGVM010000****** root 6.00741 (regular) 5.0 MR4 (7605) |- STATUS: db: not modified; conf: out of sync; cond: unknown; dm: autoupdated; conn: down |- vdom:[3]root flags:1 adom:root pkg:[imported]FGVM010000****** Where the OID will be 158 for the respective FortiGate: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf 158 Note: This operation is possible if the FGFM tunnel between the FortiGate and the FortiManager is up; otherwise, it will be necessary to perform troubleshooting as explained in Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot connectivity issues The following is an explanation of when it is useful to perform the Retrieve: FortiManager device settings and sync status Related articles: Technical Tip: How to fix synchronization issue in FortiManager Technical Tip: How to do bulk retrieve config in FortiManager using a script

topics.title: FortiNAC-F does not assign a VLAN via MAB to FortiAPs managed by a FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionReasons why FortiNAC-F answers MAB requests for FortiGate-managed FortiAPs with an Access-Accept that carries no VLAN, and how to fix it. The fix is one global setting: Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points, under System -> Settings -> Network Device.ScopeFortiNAC-F 7.6.x (validated on 7.6.7).FortiGate acting as wireless controller for FortiAPs, modeled in FortiNAC Network -> Inventory.FortiAPs connected to a third-party access switch (example: Aruba CX 6200) that uses FortiNAC as RADIUS server for MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB).SolutionSymptoms:The FortiAP's switch port stays in the static access VLAN instead of moving to the VLAN set in the Network Access Policy.The FortiAP appears under the FortiGate in Network -> Inventory as a Wireless Access Point.Searching the AP MAC in Users & Hosts -> Hosts returns nothing.Device Profiling Rules (for example Vendor OUI, type Wireless Access Point) never process the AP.Network Access Policies whose User/Host Profile matches the AP MAC never match.Deleting the AP from Inventory makes the policy work temporarily; the AP returns under the FortiGate at the next poll or reconnect.The RADIUS log shows an Access-Accept with no VLAN attributes (example values):[Access-Request] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ User-Name = aabbccddeeff, Service-Type = Call-Check, Calling-Station-Id = AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF, NAS-Identifier = ACCESS-SW-01, NAS-Port-Type = Ethernet, NAS-Port-Id = 1/1/2 ] [Access-Accept] AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF USER [aabbccddeeff] DEVICE [10.0.0.10] ATTRIBUTES [ REST-HTTP-Status-Code = 200, Cleartext-Password = "aabbccddeeff", Class = 0x..., Hint = "...", Tmp-String-1 = "request" ]The Access-Accept carries no Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Medium-Type or Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, so the switch keeps the port in its default VLAN.Cause:This is expected behavior. FortiNAC models FortiGate-managed FortiAPs as network devices (Inventory elements), not as hosts. When a Wireless Access Point connects to a managed switch port, FortiNAC changes the port type to WAP Uplink.By default, FortiNAC does not evaluate Network Access Policies for Wireless Access Points and does not enforce any policy on a WAP Uplink port. With no host record and no applicable policy, the MAB Access-Accept carries no VLAN.SolutionEnable Network Access Policy evaluation for Wireless Access Points. No other change is required when the Network Access Policy and port configuration are already in place.In the FortiNAC GUI, go to System -> Settings -> Network Device.Select Enable Network Access Policy for Wireless Access Points.Select Save Settings.Confirm the switch port where the FortiAP connects is a member of the Role-Based Access port group. This is required for the setting to take effect.Optional: Set Wireless Access Point Enforcement Group to a port group. FortiNAC adds a port to it when a Wireless Access Point connects; it does not remove the port automatically.Reconnect the FortiAP or bounce its switch port so a new MAB request is sent.Verification:The RADIUS Access-Accept for the AP MAC now includes Tunnel-Type = VLAN, Tunnel-Medium-Type = IEEE-802 and Tunnel-Private-Group-ID = the policy VLAN.Network -> Inventory -> switch -> Ports: The AP port shows the expected VLAN, and Port Changes records the change.Verify the VLAN assigned to the switch port interface.Notes:Deleting FortiAPs from Inventory is not a workaround; FortiNAC re-adds them under the FortiGate.The AP port must not be in the Authorized Access Points group, which prevents VLAN switching on the port.If the port is also in Reset Forced Default, set its Default VLAN equal to the policy VLAN to avoid the VLAN cycling between the two.Confirm RADIUS and VLAN switching are enabled in the switch Model Configuration, with a RADIUS attribute group that includes RFC VLAN attributes.Tunnel-mode SSIDs are preferred. topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains how to edit the FortiClient XML file to distinguish multiple IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using Network ID instead of Peer ID.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient.SolutionWhen multiple dial-up IPsec IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels are configured on FortiGate, a unique Network ID must be defined on each Phase 1 configuration. This allows FortiGate to correctly match incoming IKEv2 initiations with the appropriate tunnel.If the Network ID is not defined, FortiGate cannot reliably determine which Phase 1 configuration to use when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels reside on the same interface. This behavior differs from IKEv1, where Peer IDs were used to distinguish between tunnels. Use the following CLI syntax to define the Network ID for each Phase 1 configuration: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit " " set ike-version 2 set network-overlay enable set network-id next end The Network ID must be defined on both the FortiGate Phase1 and the FortiClient configuration to ensure correct tunnel matching.Note: The Network ID setting cannot be configured on unmanaged or standalone Forticlient. For managed Forticlient, configuration of Network ID is supported through Forticlient EMS starting with versions 7.2.6 and later or 7.4.1 and later.The FortiClient XML configuration file can be manually edited or provisioned via EMS with the Network ID attribute. Locate the section of the XML, and insert the tag as shown below.Note: Occasionally, this value is not included in the configuration. topics.title: Preserving client IP addresses across AP group VLANs with Layer 3 intra controller roaming
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to enable a new Layer 3 intra-controller roaming feature on a bridge-mode SSID, so wireless clients can move between FortiAP groups that are mapped to different VLANs, while retaining their original IP address.ScopeFortiGate 60F with FortiOS 7.4.11 and two FortiAP-441K access points with FortiAP firmware 7.6.3, managed by the same FortiGate.The source lab used feature-specific STS builds. The version labels above identify the tested release families and do not establish support in every build. Confirm that the target build exposes 'l3-intra-roaming' before applying this configuration.Solution1. Prepare the environmentUse two authorized FortiAPs managed by the same FortiGate and broadcasting the same bridge-mode SSID. Configure the SSID authentication before applying the following changes. The selected test used WPA2 Personal.Create two managed AP groups and assign one access point to each:FortiAPAP groupClient VLANManagement IPFAP1-loungeNorth10010.10.201.2FAP2-officeSouth20010.10.202.2Provide the required VLANs, DHCP scopes, gateways, and routing. Ensure the FortiAPs can communicate directly, without NAT in the path, when using direct roaming mode.Advertise the SSID on both access points. The tested 5 GHz channels were 140 and 132. Adjust transmit power to provide overlapping coverage and allow the client to select another access point when moving. Check the RF environment before starting the test.2. Map the AP groups to VLANs and enable intra-controller roamingOn the FortiGate, edit the existing SSID object. Replace with its configured name. The groups North and South must already exist and contain the corresponding access points.config wireless-controller vap edit " " set local-bridging enable set vlan-pooling wtp-group config vlan-pool edit 100 set wtp-group "North" next edit 200 set wtp-group "South" next end set l3-roaming enable set l3-intra-roaming enable set l3-roaming-mode direct next endThe key setting is 'set l3-intra-roaming enable' in the SSID configuration. The VLAN pool associates each participating AP group with its local client VLAN. Configure both groups; enabling the roaming setting alone does not replace this mapping.These changes modify an existing SSID, not a complete SSID creation script. Preserve the existing authentication and radio assignments. Review existing VLAN pool entries before applying the example.3. Validate IP preservationConnect a client to the SSID and record its IP address, associated FortiAP, and VLAN. Start a continuous connectivity test to a reachable destination. Move the client between the coverage areas, then return to the original access point.In the FortiGate wireless client monitor, compare the IP, FortiAP, FortiAP IP, and VLAN fields. The access point and local VLAN context should change while the client IP remains unchanged during the roaming test.Figure 1: iPhone test across FAP1-lounge (VLAN 100) and FAP2-office (VLAN 200). Both records show the client IP 10.10.200.3. Customer SSID labels are redacted.Figure 2: The iPhone is shown back on FAP2-office in VLAN 200 with the same IP, 10.10.200.3.Figure 3: Android test showing the same client IP, 10.10.100.2, across the two FortiAPs and VLAN contexts.Figure 4: Windows test showing client IP 10.10.200.4 across the same VLAN 100 and VLAN 200 roaming path. Customer SSID and personal device labels are redacted.The tested monitor sometimes retained duplicate client records after roaming. The paired rows show the observed IP and VLAN contexts; they do not prove simultaneous associations. Correlate the monitor with reassociation events and the client-side connectivity test.ResultThe selected local-lab test successfully validated roaming between North/VLAN 100 and South/VLAN 200 with iPhone, Android, and Windows clients retaining their original IP addresses. The report also records successful return to the original access point.IP preservation applies to the tested roaming sequence. It does not imply that a client keeps its address indefinitely after disconnecting or rehoming. The results do not establish zero packet loss or a universal roaming-time guarantee.

topics.title: Capturing Zebra ZS300 BLE data with FortiAP for temperature monitoring
topics.summary: DescriptionConfigure BLE scanning on a FortiAP to collect advertisements from Zebra ZS300 temperature sensors for processing and visualization by an external application.ScopeThe main proof of concept used a FortiGate 60F running FortiOS 7.4.12 and a FortiAP-233G running firmware 7.4.5. A separate local validation used a FortiAP-234F.The workflow illustrates BLE scanning on both models. Configuration availability depends on the FortiAP model and firmware.Solution1. Configure BLE scanningOn the FortiGate, create a BLE profile using the scan parameters validated during the proof of concept:config wireless-controller ble-profile edit "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" set ble-scanning enable set scan-type active set scan-threshold "-90" set scan-period 4000 set scan-time 1000 set scan-interval 50 set scan-window 50 next endAssign the BLE profile to the FortiAP profile. Replace with the existing profile name.config wireless-controller wtp-profile edit " " set ble-profile "ZEBRA-ZS300-BLE" next endIf the FortiAP profile is shared, this change affects the other access points using it.2. Verify the BLE configurationFrom the FortiAP CLI, run:cw_diag -c ble-configThe following excerpt shows the scan configuration observed during the main proof of concept:WTP Bluetooth Low Energy Configuration: ble scan report interval : 30 ble scanning : enabled (mode=active,thresh=-90,period=4000,time=1000,intv=50,wind=50)BLE scanning must be enabled. The iBeacon and Eddystone advertising settings also displayed by this command describe advertisements transmitted by the FortiAP and are not required to interpret the Zebra sensor data.3. Verify sensor receptionPlace the active sensor within BLE coverage and run:cw_diag -c ble-scanThe following output is transcribed from the local validation screenshot:BLE_DEV (001/001), mac ce:c3:25:fc:4e:a0 gen : 1 rssi : -88 addr type : random name : GEOMOV14587_LE manufacture : first seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 last seen : Mar 17 14:55:48 channel : 38 raw data : 22 0201020f0947454f 4d4f563134353837 5f4c45020a00Use the known sensor MAC address and its serial-number mapping in the sensor inventory to identify the intended device. Check the reception timestamps, RSSI, and raw data field.For devices using random BLE addresses, verify the identity mapping instead of assuming that the displayed address remains permanent.Figure 1: BLE configuration and scan output from the FortiAP-234F used for local validation. The main laboratory used a FortiAP-233G. The screenshot illustrates the scan workflow on another model; it does not independently demonstrate Zebra temperature decoding.4. Display temperature dataDuring the proof of concept, an external collector accessed the FortiAP over SSH through an IPsec VPN and retrieved BLE scan output every five seconds. The external application identified the Zebra sensor, processed the captured payload, and displayed temperature information in a dashboard.The FortiAP provided BLE scan data. The external application decoded the payload, stored historical data, and visualized it on a dashboard.Figure 2: Dashboard supplied as evidence of the proof of concept. The displayed period includes 12,044 events, an average RSSI of -78 dBm, an average battery level of 68.5%, and an average temperature of -19.01 °C. The dashboard also displays a mean kinetic temperature of -19.18 °C. These values are aggregated metrics, not individual instantaneous measurements.Note: Restrict SSH access to the authorized collector and protect its credentials. The five-second collection interval is independent of the BLE report interval shown by ble-config and does not guarantee a new temperature measurement on each query. Validate collection performance and the automation method before production deployment.

topics.title: RMA Information: Hardware failure and replacement with a spare unit on-site (support procedure)
topics.summary: Description This KB article describes, how to manage an RMA request (a hardware replacement request within the technical support contract) with the Fortinet Customer Service and Support (Fortinet CSS), when another (possibly temporary) spare unit is already available on-site. In case of a hardware failure on a Fortinet product and a need for replacement, when a spare unit is already available on-site (for example: a "cold spare" unit, or a temporarily loaned unit from a Fortinet reseller or distributor), for a smooth RMA exchange of the defective unit by the Fortinet CSS, Fortinet recommends to proceed as follows: 1. With the Fortinet CSS, create an RMA ticket first, using the serial number of the defective unit.2. In the RMA ticket, describe the problem with the defective unit, and make sure to mention to which spare/replacement unit (specify the serial number) the support contract will be transferred to.3. Once the RMA ticket has been created, request the Fortinet Customer Service (Fortinet CS) to transfer the support contract from the defective unit to the spare unit, possibly by creating another ticket (this time, a CS ticket), or making a phone call. Important step is to create an RMA ticket with Fortinet before transfering the support contract and all FortiGuard service subscriptions to the spare/replacement unit. Proceeding this way will prevent the defective unit to be considered as not covered by a valid support contract later on, resulting in an RMA refusal by Fortinet internal customer support systems. For more information on how to contact Fortinet CSS, please see our Contact Us page and refer to the Ticket Creation Guide, available for download on the Fortinet support portal (on the main Fortinet website, select Service & Support > Support Login > login with your credentials).

topics.title: How to fix "error firewall service custom protocol" after ADOM upgrade
topics.summary: Description A fix for the installation issue with multiple "firewall service custom" objects that may occur after an ADOM upgrade. Post vdom failed: error firewall service custom protocol- TCP_UDP_20101 TCP/UDP/SCTP:-999 - invalid value - prop[protocol]: option(TCP/UDP/SCTP) Copy objects for vdom Main_VDOM "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "certificate-inspection", id=18459, SKIP - (null) "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "deep-inspection", id=18474, SKIP - (null) Scope FortiManager. Solution When upgrading from FortiOS 7.4 to 7.6, the default protocol changes from TCP/UDP/SCTP to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP. To match this logic, a 7.6 ADOM should be used in FortiManager. However, it might appear that after upgrading the ADOM, "firewall service custom" objects fail to be installed. When drilling down to the object, it can be observed that the UUID of the object is set to ZERO, which is causing the issue during the installation: To resolve this problem and generate a correct UUID, it is possible to add the comment to the object, click the "Ok" button to update the object, and verify that a new UUID was generated. However, it may be challenging if it requires updating a bunch of such objects. To address this situation, use a script: Step 1: First, print a list of all objects to check how many have a ZERO UUID. execute fmpolic print-adom-object 167 +all Step 2: Take note of all affected objects and create a script. config firewall service custom edit "Jitsi_TCP_4443" unset uuid end Step 3: Run the script against the "Policy Package or ADOM DB". Step 4: Verify the object has a new, updated UUID and the installation runs without an error.

topics.title: Upgrade firmware fails with 'New image is too big'
topics.summary: Description This article describes troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error 'New image is too big '. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer. Solution Typically, this error occurs during a FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager 8.0.X firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image. This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: "New image is too big”. This known issue, tracked with the ID 1329518 in the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer Known Issues , is not a bug but a system requirement to upgrade the products to the newest and bigger firmware releases Most common causes: Insufficient flash disk space : The flash partition does not have enough free space to store the new firmware image during the upgrade process. Small virtual disk allocation : The VM was originally provisioned with a flash disk that is too small for the target firmware version. Diagnostic steps: Take the firmware update from version 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 for FortiAnalyzer VM as an example. Check flash disk usage: Run the following command on the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer CLI to view the flash disk size and current usage: diagnose system flash list Example output showing the flash disk status: ImageName Version TotalSize(KB) Used(KB) Use% BootImage RunningImage primary FLVM64-8.0-FW-build0105-260420 1006252 592344 59% Yes Yes If the Use% is high or the total size is too small for the target firmware, this confirms the issue. Resolution: Expand the flash disk (FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM). Take a config backup of the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer. Shut down the VM using the following CLI command: execute shutdown Delete all snapshots and wait for the operations to be completed. Important note : Without deleting existing snapshots, the disk expansion on the hypervisor side will not be reflected in the flash memory expansion of the FortiManager or FortiAnalyzer. Expand Disk 1 (or 0) by 4 GB or more in the hypervisor. Note: Do not expand the virtual disk too much, as the additional space will not be available for data. Boot up the VM and verify the flash disk was automatically extended: diagnose system flash list If the VM witnesses a file system error, run: diagnose system fsck harddisk Perform the firmware upgrade by manually uploading the firmware image and verify the error no longer appears. topics.title: FortiManager to FortiGate policy install fails with a custom protocol error
topics.summary: Description Troubleshooting steps for a custom protocol error that occurs when performing a policy installation to FortiGate. Scope FortiManager. Solution The following issue may be encountered by users when performing policy installation to FortiGate v7.6 to a v7.4 ADOM in FortiManager. This issue occurs because the protocol types defined in the default firewall service objects differ between ADOM versions. For example, in v7.4, the default protocol for the DNS service is TCP/UDP/SCTP , whereas in v7.6, it has been updated to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP . To resolve this issue, upgrade the ADOM to v7.6 so that the default firewall service object definitions in FortiManager align with those on the FortiGate. topics.title: Unable to delete a VDOM from FortiManager when its management VDOM is in a different ADOM
topics.summary: Description How to delete the VDOM using FortiManager when the management VDOM is not present in the same ADOM as the target VDOM. Scope FortiManager. Solution FortiManager enforces a device/VDOM model constraint that prevents deleting a VDOM while its management VDOM resides in a different ADOM. This article explains the constraint and provides two practical workarounds. FortiManager's ADOM (Administrative Domain) architecture determines how VDOMs are assigned and managed. In Normal Device Mode, all VDOMs from a single FortiGate must be placed in the same ADOM. In Advanced Device Mode, individual VDOMs from the same FortiGate can be assigned to separate ADOMs, enabling multi-tenant management. The deletion restriction occurs because FortiManager's device database tracks the management VDOM's ADOM assignment. When the management VDOM is in a different ADOM than the target VDOM, FortiManager cannot process the deletion through its normal device database operations. This is consistent with expected behavior where FortiManager displays errors when the management VDOM is not in the current ADOM for example, the error 'The management VDOM for device xxxxxx is not in the current advanced ADOM'. Workaround 1: Move the VDOM to the Same ADOM. Temporarily move the non-management VDOM so that both the management VDOM and the target VDOM reside in the same ADOM, then delete the VDOM. Workaround 2: Delete Directly on the FortiGate and Resync. Delete the VDOM directly on the FortiGate (bypassing FortiManager's ADOM restriction), then resynchronize the FortiGate on FortiManager. Verify the VDOM is removed from FortiManager's device database. Note : If the VDOM was created in FortiManager's device database but not properly saved, you may encounter an "Internal error" (code -20001) when attempting deletion. In such cases, run the following command on FortiManager to fix the database: diagnose cdb upgrade check resync-dev-vdoms This resyncs and removes any missing VDOMs from the device database.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCEP decryption failure with aes-256-cbc encryption
topics.summary: Description This article describes the cause of SCEP decryption failures on FortiAuthenticator when receiving enrollment requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc from certain third-party devices. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When a third-party device uses aes-256-cbc encryption for SCEP enrollment requests, FortiAuthenticator may fail to decrypt the PKCS#7 enveloped data. This results in a decryption failure during the SCEP process. Root cause: The issue is caused by a compatibility problem in how FortiAuthenticator handles SCEP requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc. While other encryption methods like des-ede3-cbc work correctly, requests using aes-256-cbc trigger a decryption error in the SCEP daemon. Symptoms: The following error messages appear in the FortiAuthenticator debug logs: PKCS7 message encrypted with aes-256-cbc (427) utils.cpp:386: decryption failed mo_pkcs7unwrap.cpp:526: cannot decrypt PKCS#7 enveloped data error:1C800064:Provider routines:ossl_cipher_unpadblock:bad decrypt Resolution: This is a known issue tracked under engineering ticket 1198353 and is expected to be resolved in an upcoming FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 GA release. topics.title: Technical Tip: Unable to receive authentication code via SMS
topics.summary: Description This article describes the procedure for sending an authentication code through SMS when the user reports that the authentication code message was not received. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If the SMS gateway message template is configured with the variable {{:token_code}} , but users receive a message without the OTP code, such as: "Your OTP login is . Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP." This indicates that the token code placeholder is not being substituted with the generated authentication code , resulting in a blank value in the SMS content. If the OTP code is missing when using the {{:token_code}} variable, modify the SMS gateway message template to: Your OTP login is {{:message}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. After updating the template, the authentication code will be included correctly in the SMS message delivered to the user. Configure the SMS gateway replacement message as shown below: Plain Text Your OTP login is {{:token_code}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines The {{:token_code}} placeholder will be replaced with the generated OTP, ensuring that users receive the authentication code in the SMS message. Modify the replacement message to {{:token_code}} . Navigate to System -> Administration -> Replacement messages . After changing the replacement message variable to {{:message}} , the authentication code is populated correctly in the SMS message. Example configuration: Plain Text Your OTP login is {{:message}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines Result: Plain Text Your OTP login is 123456. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines The {{:message}} variable is replaced with the generated OTP, allowing the user to receive the authentication code in the SMS message. When using the Test Settings option, the SMS message may be received as: Plain Text Your OTP login is FAC_FQDN. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. This behavior is expected because FortiAuthenticator does not generate an actual token code during the test. Instead, it sends a test message in which the {{:message}} variable is replaced with the FortiAuthenticator FQDN (FAC_FQDN) to verify SMS gateway connectivity and message delivery. Note : When using the Test Settings option, the test message will not contain an OTP code because FortiAuthenticator does not generate a token during the test process. As a result, the message will contain the test value instead of an actual authentication code. To verify OTP delivery with a generated token code, perform a real authentication request rather than using Test Settings .

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCIM user and group synchronization failure between FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate
topics.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve an issue where users and groups do not synchronize from FortiAuthenticator to FortiGate despite a successful TLS connection. Scope FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator. Solution When FortiAuthenticator acts as a SCIM client and FortiGate acts as a SCIM server, the synchronization of users and groups may fail if the base URL is configured incorrectly. Even if the TLS connection is established, the FortiGate SCIM daemon may fail to associate the incoming request with the configured SCIM client. The issue occurs when the base-url in the FortiGate SCIM configuration includes a port number. The base URI should typically consist of the protocol, domain name, and initial path. Including the port number in the base-url prevents the FortiGate from correctly identifying the SCIM client, resulting in the following debug error: diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application scim -1 diagnose debug enable url:https://10.5.146.127/scim/v2/Users/user_2 HTTP/1.1 used to find client:NULL. can't found client or client disabled. change state from wait_req to disconnect change state from disconnect to done change state from init to accepting change state from accepting to connect SSL_accept succeeded. Resolution Log in to the FortiGate command line interface. Verify the current SCIM configuration to check for a port number in the base-url: show user scim Remove the port number from the base-url. For example, change https://10.5.146.127:44559/scim/v2 to https://10.5.146.127/scim/v2: config user scim edit set base-url "https:// /scim/v2" next end Perform the user and group synchronization from FortiAuthenticator. topics.title: Technical Tip: Clarification of the 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in FSSO debug log when Entra ID is being used
topics.summary: Description This article clarifies the error log message 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in the FSSO debug log in the FortiAuthenticator when Entra ID is being used and remote LDAP is not configured. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution FortiAuthenticator FSSO supports logon events from native Microsoft Entra ID-joined workstations through the FortiClient SSOMA (FortiClient Single Sign-On Mobility Agent). For example, when an endpoint joined to Microsoft Entra ID connects to the network, FortiClient SSOMA sends the user identity and endpoint IP address to FortiAuthenticator. FortiAuthenticator then performs a group membership lookup against Microsoft Entra ID through the OAuth API and shares the retrieved Entra ID group membership information with the FortiGate. The configuration example can be found in the following document: FortiAuthenticator SSOMA for native Microsoft Entra ID joined workstation In a normal scenario, the following FSSO debug messages can be observed at 'https:// /debug/fsso-agent/' when FortiAuthenticator processes the SSOMA logon event and performs the Entra ID group membership lookup through the OAuth API: 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FortiClient connected: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268/192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Received 1 event(s) from FCT: 192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT LOGON 2026-02-10-10:50:23/1970-01-01-10:00:00 FortiClient (null):L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM/192.168.1.20 TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Exclusion List [DEBUG]: Looking up user JOHN.SMITH [3,-1] in exclusion table 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: SSOMA UUID: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268 EMS S/N: (null) EMS tenant ID: (null) 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: domain TESTDOMAIN.COM tenant ID 443EE9E8-11FF-4C82-9E41-39331045260A 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Logon Cache [DEBUG]: Allow newer FortiClient logon L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM:192.168.1.20 to overwrite existing older FortiClient logon L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM:192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Group Cache [DEBUG]: cache disabled for FortiClient logon, try to load user groups for TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: pending user TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH group lookup with tenant ID 442EE2E1-22FF-4C82-9E41-39321045460A 08/19/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT disconnected: 192.168.1.20 There could be a scenario following error log is observed when FortiAuthenticator is doing the group membership lookup in Entra ID: 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FortiClient connected: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268/192.168.1.20 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] Received 1 event(s) from FCT: 192.168.1.20 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FCT LOGON 2026-02-10-08:28:19/1970-01-01-10:00:00 FortiClient (null):L2003.TESTDOMAIN.COM/192.168.1.20 TESTDOMAIN.COM/JOHN.SMITH 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] Exclusion List [DEBUG]: Looking up user JOHN.SMITH [3,-1] in exclusion table 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: SSOMA UUID: 2250D4202FDD4FB125FD1B512DECD268 EMS S/N: (null) EMS tenant ID: (null) 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9DC456C0] FCT 192.168.1.20: cannot get DNS name of domain TESTDOMAIN.COM from Domain Manager 02/10/2026 08:28:20 [9D3E16C0] FCT session SSL connection established (172.11.0.80) The error 'cannot get DNS name of domain TESTDOMAIN.COM from Domain Manager' does not necessarily indicate a DNS resolution problem or an issue with the FortiAuthenticator Domain Manager itself. Instead, it is related to how FortiAuthenticator processes the incoming FSSO logon event received from FortiClient SSOMA. The general procedure is as follows: When FortiAuthenticator receives an SSOMA logon event from a native Microsoft Entra ID-joined endpoint, it requires the tenant ID provided by FortiClient SSOMA in order to perform the Microsoft Entra ID group membership lookup. In the working example above, the Tenant ID 443EE9E8-11FF-4C82-9E41-39331045260A was present, which can be found in the debug log. FortiAuthenticator can therefore associate the logon with the correct Microsoft Entra ID tenant and retrieve the user's group membership through OAuth. If the tenant ID is missing from the SSOMA logon event, FortiAuthenticator cannot identify the corresponding Entra ID tenant. It then falls back to processing the user as an on-premises Active Directory user. As part of this fallback process, FortiAuthenticator queries the Domain Manager for the corresponding domain and attempts to perform the group lookup through a configured remote LDAP server. If no matching remote LDAP server or domain is configured on FortiAuthenticator, the error 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' is generated. In this scenario, troubleshooting should focus on the FortiClient/SSOMA side to determine why the tenant ID is not included in the logon information sent to FortiAuthenticator. topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient VPN IKEv2 Token login not working when using EAP-MS-AUTH (mschapv2)
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue that occurs when attempting to log in with a user account that has a second factor assigned to it. Removing the token from the user lets the login succeed. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiClient, FortiGate with IPsec IKEv2 dial-up VPN and FortiToken 2FA. Solution A user with a token assigned to the user account fails to log in. At the time of failure, the FortiAuthenticator RADIUS debug log shows entries similar to the following: 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780491+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap: Peer sent packet with method EAP GTC (6) 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780499+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap: Calling submodule eap_gtc to process data 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780508+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap_gtc: # Executing group from file /usr/etc/raddb/sites-enabled/default 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780516+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) eap_gtc: Auth-Type FACAUTH { 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780524+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) facauth: This is a response to Access-Challenge 2026-09-01T17:07:40.780533+02:00 FortiAuthenticator radiusd[48048]: (2) facauth: ERROR: partial auth user not found A 'partial auth' user is a user who has passed the first factor (password) but has not yet completed the second factor (token code). The error means the token response arrived, but FortiAuthenticator no longer holds the authentication context from the first step. The authentication flow is as follows: FortiClient initiates an IKEv2 connection. IKEv2 requires EAP for user authentication, and FortiClient offers EAP-TTLS and EAP-MSCHAPv2. The user's password is validated successfully, and FortiAuthenticator sends an Access-Challenge requesting the token code. FortiClient returns the token code (EAP-GTC in the log above). FortiAuthenticator cannot match this response to the pending partial authentication, logs 'partial auth user not found', and rejects the request. This behavior is expected when FortiAuthenticator is not configured to allow 2FA for this type of EAP authentication. Note that FortiAuthenticator supports EAP-TTLS with 2FA as of version 8.0.4 and it is recommended to switch to EAP-TTLS when possible due to security considerations on EAP-MSCHAPv2. Enable the setting that allows two-factor authentication for IKEv2 EAP authentication from FortiClient, as described in the FortiAuthenticator Administration Guide under Policies . In short: Go to GUI -> Authentication -> RADIUS Service -> Policies and edit the policy matching the FortiGate RADIUS client. Go to 'Authentication factors' and expand the 'Advanced options'. Enable the setting 'Allow OTP for EAP-MSCHAPv2 Authentication with FortiClient'. Save the policy and test the VPN connection again. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving authentication errors for child domain users in FortiAuthenticator
topics.summary: Description This article describes a solution to the authentication error encountered by child domain users when logging in to VPN via FortiAuthenticator. The user may experience an error message indicating that the machine is protected by an authentication firewall and the specified account is not allowed to authenticate to the machine. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution After upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.5.6 to 6.6.9 , authentication failures may occur for users from a child domain. The following error is seen in the RADIUS logs: mschap: ERROR: Program returned code (1) and output 'Logon Failure: The machine you are logging onto is protected by an authentication firewall. The specified account is not allowed to authenticate to the machine. (0xc0000413)' To resolve the authentication issue for child domain users: Navigate to Authentication -> Remote Auth. Servers -> LDAP . Edit the configured Active Directory LDAP server. Under Windows Active Directory Domain Authentication , enable Allow Trusted Domain . Ensure that the FortiAuthenticator is joined to the Active Directory domain. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiAuthenticator HA secondary node failing to synchronize TACACS+ related tables
topics.summary: Description This article describes the issue of a FortiAuthenticator High Availability (HA) secondary node failing to synchronize TACACS+ related tables. The user may experience issues with TACACS+ clients, policy mapping, and policy-realm-group mappings not being synchronized between the primary and secondary nodes. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution In certain scenarios, the TACACS+ related database tables on the FortiAuthenticator HA secondary node fail to synchronize correctly with the primary node. To resolve the issue of a FortiAuthenticator HA secondary node failing to synchronize TACACS+ related tables, follow these steps: Navigate to System -> Dashboard -> HA Status on the load balancer node and select the Rebuild Tables button. This causes the load-balancing node to rebuild its database from information synced from the primary. If the tables appear to be in sync (same number of entries) but the status still shows out of sync, recalculate the cluster checksums by navigating to the debug page of the primary FortiAuthenticator at https:// /debug, then go to High Availability -> Loadbalancing HA Sync and select Recalculate LB-HA checksums . Verify that TACACS+ configuration references objects (e.g., remote servers, groups) that exist on the load-balancing node. If a TACACS+ policy references a remote LDAP server that is not present on the load-balancing node, this will result in an error. Check the FortiAuthenticator version and consider upgrading to the latest version if necessary, as there may be known issues with older versions. topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue where administrator role users are unable to authenticate after upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.6.2 to 6.6.10, while other users can log in successfully. The issue is related to CHAP authentication. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If an administrator-role user is unable to authenticate through SSL VPN after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10, recreate the affected user account in FortiAuthenticator and reassign the FortiToken. Perform the following steps: Delete the affected administrator user from FortiAuthenticator. Re-import the user from the configured LDAP server. Reassign the FortiToken to the newly imported user. Test SSL VPN authentication with the affected user. After completing these steps, the user should be able to authenticate successfully through SSL VPN. This procedure can be used as a workaround when only specific administrator-role users are affected following the FortiAuthenticator upgrade. topics.title: Technical Tip: How to fix BdsDxe : failed to load Boot0001 UEFI NUTANUX VDISK in Nutanix Environment
topics.summary: Description This article describes a failed deployment of a FortiAnalyzer instance when performing VM migrations from VMware (ESXi) to Nutanix. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution Error: Reason: Wrong boot mode selection: FortiAnalyzer firmware images have strict requirements regarding the hypervisor BIOS type. The boot disk is attached to the wrong bus: FortiAnalyzer images expect the virtual disk to be mapped correctly so the bootloader can initialize. Missing or unassigned secondary data: DiskFortiAnalyzer is a logging and reporting tool; it cannot function or boot correctly without a dedicated storage partition. Resolution: Change the boot mode in the Nutanix Environment: In the Nutanix Prism console, go to Update VM -> Boot Configuration -> Change the boot mode from UEFI to Legacy BIOS (or Default) . Cloned .qcow2 boot image disk: Clone the image and explicitly attach it to the SCSI bus (e.g., SCSI Index 0). Add a new disk to the instance: Create a second, empty disk on the SCSI bus (e.g., 100 GB+ depending on licensing requirements) alongside the primary boot disk.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Error 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' when trying to upgrade VM from firmware version 6.6.7
topics.summary: Description This article describes how the error 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' can occur on FortiAuthenticator VM when trying to update from firmware version 6.6.7, and how to resolve it. Scope FortiAuthenticator VM v6.6.7. Solution Under some circumstances, the error message 'Image validation failed: The current image model number is different from the appliance's.' may crop up when trying to upgrade a VM from firmware version 6.6.7. The error usually includes the detail '(current appliance model is FACVMS)'. After uploading the target firmware, FortiAuthenticator can show an error as depicted here: This occurs under the following conditions: The FortiAuthenticator VM is currently in firmware version 6.6.7 (either deployed or upgraded to it). A subscription license was uploaded to FortiAuthenticator VM. Subscription licenses can be identified by the serial number beginning with 'FACVMSxxxxxxxxx' and is visible in the dashboard. Subscription licenses are only meant to be activated on firmware version 8.0 and higher, but firmware version 6.6.7 allows subscription licenses to be applied in error (tracked under Engineering ID 1229991). This breaks the upgrade process, as the VM considers itself a different model and no longer accepts the proper model firmware images. Firmware version 6.6.8 and higher in the v6.6 branch do not allow uploading a subscription license in order to prevent this error. There are two options to solve this: If a different (non-subscription) VM license is available, that can be applied instead to override the subscription license. Once the non-subscription license is validated, the FortiAuthenticator VM allows upgrades again as expected, and the subscription license can be reapplied after upgrading to v8.0.x. Set up a new (unlicensed) VM, upgrade it to firmware version 8.0.x, and then apply the subscription license. This option means a loss of configuration. Switching to a different VM and restoring a configuration backup is not an option, as the VM license information is part of the configuration backup, and the error will persist through migrating the VM. This issue is most commonly observed in Azure VMs, as the marketplace templates start out in firmware version 6.6.7. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Incorrect VLAN assignment when using FortiAuthenticator dynamic VLANs
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot incorrect VLAN assignment when FortiAuthenticator is used to return dynamic VLAN attributes in RADIUS Access-Accept messages. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution Incorrect VLAN assignment may occur when FortiAuthenticator is configured for RADIUS Authentication if the same remote LDAP user or computer object is a member of more than one Active Directory or FortiAuthenticator user group, and when each group has a different RADIUS VLAN attribute configured. For example, if a user or device is a member of both the Students and the Staff group, then the FortiAuthenticator will return both VLANs to the NAC (e.g., FortiGate). Since the NAC (Network Enforcement Device, e.g. a FortiGate) can only assign 1 x VLAN, the latter of the two will be assigned to the client device, which may or may not be correct, possibly resulting in a Student being placed in the Staff VLAN (or vice versa). To troubleshoot this behaviour, check the RADIUS Access-Accept message in FortiAuthenticator's RADIUS debug (i.e. https:// /debug/radius) and confirm whether more than one VLAN is being returned. Correct example (1 x PVID is returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLAN Problem example (2 x PVIDs are returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLAN Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "64" Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Type += VLAN If more than one VLAN (referred to as Tunnel-Private-Group-ID) is returned, check the user's group membership (for example in Active Directory) and/or the Synced User Groups on the FortiAuthenticator itself (as it is possible to add user/devices by to multiple groups) and correct it such that the user is only a member of one group.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Error 'relation does not exist' when running a custom SQL dataset on FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to address the following error which may occur when executing a custom SQL dataset on FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist LINE 5: ...vname","csf","devgrps" ,ti6.epname AS epname FROM adom***_FG... Scope FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3. Solution The issue occurs when the SQL query generated for the custom dataset references a log table that is not available in the database. For example, the following command is used to execute the custom SQL dataset: execute sql-query-dataset ADOM test1 FGVM8VTM20123456 faz "2026-07-01 00:00:00" "2026-07-01 23:59:59" The command fails with: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist Command fail. Return code 1 To verify the SQL query generated by FortiAnalyzer, enable SQL query debugging: diagnose sql debug sqlqry dbgon diagnose sql debug sqlqry show The generated SQL query contains a reference to the following table: FROM adom***_FGT_wlog ti1 However, the database returns the following error: ERROR: relation "adom***_fgt_wlog" does not exist This confirms that the custom SQL dataset fails when the generated query attempts to access the referenced log table. After collecting the required debug information, disable SQL query debugging: diagnose sql debug sqlqry dbgoff Upgrade FortiAnalyzer to v7.6.7 or later. The issue is resolved after upgrading FortiAnalyzer from version v7.6.3 to v7.6.7. After completing the upgrade, execute the affected custom SQL dataset again and verify that it completes successfully. topics.title: Technical Tip: EAP-TLS Authentication Fails with error 'Authentication failed for EAP method type 13'
topics.summary: Description This article describes the steps to troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator. The user is experiencing issues with EAP authentication, resulting in an error message indicating that authentication failed for EAP method type 13 (EAP-TLS). This message is generic and returned by the client/supplicant whenever the TLS handshake or certificate validation fails during EAP-TLS negotiation. The actual reason must be identified from FortiAuthenticator debug logs, client-side logs, or packet captures. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution To troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Verify CA and certificate configuration Confirm that the CA certificate is correctly configured and has the appropriate Client Authentication or Server Authentication entries under its Key Usage / Extended Key Usage list. On the FortiGate CLI, run the following command to check the configured WiFi CA and server certificate: get system global | grep wifi This will show the 'wifi-ca-certificate' and 'wifi-certificate' currently in use, allowing to confirm the correct certificates are assigned. Check the certificate chain. Ensure that the Root CA and any Intermediate CA(s) that issued the client and/or server certificates are installed and trusted: On FortiAuthenticator: under Certificate Management -> Certificate Authorities -> Trusted CAs . On the client device: In the OS/device trusted root and intermediate certificate store. A missing intermediate CA is a common cause of TLS validation failure even when the leaf certificate is valid. Verify CRL/OCSP reachability: Verify that the client can reach the CRL/OCSP endpoints. If not required, consider disabling revocation checks for testing. Investigate logs and packet captures: Enable RADIUS debug logs on FortiAuthenticator and take a packet capture on the FortiGate/FortiAuthenticator during a reproduced failure, to identify the exact point of failure in the TLS/EAP exchange. Resolution : The issue was resolved by changing the fragmentation setting to pre-encap on the FortiGate. Large EAP-TLS certificate exchanges are fragmented across multiple RADIUS packets; incorrect fragmentation handling between the FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator can cause the TLS handshake to fail or time out, surfacing as a generic 'Authentication failed for EAP method type 13' error. To adjust this on the FortiGate, under the relevant EAP/802.1X or WiFi SSID configuration, change the fragmentation as shown below on the IPsec phase1 interface: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set ip-fragmentation pre-encapsulation next end Like E 1 Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClientEMS Upgrade Failure due to Grafana Package Error
topics.summary: Description This article describes a solution to an issue where the upgrade of FortiClientEMS fails due to a Grafana package error. The upgrade from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8 results in a failed upgrade. The error message observed: Setting up grafana (13.1.1) ... mv: cannot move '/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled' to '/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled': Directory not empty dpkg: error processing package grafana (--configure): installed grafana package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 Errors were encountered while processing: grafana dpkg configure failed. Aborting. Scope FortiClientEMS. Solution The EMS v7.4.8 upgrade includes a Grafana package update (to v13.1.1 in this case). During the package installation, the post-installation script attempts to move the bundled plugins directory from the package's default location (/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled) to the runtime data directory (/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled). The error Directory not empty means that /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled already existed and contained files when the mv command tried to move the new bundled plugins there. Note: This is a known issue with Grafana v13.1.1: Upgrade to Grafana 13.1.1 had errors . To resolve the EMS upgrade failure due to a Grafana package error, follow these steps: Run the command to rename the plugins-bundled directory. sudo mv /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled.bak Run the command to configure the packages. sudo dpkg --configure -a Retry the upgrade process to complete the installation of FortiClient/EMS version 7.4.8. By following these steps, the upgrade failure due to the Grafana package error should be resolved, and the FortiClientEMS upgrade should complete successfully. forticlientems Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Technical tip: Troubleshooting FortiClient EMS classification tag synchronization failures
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a classification tag sync failure. Scope FortiClient EMS. Solution In some cases, it may be necessary to use classification tags for endpoints in FortiClient EMS. After creation, it can be verified that some of the TAGs were not shared with the FortiGate. The main reasons for this could be: The Fabric connector configuration in FortiClient EMS does not have the classification tag sharing option configured: Therefore, review this configuration by navigating to Fabric & Connectors -> Fabric Devices to enable the Classification Tags tag type. The classification tag contains prohibited characters: Due to restrictions on the use of certain characters in FortiGate objects, an object will not be created on the FortiGate if, for example, a tag containing parentheses is created. This means the tag will not be synchronized to the FortiGate. If a classification tag contains disallowed characters, it will be necessary to delete and recreate the tag. Avoid using characters such as ' <>()#"'' , opting instead for '+', '-', or ' _' to ensure the tag is shared successfully. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting. It also explains the difference between NTP synchronization on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData Main Host and the Security Event Manager Controller, and why the controller may generate significantly more NTP requests than the Main Host. Scope FortiAnalyzer-BigData. Solution Starting from FortiAnalyzer-BigData v7.2.7 , the firmware upgrade process includes an NTP preflight validation. Accurate and consistent time synchronization is important for the distributed BigData cluster. If the configured NTP server cannot be successfully validated, the firmware upgrade is blocked. A typical symptom is that NTP synchronization on the Main Host appears healthy: diagnose system ntp status MS Name/IP address Stratum Poll Reach LastRx Last sample =============================================================================== ^* ntp-server.example.com 2 9 377 301 -92us[-123us] +/- 622us However, checking NTP from the Security Event Manager Controller may intermittently fail: fazbdadm check ntp ntpdate: rate limit response from server. ntpdate: no server suitable for synchronization found [ERR] NTP server ntp-server.example.com is not valid or not reachable Running the same command again may succeed: fazbdadm check ntp server , stratum 2, offset -0.000775, delay 0.02631 adjust time server offset -0.000775 sec NTP server ntp-server.example.com is valid~ This behavior can occur when the external NTP infrastructure applies rate limiting to the Security Event Manager Controller. Main Host and Controller NTP behavior: The Main Host and Security Event Manager Controller are separate components of FortiAnalyzer-BigData. The Main Host runs on Blade A1. The Security Event Manager consists of the remaining blades, with one blade acting as the Security Event Manager Controller (BD Controller). The NTP server configured under the following Main Host configuration is used by the BigData environment: config system ntp config ntpserver edit 1 set server "ntp-server.example.com" next end set status enable end The minpoll and maxpoll settings under config system ntp control the Main Host NTP client. They should not be used to determine the polling interval of the Security Event Manager Controller. The controller maintains its own NTP daemon configuration and uses the configured external NTP server address. Depending on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData version, the controller may use ntpd or chronyd . For example, the effective chrony configuration on a controller may contain: server ntp-server.example.com prefer minpoll 3 maxpoll 4 iburst The values are powers of two: minpoll 3 = 2^3 = 8 seconds maxpoll 4 = 2^4 = 16 seconds Therefore, the controller may poll the external NTP server considerably more frequently than the Main Host. The iburst option can additionally send several NTP queries in a short period when establishing synchronization. Why rate limiting can cause a large number of requests: When the NTP server applies rate limiting, the controller may not receive the responses required to successfully synchronize or validate the server. This can result in additional synchronization attempts and retry behavior: Controller sends NTP queries -> NTP server rate-limits the requests -> NTP operation fails -> Additional synchronization/retry attempts -> More NTP requests. Consequently, rate limiting can have the opposite of the intended effect: instead of reducing the overall traffic, failed synchronization attempts can result in additional requests. For example, in one environment, approximately 59,000 NTP requests in 24 hours were observed from the Security Event Manager Controller, while only a few hundred requests were observed from the Main Host. The high request count was associated with NTP server rate limiting and subsequent retry behavior. Checking NTP on the Security Event Manager Controller: The following command actively validates the configured NTP server: fazbdadm check ntp Depending on the NTP implementation, the check uses an active query such as ' ntpdate -q' or the equivalent chrony query. Active validation can generate a short burst of requests and is more sensitive to server-side rate limiting than normal background synchronization. Avoid running this command repeatedly when investigating an NTP rate-limit issue, as each execution generates additional NTP traffic. For local NTP daemon health, the following internal diagnostic command can be used: fazbdadm check ntp-health This command checks the local host NTP health state. If NTP is healthy, the command returns no output. If NTP is unhealthy, an error similar to the following is returned: Chrony server status is not healthy: This command is useful when troubleshooting because it checks the local NTP daemon health without repeatedly performing the same active external NTP validation. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient EMS SAML Authentication Failure when FortiClient shows a 'Server encountered an error, please try again later' message
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot SAML authentication issues in FortiClient EMS when FortiClient shows a ' Server encountered an error, please try again later ' message during user authentication. In this scenario, users are unable to register FortiClient with FortiClient EMS using an invitation code because the SAML authentication process fails. Scope FortiClient EMS. FortiGate. Solution If users encounter a server error when authenticating with SAML, perform the following checks: In FortiClient EMS , navigate to User Management -> SAML Configuration and edit the affected SAML profile. Verify the Service Provider (SP) certificate configured in the SAML profile. Ensure the certificate is a server certificate . Do not use a wildcard certificate, as it may prevent the SAML signing key from loading correctly. If necessary, temporarily remove the configured SP certificate and test the authentication again to determine whether the certificate is the source of the issue. Review the FortiClient EMS diagnostic logs for SAML-related errors. In particular, examine the following FortiClient EMS log file: python_logs/debug_ - - A common indication of this issue is the following error: xmlsec.Error: (1, 'cannot load key') This error typically indicates that FortiClient EMS is unable to load the private key associated with the configured SP certificate. After correcting the certificate configuration, retry the FortiClient registration using the invitation code. For additional information about configuring SAML authentication, refer to SAML Configuration .
