topics.title: Technical Tip: Resolving an upgrade failed error during FortiClient EMS update caused by the Microsoft SQL Server Express database reaching size limit
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve the Setup Failed error 0x80070643 during a FortiClient EMS v7.2 upgrade. Scope FortiClient EMS v7.2 On-Premises using Microsoft SQL. Solution During the upgrade from FortiClient EMS v7.2.12 to v7.2.13 or v7.2.14, the installer may fail with the error Setup Failed and code 0x80070643. In the installer logs, the following SQL error may be observed: Could not allocate a new page for database 'FCM_default' because the 'PRIMARY' filegroup is full due to lack of storage space or database files reaching the maximum allowed size. This behavior is consistent with the Microsoft SQL Server Express database reaching its 10 GB size limit. To validate the database size, check the .mdf files in the following path: C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL12.FCEMS\MSSQL\DATA\ Before applying any change, create an EMS backup from EMS -> Dashboard -> Backup . If EMS is running on a virtual machine, create a VM snapshot as well. Stop all FortiClient EMS services from the Windows Services console. These services are usually listed as 'FCEMS_xxxx'. Open cmd.exe as Administrator and connect to the EMS database: sqlcmd -E -S.\fcems -d fcm_Default Delete historical EMS events: 1> truncate table events 2> go 1> exit Execute the database shrink operation: sqlcmd -E -S.\fcems -d fcm_Default 1> DBCC SHRINKDATABASE(fcm_Default,10) 2> go 1> exit The database name may vary between deployments. Validate whether the database is named fcm_Default, fcm_default, or fcm_root, and adjust the command accordingly. Restart the FortiClient EMS services and run the upgrade again. The EMS log retention setting removes records older than the configured retention period, but it does not necessarily reduce the physical size of the SQL Server .mdf file. For this reason, the database file may remain close to the SQL Server Express 10 GB limit even after old records are removed. As a preventive measure, monitor the EMS database size periodically, keep regular EMS backups, and consider migrating to Microsoft SQL Server Standard or Enterprise if the EMS database continues growing near the SQL Server Express limit. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to view Outbreak Alerts in FortiAnalyzer
topics.summary: Description This article describes troubleshooting steps for situations where Outbreak Alerts are not displayed or cannot be viewed in FortiAnalyzer. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution Navigate to FortiAnalyzer -> Incidents & Alerts -> FortiGuard Services -> Outbreak Alerts . If the Outbreak Alerts pane is not displaying alerts or cannot be accessed, continue with the troubleshooting steps below: Verify the Outbreak Detection Service license. Ensure that the Outbreak Detection Service license is active under Dashboard -> Status -> License Information. Verify FortiGuard license synchronization. If the Outbreak Detection Service license is not active, verify that FortiAnalyzer can communicate with FortiGuard and that the license information has been updated. Refer to Technical Tip: License does not reflect in FortiAnalyzer/FortiManager . For air-gapped environments or if FortiAnalyzer is using FortiManager as a FortiGuard server, refer to Technical Tip: Configure FortiAnalyzer/FortiManager to use FortiManager as a FortiGuard server in an air-gapped network . Verify the FortiGuard connector status. Confirm that the FortiGuard connector is active under Incidents & Alerts -> Automation -> Active Connectors . Verify connectivity to the FortiGuard API/FortiGuard connector. If the FortiGuard connector is not active, verify DNS resolution and network connectivity to the FortiGuard API server. Run the following CLI command: execute ping productapi.fortinet.com If FortiAnalyzer is deployed behind a proxy, configure the proxy and ensure that outbound HTTPS access to ' productapi.fortinet.com ' over TCP port 443 is permitted. For proxy configuration in FortiAnalyzer, refer to Enabling updates through a web proxy . Verify HTTPS connectivity. Ensure that FortiAnalyzer can establish an HTTPS connection to ' productapi.fortinet.com ' over TCP port 443. Successful communication with this server is required for the FortiGuard connector to function correctly and for Outbreak Alerts to be generated. Note: In a fully air-gapped environment with no Internet access and no proxy connectivity to ' productapi.fortinet.com ', the Outbreak Alerts feature is not supported, as it depends on communication with the FortiGuard Cloud service. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClientEMS troubleshooting tool for addressing IP/MAC filtering issues
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to use the FortiClientEMS troubleshooting tool to collect diagnostic logs when addressing IP/MAC filtering issues. In addition, it explains and walks through the most relevant logs for common IP/MAC access failure use cases. Scope FortiClientEMS v7.4.5+, FortiGate v7.6.4+, FortiClient. ZTNA. Solution This article focuses on live debug log collection due to its superior effectiveness and level of detail compared to historical log collection. Note the requirements for versions of FortiClientEMS (v7.4.5+), FortiGate (v7.6.4+), and FortiClient (macOS v7.4.4+, Linux v7.4.5+). The scenario that this article will focus on is a user attempting to access an internal resource over a VPN tunnel with ZTNA Posture Tag installed on a firewall policy (IP/MAC Filtering). Example of the policy below: The live troubleshooting tool will collect diagnostics from FortiClient, FortiClientEMS, and FortiGate CLI. It is best to have Debug log level enabled on both FortiClient and FortiClientEMS before running the tool. The troubleshooting workflow: Add FortiGate acting as a VPN gateway, and FortiClient having access issues over VPN. Reproduce the issue by connecting FortiClient to the VPN tunnel and attempting to access the resource in question. Wait for 1-2 extra upload intervals to make sure all the required logs have been collected and uploaded. The next section will discuss the most relevant logs the troubleshooting tool collects when it comes to IP/MAC filtering. FortiClientEMS Troubleshooting tool log reference. FortiClient: The tool executes and uploads FortiClient diagnostics, which is the most complete troubleshooting package one can collect. Make sure the log level was set to Debug prior to running the tool for more detailed troubleshooting data. FortiClientEMS: The tool collects server-side diagnostics, which may include logs revealing details like posture tag exchange between FortiClientEMS and FortiGate. FortiGate: The tool runs multiple FortiOS CLI commands related to Zero Trust tags as well as communication between FortiGate and FortiClientEMS. The troubleshooting tool executes multiple CLI commands on FortiGate the most interesting of which are presented below: diagnose firewall dynamic list diagnose debug application fcnacd -1 diagnose endpoint filter show-large-data yes Here: diagnose firewall dynamic list - shows 'posture tag - IP' mappings; FortiGate updates FortiClientEMS with FortiClient's VPN IP-address and, in return, receives a list of posture tags the endpoint is matched with. diagnose debug application fcnacd -1 - live diagnostics capturing posture tag data exchange between FortiGate and FortiClientEMS. diagnose endpoint filter show-large-data yes - used as a supplement for the above command and enables better readability of the output (unzips text with tag information). Reading FortiGate diagnostic output. Typically, FortiClient and FortiClientEMS are easier to troubleshoot when it comes to issues with endpoint matching a posture tag. Refer to Troubleshooting Tip: Troubleshooting of common posture tagging rules in FortiClient EMS . The most complex issues usually 'hide' themselves within the FortiGate CLI output. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiAnalyzer license update issue
topics.summary: Description This article describes a troubleshooting process for resolving a FortiAnalyzer license update issue where the license has been renewed, but the GUI still does not reflect the update. The user may encounter this issue when the FortiAnalyzer device is unable to connect to the FortiGuard server. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution To resolve the FortiAnalyzer license update issue, perform the following checks: Verify internet connectivity. Confirm that the FortiAnalyzer has internet access by testing connectivity to a public DNS server (for example, 8.8.8.8). Verify DNS resolution of the FortiGuard FQDN: Run the following command: execute ping usfds1.fortinet.com Check the output. If the output is: ping: bad address 'usfds1.fortinet.com' This indicates that FortiAnalyzer is unable to resolve the FortiGuard FQDN, which is most likely a DNS-related issue. Configure a reachable DNS server. Try using a public DNS server and run the command below again: execute ping usfds1.fortinet.com Collect FDS debug logs. If the issue persists and the same error is returned, collect FDS debug logs using: diagnose fmupdate view-linkd-log fds Review the debug output. If the logs contain entries similar to the following: 2026/06/10_11:20:52.562 info fds_svrd[15660]: __evlog_conn_status,1164: svc=FGT, addr=usfds1.fortinet.com, status=-1(failed), failed_reason=0(), svrnode=addr:usfds1.fortinet.com, port:443, tz:7, distance:0, src:DEFAULT, now-g_conn_time=1202, report server connect failed info2026/06/10_11:30:53.642 info fds_svrd[15660]: Start fds client session to 'usfds1.fortinet.com:443', task=SELPOLL svc=FGT2026/06/10_11:30:53.650 info fds_svrd[15660]: Check update(SELPOLL) with [FGT] fds usfds1.fortinet.com FAIL This indicates that FortiAnalyzer is attempting to reach the Fortinet licensing servers via usfds1.fortinet.com over HTTPS (TCP port 443), but the connection is failing. Verify firewall or proxy policies. Ensure that any firewall or proxy located between FortiAnalyzer and the internet allows outbound access on TCP port 443 and that the following FQDNs are whitelisted: fds1.fortinet.com usfds1.fortinet.com Once connectivity to these FortiGuard servers is established, the license information should be updated successfully. topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiGate unable to sending log to FortiAnalyzer when FIPS-CC enable
topics.summary: Description This article describes the case where, when FIPS-CC mode is enabled on the FortiGate, the device is unable to send logs to FortiAnalyzer. Scope FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate, FIPS-CC. Solution When FortiGate enables FIPS-CC mode, the OFTP is unable to establish. From FortiGate, the connection status is UP. While from FortiAnalyzer, there is no authorized device pop-up notification. The packet capture showed that the FortiGate reset the connection. To successfully send logs from a FIPS-CC-enabled FortiGate to FortiAnalyzer using OFTP, both devices must use custom certificates signed by the same Certificate Authority (CA). config system certificate oftp set mode custom set certificate set private key end However, there is another option that can be done from FortiAnalyzer, which is to enable the FIPS-CC mode. To enable the FIPS-CC mode: config system fips set status enable set entropy-token enable end Enabling the FIPS-CC mode would delete all the config and logs; the command must be run at the console. Once the FIPS-CC has been enabled from the FortiAnalyzer side, the new FortiGate needs to be authorized to enable the FIPS-CC mode. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Maps not loading in FortiAnalyzer GUI and returning 'Internal Server Error'
topics.summary: Description This article describes a possible reason for the Google Maps frames in FortiAnalyzer not loading and instead returning 'Internal Server Error'. The example below is from Device Manager, but the same can occur in FortiView and other pages using Google Maps overlays. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution As mentioned in the article Technical Tip: How to resolve map server connectivity issue , FortiAnalyzer requires access to mapserver.fortinet.com . To allow the communication, the map server requires the FortiAnalyzer to present a Fortinet-issued embedded certificate, having a CN value matching the FortiAnalyzer Serial Number. If the correct certificate is not provided, even though the connection to the server is successful, FortiAnalyzer would fail to download the Google API information, as visible from the last message in the debug snippet below: FAZVM64 # diagnose system mapserver test * Trying 208.91.114.183:443... * Connected to mapserver.fortinet.com (208.91.114.183) port 443 * ALPN: curl offers http/1.1 * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1): * CAfile: /etc/cert/ca.crt * CApath: /etc/cert/ca * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2): * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Encrypted Extensions (8): * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Request CERT (13): * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11): * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, CERT verify (15): * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (20): * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS change cipher, Change cipher spec (1): * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Certificate (11): * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, CERT verify (15): * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Finished (20): * SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 * ALPN: server accepted http/1.1 * Server certificate: * subject: C=US; ST=California; L=Sunnyvale; O=Fortinet; OU=FortiManager; CN=mapserver.fortinet.com; emailAddress=support@fortinet.com * start date: Jan 23 21:56:50 2026 GMT * expire date: Feb 14 21:56:50 2027 GMT * issuer: C=US; ST=California; L=Sunnyvale; O=Fortinet; OU=Certificate Authority; CN=fortinet-subca2001; emailAddress=support@fortinet.com * SSL certificate verify ok. * using HTTP/1.1 > Send 91 bytes * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Newsession Ticket (4): * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Newsession Ticket (4): * old SSL session ID is stale, removing Certificates and check the details of the local Fortinet certificates. Virtual machines originally deployed before 2019, and still using the original license file, may have certificates with CN=FAZ-VM0000000001 or CN=FAZ-VM0000000000 In such a case, the solution is to download the new license file from the support portal ( Support ) and reapply it on the unit under Dashboard -> License Information widget > VM License -> Upload License button . This will cause the VM to reboot, and the issue should be resolved after that. FortiAnalyzer hardware: Hardware models of the D-series and older, and the first revisions of some E-series models, may display correct local certificates under System Settings -> Certificates , but in fact use a hardware-level certificate with CN=FortiAnalyzer when communicating with the map servers. There is currently no solution in this case. Contact the Fortinet Technical Support if further information or assistance is required. topics.title: Technical Tip: Configure event handlers for failed login attempts on FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer devices
topics.summary: Description This article describes the steps to configure event handlers for failed login attempts on FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer devices. Scope FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate. Solution There are situations where it is needed to receive a notification when the admin user for FortiGate access or FortiAnalyzer access fails the credentials after several attempts. This could be considered a risk or be under brute force attack. In order to have visibility in versions from v7.6.2, 2 event handlers help to detect failure attempts to log in FortiGate devices and FortiAnalyzer access. To configure these event handlers for failed login attempts, the administrator can enable them in the following path: Incident & events -> Event Handlers -> Enable handlers called 'Default-Brute-Force-Account-Login-Attack-FAZ' & 'Default-Brute-Force-Account-Login-Attack-FGT'. In case it would also be needed to receive a notification via email. It could be configured as an SMTP server profile ( Technical Tip: How to set up Email Notifications with notification.fortinet.net) in FortiAnalyzer and then linked to a Notification profile ( Technical Tip: How to configure a handler to send an email for each triggered event) for these event handlers. By default, in event handlers, the trigger is when there are 5 or more failed logging attempts in 1 day. In case it is needed to customize the number and time period, the administrator can clone ( select the right button to display options ) the handlers and set the values needed by editing the rules in the cloned handler. After customizing the handlers and enabling them, each time the conditions are triggered, an event will be created, and in case a notification profile was linked, the e-mail will also be received.

topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient EMS cannot generate a digitally self-signed FortiClient exe installer
topics.summary: Description This article describes why FortiClient EMS cannot generate a digitally self-signed FortiClient exe installer. Scope FortiClient EMS v7.4 onwards Solution When the end user manually runs a FortiClient exe installer in an attempt to upgrade FortiClient version, Windows Microsoft Defender SmartScreen will pop-up below message: The user will have to select 'Run anyway ' to upgrade FortiClient. Below is the reason why FortiClient EMS can never self-sign a FortiClient exe installer: Private key security risk. The signing certificate private key must be stored on the FortiClient EMS server. In the event where the server itself is compromised, the bad actor will be able to obtain the software's private key and use it to sign their malware as 'trusted and made by Fortinet'. To avoid this pop-up message from appearing, it is possible to upload the company's own digital certificate to sign the FortiClient EMS-packaged FortiClient exe installer. Go to System Settings -> EMS Settings -> Sign Software Packages -> toggle ON. Input the timestamp server FQDN or IP, upload the Certificate -> Save . For the existing FortiClient installer, edit the installer in any way to repackage it. The repackaged installer will be signed by the certificate uploaded in step 3. When creating a new FortiClient installer, it will be signed by the certificate, too. Configured days in retention policy: To resolve the issue of incorrect log retention days on the FortiAnalyzer, follow these steps: Go to System Settings -> ADOMs -> View Storage Info to check the current log retention settings. Check the logview -> logs -> Logbrowse section to see if there are any logs that are older than the configured retention period. Use the logbrowse feature to filter logs by date and identify any logs that are causing the incorrect retention days to be displayed. If it is necessary to see the exact value of the 365 days retention in the GUI, download the files to have a backup of them and then delete the logs that are older than the configured retention period to ensure that the FortiAnalyzer is only retaining logs for the correct amount of time. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Recovering access to FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM on Microsoft Hyper‑V when the admin password is lost
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to recover access to a FortiManager or FortiAnalyzer virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V when the admin password is lost, and no configuration backup is available. Scope FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer VMs running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Solution Preparation and important notes. Any action taken upon the information in this article is strictly at personal risk. This procedure is intended for environments without VM snapshots to avoid data corruption. Always back up existing VHD/VHDX files before making changes. Use the same firmware version as currently running on the VM to prevent compatibility issues. System disk replacement procedure. Prepare the Replacement system disk. Go to the Fortinet Support Portal: Support portal . Download the Hyper-V firmware package matching the current version: FortiAnalyzer: FAZ_VM64_HV-v -build -FORTINET.out.hyperv.zip . FortiManager: FMG_VM64_HV-v -build -FORTINET.out.hyperv.zip . Extract the downloaded file. Locate the system disk file: FAZ.vhd or FMG.vhd. Rename the file to either of the following: faz2.vhd or fmg2.vhd. Replace the System Disk in Hyper-V. Shut down the VM in Hyper-V Manager. Open VM Settings . Navigate to IDE Controller (Primary) . Identify the system disk (faz.vhd or fmg.vhd). Remove the system disk attachment. Do not delete the actual file from storage. Attach the new disk: Select Add Hard Drive . Choose Use existing virtual hard disk . Select faz2.vhd or fmg2.vhd. Ensure: The data disk (DATADRIVE.vhd) remains attached. No changes are made to the data disk. Apply settings and start the VM . System reconfiguration after boot. After the VM starts: Access the console via Hyper-V: 'Right-click' the VM and Connect . Log in: Username: Admin. Password: (Leave blank). Reconfigure: Network settings (IP, Gateway, DNS). Hostname and interfaces. Reapply: VM license. Verify: GUI access. Logs and ADOMs are intact. Error handling. Error: 'There is no Operating System.' This indicates a disk or boot order issue. Resolution: Ensure the new disk is attached as the primary system disk (IDE 0:0). If unresolved: Deploy a new VM using the correct Hyper-V image. Attach the original data disk as secondary. Optional: Configuration migration. If a configuration backup exists, use the following command: execute migrate all-settings : Before running the migration: Enable workflow mode (if previously used). Enable ADOMs (if multiple were configured). This ensures configuration is restored without affecting log data. Final validation: After successful recovery: Verify login via console and GUI. Confirm: Log data integrity. ADOM structure. Device information. Validate: License status. Reporting functionality. Create and store a new configuration backup . topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to solve the problem on FortiAnalyzer when PostgresSQL stuck during upgrade
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to solve the problem during FortiAnalyzer upgrade. Scope FortiAnalyzer v7.2.x, v7.4x, v7.6.x. Solution When trying to upgrade FortiAnalyzer, PostgresSQL maybe stuck at 41% with a console alert 'fail to upgrade postgres'. diagnose sql status upgrade-db Upgrading log SQL database 41%, stage: [Upgrade] started at: Tue Jul 1 17:09:18 2025 This is happening when trying to upgrade FortiAnalyzer without an upgrade path. Check the upgrade path in the link: Upgrade Path Tool Run the command below on the FortiAnalyzer that is having the issue and try to rebuild the database again: execute sql-local rebuild-db This command will cause the FortiAnalyzer to reboot, purge the analytics database, and start inserting the archive logs into the PostgreSQL/ClickHouse database. Although this procedure does not remove any log files, it is highly recommended to take a VM snapshot and/or back up the system configuration and log files to an external FTP server. Since this will rebuild the SQL database for all ADOMs, it may take a long time to complete, depending on the volume of logs stored and the current system resources available. There is no way to speed up this process.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: '500 Internal Server Error' when accessing FortiClient EMS Linux on GUI
topics.summary: Description This article describes a possible cause of the '500 Internal Server Error' that may appear when accessing FortiClient EMS on Linux, and explains how to identify and resolve the issue. Scope FortiClient EMS Linux. Solution When accessing FortiClient EMS through the GUI, the following error may appear: Internal Server Error One possible cause of this error is a mismatch between the system timezone configuration files /etc/localtime and /etc/timezone . Check Apache logs on the Linux server hosting FortiClient EMS. Logs can be collected using one of the following methods: Diagnostic Tool (see Technical Tip: How to collect FortiClient EMS on-premise logs by diagnostic tool for instructions). Manually check the Apache logs in: /var/log/apache2 If /etc/timezone and /etc/localtime contain conflicting values, the following errors may appear in the Apache logs: [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626489 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] mod_wsgi (pid=983877): Failed to exec Python script file '/opt/forticlientems/fcm/fcm/wsgi.py'. [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626526 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] mod_wsgi (pid=983877): Exception occurred processing WSGI script '/opt/forticlientems/fcm/fcm/wsgi.py'. [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626610 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] Traceback (most recent call last): [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626632 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] File "/opt/forticlientems/fcm/fcm/wsgi.py", line 15, in [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626637 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] import fcm.settings [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626641 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] File "/opt/forticlientems/fcm/fcm/settings.py", line 342, in [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626643 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] TIME_ZONE = tzlocal.get_localzone_name() [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626646 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] File "/opt/forticlientems/fcm/env24_amd64/lib/python3.10/site-packages/tzlocal/unix.py", line 193, in get_localzone_name [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626650 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] _cache_tz_name = _get_localzone_name() [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626653 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] File "/opt/forticlientems/fcm/env24_amd64/lib/python3.10/site-packages/tzlocal/unix.py", line 144, in _get_localzone_name [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626655 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] raise utils.ZoneInfoNotFoundError(message) [Mon Mar 02 00:00:30.626665 2026] [wsgi:error] [pid 983877:tid 984027] [remote 172.23.166.213:1944] tzlocal.utils.ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'Multiple conflicting time zone configurations found:\\n/etc/timezone: Etc/UTC\\n/etc/localtime is a symlink to: Europe/Rome\\nFix the configuration, or set the time zone in a TZ environment variable.\\n' FortiClient EMS relies on the system timezone configuration. If /etc/timezone and /etc/localtime contain different values, the EMS service fails to start correctly because it cannot determine which of these values is correct, resulting in a 500 Internal Server Error when accessing the GUI. EMS cannot change these settings, even during installation. Ensure that /etc/timezone and /etc/localtime are configured consistently on the Linux system. Once the mismatch is corrected, the EMS services should start normally, and GUI access should work again. Solution When check EMS installation log, the following output shows the error message: Read: 13.5 GiB ==> 82%zstd: error 70 : Write error : cannot write block : No space left on device dpkg: error processing archive /tmp/apt-dpkg-install-ohP46o/7-forticlientems_7.4.5.2111.M_amd64.deb (--unpack): new forticlientems package pre-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 /*stdin*\ : Read error (39) : premature end tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now dpkg: error while cleaning up: The keyword 'premature end' means the installation has not even started yet. It is recommended to have /tmp 1.5 times free disk space larger than /opt/forticlientems. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Web filter logs only show blocked in FortiAnalyzer
topics.summary: Description This article describes an issue where web-filter logs only show 'Blocked' and describes steps to troubleshoot the issue. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution There are multiple ways to check the web-filter logs in FortiAnalyzer. One is through the Log view -> Logs -> Fortinet Logs -> FortiGate -> Security -> Web Filter . The second method is through the FortiView -> Applications & Websites . Each method has its own benefits. FortiView has the advantage of being graphically visual and more compact, while Log Browse contains a lot more information without visuals. However, there may be an issue where it is only showing 'Blocked' websites, and the user requirement is to have all traffic be logged. The following steps can be followed to work on the issue: Verify the issue. Check FortiGate to see if it is generating the logs. If FortiGate itself does not generate the logs, the issue is mainly on FortiGate. The command below can be used to generate test logs on FortiGate: diagnose test log Check the logging configuration. FortiGate has the capability to configure the logging to comply with the storage requirements. Sometimes, the logging is reduced to accommodate the small storage and is unable to log all traffic entries. If the FortiGate has VDOM enabled, it is worth checking the override-setting. Check the policy configuration and profile configuration. Some configurations is policy or profile specific. In this case, with the web-filter profile, it is necessary to enable the following settings: config webfilter profile edit "sniffer-profile" <----- Profile name. set web-url-log enable set log-all-url enable end If all of the steps are complete and the situation remains the same, reach out to TAC for support to check the configuration in more details. Create a ticket through the Support portal . If the issue is identified as a FortiGate issue (Step #1), use the FortiGate serial number for the ticket creation. Otherwise, use the FortiAnalyzer ticket. Attach the configuration backup file to the ticket. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Cannot access FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer via the GUI after upgrade
topics.summary: Description This article describes a general fix for situations where the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer GUI is inaccessible after a firmware upgrade. The user is unable to access the GUI, and the service is not running, resulting in a defunct state. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer. Solution Context: In this scenario, the user has encountered problems accessing FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer through the GUI after a firmware upgrade. The message received in the browser is 'Connection_refused'. Access is established via the CLI, and the user ensures the device is working properly after the upgrade. Validation process: Check the current administrator settings and confirm no changes were made, and that HTTPS access continues using port 443 and HTTP 80. Enable a packet capture in FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer using port 443 and confirm the packets are received to eliminate the possibility of a network issue. Verify that the correct upgrade path was applied correctly (from the latest 7.2 version to v7.4.10) (run diagnose cdb upgrade summary ). Confirm there were no crashes related to the HTTP service ( run diagnose debug crash read ). Validate the current process list and status in process execution. In the current execution process, httpd is tagged as defunct, and checking the current process list shows httpd in a zombie status. Attempt to reset the httpd process and see whether the issue persists. In this example, the system resources were found in non-compliance with the minimum requirements of vCPU: there are only 2 vCPUs. After assigning 2 more vCPUs in the Hypervisor, the GUI session was established. If the resources are fine and the issue persists, perform the following: Unset HTTP/HTTPS administrative ports from the CLI. config system admin setting unset http_port unset https_port end Unset the admin GUI certificate. config system admin setting unset admin_server_cert end Reboot the device to allow the web service to start with default parameters. Note : Some useful commands to use when troubleshooting GUI responses: diagnose debug application gui 255 diagnose debug service httpd 255 diagnose debug service main 255 diagnose debug apache access-log diagnose debug apache error-log

Scope FortiAnalyzer ,FortiManager Solution Ensure the affected FortiAnalyzer/FortiManager model comes with IPMI ( The Intelligent Platform Management Interface). For more information, see Technical Tip: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer models that support monitoring of sensor readings . Perform the troubleshooting steps below: Gracefully shut down the FortiAnalyzer. It is necessary to keep integrity of the file system and DB: exec shutdown Unplug power cords and follow the next step while all power cords are disconnected: Press down the system power button (front-top-right) and hold it down for 30 seconds. Release the power button (after 30sec) Reconnect all power cords. Power up the device by pressing the power button. Once FortiAnalyzer boots up, run the command again. exec sensor list FortiAnalyzer should be able to display the output of 'exec sensor list'. topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiAnalyzer NOT ACCESS GUI Error PR_END_OF_FILE_ERROR
topics.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve an access issue on FortiAnalyzer when the device is reachable via SSH but not accessible through HTTPS. Scope FortiAnalyzer Solution When attempting to access the FortiAnalyzer device via HTTPS, the GUI fails to load and the browser displays the following error : PR_END_OF_FILE_ERROR . Behavior: The https service on FortiAnalyzer is enabled: config system interface edit port4 set ip 10.5.100.80 255.255.0.0 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp http fgfm end Admin access is also enabled: get system admin setting https_port : 443 admin_server_cert : FAZ-2025 Solution: To verify the current HTTP port configuration, check the http_port setting within the config system settings context. (setting)# get access-banner : disable admin-https-redirect: enable admin-login-max : 256 admin-scp : enable admin_server_cert : FAZ-2025 auth-addr : ( ) auth-port : 443 banner-message : ( ) fgt-gui-proxy : enable fgt-gui-proxy-port : 8082 firmware-upgrade-check: enable fsw-ignore-platform-check: disable gui-theme : neutrino http_port : 8080 https_port : 443 idle_timeout : 900 idle_timeout_api : 900 idle_timeout_gui : 900 idle_timeout_sso : 900 objects-force-deletion: enable preferred-fgfm-intf : ( ) show-add-multiple : disable show-checkbox-in-table: disable show-device-import-export: disable show-fct-manager : disable show-hostname : disable show-log-forwarding : enable unreg_dev_opt : add_allow_service webadmin_language : english If the http_port is set to a value other than 80, use the following command to reset it: (setting)# unset http_port To verify that this parameter has been configured with a default port, run the command again: (setting)# get access-banner : disable admin-https-redirect: enable admin-login-max : 256 admin-scp : enable admin_server_cert : FAZ-2025 auth-addr : () auth-port : 443 banner-message : ( ) fgt-gui-proxy : enable fgt-gui-proxy-port : 8082 firmware-upgrade-check: enable fsw-ignore-platform-check: disable gui-theme : neutrino http_port : 80 https_port : 443 idle_timeout : 900 idle_timeout_api : 900 idle_timeout_gui : 900 idle_timeout_sso : 900 objects-force-deletion: enable preferred-fgfm-intf : () show-add-multiple : disable show-checkbox-in-table: disable show-device-import-export: disable show-fct-manager : disable show-hostname : disable show-log-forwarding : enable unreg_dev_opt : add_allow_service webadmin_language : english (setting)# end Now, try t o access the FortiAnalyzer via the GUI. The HTTPS service must be running. Explanation: The Web Service (SOAP/XML API) uses TCP port 8080. If this port is already used by another service or application, it may cause a conflict when accessing the GUI. topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to resolve FortiAnalyzer 7.6 version showing Rebuilding SQL database status stuck at 99% for long time
topics.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve FortiAnalyzer 7.6 version GUI alert showing rebuilding SQL database stuck at 99% for long time and not proceeding further. Scope FortiAnalyzer v7.6.0 and later. Solution The FortiAnalyzer database upgrade from PostgreSQL (PSQL) to ClickHouse is an automatic background process that occurs when the FortiAnalyzer firmware is upgraded to version 7.6.0 or later. The database upgrade takes long time depending on the log database in FortiAnalyzer. Sometimes the rebuilding database gets finished however the status shows stuck at 99% during the completion stage and it does not proceed further. FortiAnalyzer GUI shows an alert saying Rebuilding SQL database showing progress of 99% with a short estimated remaining time and not moving forward. To confirm the database upgrade is finished perform the following two steps, Run ' diagnose sql show db-size ' multiple times and verify the size of the database is not increasing. FAZ01 # diagnose sql show db-size Size: 17574.92 GB FAZ01 # diagnose sql show db-size Size: 17574.92 GB FAZ01 # diagnose sql show db-size Size: 17574.92 GB Run ' diagnose sql status migrate-db ' and check the progress for 99% FAZ01 # diagnose sql status migrate-db Migrating log SQL database. started : Thu Jan 22 00:12:44 2026 took : 8d18h8m45s remain : 6m17s progress: 99% When the database size is not increasing and progress is at 99%, this means it is only a status update issue and that the database migrate has already been completed, meaning the latest logs are already visible. To resolve the issue, execute the following commands and wait for 5 minutes. After, verify the status of the migration again. diagnose siem process list diagnose test app siemdbd 99 Notice the message changed from 'Migrating log SQL Database' to 'Migrating log SQL database accomplished'. After running these commands, the alert message is also removed from the FortiAnalyzer GUI. FAZ01 # diagnose sql status migrate-db Migrating log SQL database accomplished. started : Thu Jan 22 00:12:44 2026 took : 29d9h40m18s Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to fix the 'Failed to sync user to FortiToken Cloud' error
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot an issue where the admin is not able to sync the user from FortiAnalyzer to FortiToken Cloud. See Fortitoken Cloud Login . Scope FortiAnalyzer and FortiCloud. Solution The issue can be caused by the following: FortiAnalyzer is unable to reach the FortiToken Cloud server. FortiToken licensing issue. To start, run the following debug commands to identify the specific error. diagnose debug application authentication 255 diagnose debug enable Go to Administrator -> User profile -> FortiToken Cloud -> Email -> Assigned Email -> 'OK' . Some debug messages should be generated after selecting the 'OK' button. If the message mentions a timeout issue, refer to the 'Verify connectivity to FortiToken Cloud' section of this KB article. Otherwise, refer to the 'Verify Licensing issue' section. Verify connectivity to FortiToken Cloud: The debug produces the following output: ftc_get_user: FTC_user ftc_curl: https://ftc.fortinet.com:8686/api/v1/user?username=FTC_user&vdom=FMG-FAZ * Host ftc.fortinet.com:8686 was resolved. * IPv6: (none) * IPv4: 69.167.109.248 * Trying 69.167.109.248:8686... * Connection timed out after 5001 milliseconds * closing connection #0 ftc_curl got 0 bytes: (null) ftc_curl err: Timeout was reached When configuring admin with FortiToken Cloud configuration, FortiAnalyzer will connect to the public FortiToken Cloud service on port 8686 to check the license status. Ensure FortiAnalyzer can connect to the following FQDN: ftc.fortinet.com Users can do a ping test to the FQDN to test reachability: If FortiAnalyzer can ping the server but the error persists, ensure the outgoing port from FortiAnalyzer to ftc.fortinet.com on port 8686 is allowed. This can be done by checking the output of the network sniffer on FortiAnalyzer: Run the sniffer and filter for port 8686: diagnose sniffer packet any ‘port 8686’ In a separate CLI session, run the command to check FortiCloud Token status: diagnose fortitoken-cloud status The following example shows the sniffer output when traffic cannot reach FortiToken Cloud from FortiAnalyzer: Once traffic from FortiAnalyzer to ftc.fortinet.com on port 8686 is allowed, the issue should no longer persist. The following example shows the sniffer output when there is no issue with the traffic: Verify licensing issue: Several errors will be found in the debug logs: * Request completely sent off * upload completely sent off: 161 bytes < HTTP/1.1 402 PAYMENT REQUIRED < Server: nginx < Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 04:54:18 GMT < Content-Type: application/json < Content-Length: 133 < Connection: close < * Closing connection * TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, close notify (256): * TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS alert, close notify (256): ftc_curl got 133 bytes: "Your account has been disabled. Please contact your Fortinet sales representative for information on how to re-enable your account." ftc_curl err: HTTP response code said error < HTTP/1.1 402 PAYMENT REQUIRED <----- The HTTP 402 'Payment Required' error from Fortinet indicates the account has been disabled due to billing or subscription issues. The error relates to the billing point of a FortiToken Cloud Subscription. If a billing issue occurs, reach out to a Fortinet Sales Representative for further action. topics.title: Technical Tip: FortiAnalyzer rejects the FGFM/OFTP connection attempts with error 'No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled/LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id'
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve a communication issue between FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer with the error 'No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled/LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id'. Scope FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate VM. Solution It is possible that after an upgrade to firmware branch v7.4 on FortiGate (v7.4.9) and FortiAnalyzer (v7.4.8), the connection between the devices is lost. If the FortiGate is removed from the FortiAnalyzer at this point, it might not be possible to re-add the device anymore, with the error 'No devices are available for approval.'. On FortiGate, when trying to set up the connection again, the connection status may show as 'Unauthorized'. When testing connectivity from FortiGate-VM CLI, it shows the error below: FGT-VM# execute log fortianalyzer test-connectivity Testing connectivity to fortianalyzer ... Failed to get FAZ's status. oftp_connect(global-faz) failed: oftp failed to authenticate. Steps to troubleshoot connectivity issues between FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer may be found in this article: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiGate to FortiAnalyzer connectivity . However, the following error may be encountered on FortiAnalyzer when trying to re-establish the connection: Error No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id. FortiAnalyzer rejects the FGFM/OFTP connection attempts from FortiGate. The error indicates that the FortiGate VM’s client certificate does not contain a 'legal' serial number, and the FortiAnalyzer refuses the device because legacy authentication mode is disabled. To resolve the issue, the following settings need to be made on the FortiAnalyzer CLI to enable legacy authentication mode: config system log settings set legacy-auth-mode enable end After enabling this setting, the FortiGate VM should be accepted and show as properly registered in FortiAnalyzer. Note: If the connection is still rejected with: 'LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id' After enabling legacy-auth-mode, check the oftpd debug on FortiAnalyzer for 'Error login check: FGT SN= not match from cert'. This indicates the certificate contains a serial number, but not the one reported by the connecting device (for example, a FortiGate HA member presenting the peer member's replicated certificate). Legacy authentication does not bypass this check when a serial number is present in the certificate. This is expected behaviour. To resolve this, use a custom certificate containing the device's own serial number. From FortiAnalyzer v7.4.7 and v7.6.3 onwards, the serial number is also checked against the SAN field, so for an HA cluster, a single certificate listing all member serial numbers in the SAN allows every member to authenticate. The ' legacy-auth-mode ' setting was introduced in FortiAnalyzer v7.2.10 GA, FortiAnalyzer v7.4.7 GA, and FortiAnalyzer v7.6.3 GA. More information can be found in the following article: Technical Tip: Additional information about the 'legacy-auth-mode' setting and certificate on OFTP connection checking on FortiAnalyzer . In some cases, while running FortiAnalyzer on versions, for example, version 7.6.6, the same error might be visible in debug: 'LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id' Then check the Release notes -> supported models -> FortiGate special branch models . There might be incompatibility with some models, for example, FortiGate-400G, which is supported starting from FortiAnalyzer version 7.6.7. That will require a FortiAnalyzer upgrade to support this hardware model. Note : FortiAnalyzer version 8.0.0+ enforces certificate-based authentication by default, and legacy auth is a compatibility fallback for some OFTP devices.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Using FortiAnalyzer to detect activities related to the Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass | CVE-2025-34026
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to use a custom event handler in FortiAnalyzer to raise alerts for incident response related to attacks that attempt to leverage the Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass. A report is also provided to gain historical visibility into the logs. Note that this article provides alpha files which are automatically generated. The article will be continually updated as more information becomes available. For more information about this attack, see the following FortiGuard Outbreak Alert: Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass . Scope This article contains the files necessary to load an event handler and report into the FortiAnalyzer for either a Fabric ADOM or a FortiGate ADOM. The Fabric report and event handler leverage logs from other Fortinet products that can be used to detect the attack in addition to FortiGate logs. Solution What is included in Fortinet_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass.zip: Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_event-handler.json: This event handler helps identify Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass attacks detected by FortiGate and other Fortinet products. This event handler is configured for Fabric ADOMs. Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_report.dat: This report displays the findings on Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass from FortiGate and other Fortinet products. It is configured for Fabric ADOMs. fgt_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_event-handler.json: The event handler for FortiGate ADOMs is configured for FortiGate logs only. fgt_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_report.dat: The FortiGate ADOMs report includes only FortiGate charts. Steps: Download the Fortinet_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass.zip file (contains 4 files). Unzip Fortinet_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass.zip. Import Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_event-handler.json or fgt_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_event-handler.json event handler: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may have the Fabric or FortiGate type. Choose the FortiSOC module. Select Event Handler List . Select the Import option under More . Select the appropriate event handler depending on the ADOM type. Result: The event handler is enabled and will be triggered if the appropriate logs are received following the import of the event handler. Edit the event handler to customize the notification section. Import Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_report.dat or fgt_Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_report.dat to Reports: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may have the Fabric or FortiGate type. Choose the Report module. Select the Import option under 'More' . Select the appropriate file for the ADOM type to add the report to the ADOM. Result : The Versa Concerto SD-WAN Authentication Bypass_report can be run anytime as determined by an admin user. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient VPN before logon fails to connect when using windows credentials
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiClient version 7.4 fails to establish a VPN connection before user logon using Windows credentials.ScopeFortiClient version 7.4.SolutionSymptoms.Users cannot connect to the SSL VPN or IPsec VPN using the VPN Before Logon feature after upgrading to FortiClient version 7.4. The connection fails at the Windows logon screen, and no logs are generated on the FortiGate.Root cause.In FortiClient version7.4, a change in behavior causes the client to check for credentials before initiating the connection.
incidents.symptom: FortiClient version 7.4 fails to establish a VPN connection before user logon using Windows credentials
incidents.solution: Symptoms.Users cannot connect to the SSL VPN or IPsec VPN using the VPN Before Logon feature after upgrading to FortiClient version 7.4. The connection fails at the Windows logon screen, and no logs are generated on the FortiGate.Root cause.In FortiClient version7.4, a change in behavior causes the client to check for credentials before initiating the connection. If the Prompt for Username setting is disabled, FortiClient may fail to retrieve the necessary credentials from Windows, causing the pre-logon connection to halt. This differs from FortiClient version 7.2, which attempted to start the connection even if credentials were not immediately found.Resolution Contournement : To resolve this issue in FortiClient version 7.4, enable the prompt for usernames in the endpoint profile:Log in to the FortiClient EMS console.Select Endpoint Profiles -> System Settings.Select the profile applied to the affected endpoints and select Edit.Navigate to the VPN tunnel settings.Enable the prompt for username option.Save the changes and deploy the profile to the endpoints.Settings in SSL VPN tunnel configuration:Settings in IPsec VPN tunnel configuration:Permanent solution.This behavior is not present in FortiClient version 8.0.0 and above. Upgrade the FortiClient installation to FortiClient version 8.0.0 or above to restore the VPN Before Logon behavior without requiring the username prompt

sources.title: IPSec VPN FortiGate to FortiClient
sources.summary: I’m on a FortiGate 61F version 7.4.11 and FortiClient Windows version 7.4.3.I am trying to set up IPSec VPN for my remote users so that I can upgrade the FortiGate (knowing that SSL is no longer supported). I’m running into trouble with Authentication when it comes to PSK vs Peer ID from dialup group. What I want is for the tunnel to accept users from a specific local user group on the FortiGate. My problem is that if I change the Peer Options to Peer ID from dialup group, the Pre-shared Key box goes away. That’s then a problem on FortiClient since I can't leave the PSK box blank. Any help on how to solve this? Thank you! Side Note: I have an IPSec VPN for remote users set up on a different box running 7.6.6 doing exactly what I want. There are more options for Authentication on that version and I can have a PSK and the tell it to use user group I want.

incidents.symptom: Troubleshooting steps for installation failure in FortiManager version 7.6.8 due to the 'udp-not-quic' option under 'config firewall ssl-ssh-profile' when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory
incidents.solution: In version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation to fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS version 7.6.This behavior is due to a known issue, with ID 1352524 Contournement : Set 'udp-not-quic' to 'block' in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Set udp-not-quic to block in the https and dot sections of the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Go to Policy & Objects -> Advanced.Select the CLI Configurations tab.In the left pane, under firewall, select ssl-ssh-profile.Select the affected profile (for example, custom-deep-inspection), then select Edit.In the Edit firewall ssl-ssh-profile window, scroll to the https section and set udp-not-quic to block.Scroll to the dot section and set udp-not-quic to block.Select OK.Repeat steps 4 to 7 for each SSL/SSH profile that is used by the 2GB FortiGate devices.Install the policy package again.Note: Some models may not accept this setting. For example, a comment on this article reports 'Operation not supported. detail: object not support' on a FortiGate 50G. Contact Fortinet Support if the error persists.Fix: A fix is expected in FortiManager firmware versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.3.Related document:Known issues

sources.title: IKEv2 IPsec VPN – Negotiation Timeout During OTP Authentication
sources.summary: FortiClient IKEv2 IPsec VPN – Negotiation Timeout After 30 Seconds During RADIUS/EAP OTP AuthenticationHello everyone,I'm experiencing an issue with an IKEv2 IPsec remote-access VPN using RADIUS/EAP authentication with MFA/OTP, and I would appreciate your feedback or any similar experiences.Environment FortiGate: FortiOS 7.6.6 FortiAuthenticator: 6.6.8 FortiClient: 7.4.8 (ZTNA) VPN: IPsec IKEv2 Remote Access Authentication: RADIUS/EAP with MFA/OTP RADIUS server: FortiAuthenticator Issue descriptionThe issue occurs regardless of the OTP delivery method. We have reproduced it with: FortiToken Mobile SMS OTP Email OTP When the user enters the OTP within approximately 30 seconds, authentication succeeds and the VPN tunnel is established normally.However, if OTP entry takes longer than approximately 30 seconds, FortiClient remains in the "Connecting" state. The connection eventually fails with an IKE negotiation timeout, and the tunnel is not established.Important observation

incidents.title: 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: Description This articles describes an issue where the 1GbE SFP ports may fail to forward traffic on FortiGate 1800F/1801F after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8 Scope FortiGate 1800F, FortiGate 1801F, FortiOS 7.6.8 Solution Following an internal driver update introduced in FortiOS 7.6.8, the affected platforms - FortiGate 1800F and 1801F is unable to process traffic over its GE SFP slots. As a summary:GE SFP ports 17-24 are unable to process traffic.Traffic through SFP ports 25-40 is unaffected.Traffic through GE RJ45 ports is unaffected.

incidents.title: How to fix "error firewall service custom protocol" after ADOM upgrade
incidents.summary: Description A fix for the installation issue with multiple "firewall service custom" objects that may occur after an ADOM upgrade. Post vdom failed: error firewall service custom protocol- TCP_UDP_20101 TCP/UDP/SCTP:-999 - invalid value - prop[protocol]: option(TCP/UDP/SCTP) Copy objects for vdom Main_VDOM "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "certificate-inspection", id=18459, SKIP - (null) "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "deep-inspection", id=18474, SKIP - (null) Scope FortiManager.
incidents.symptom: A fix for the installation issue with multiple "firewall service custom" objects that may occur after an ADOM upgrade. Post vdom failed: error firewall service custom protocol- TCP_UDP_20101 TCP/UDP/SCTP:-999 - invalid value - prop[protocol]: option(TCP/UDP/SCTP) Copy objects for vdom Main_VDOM "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "certificate-inspection", id=18459, SKIP - (null) "firewall ssl-ssh-profile", "deep-inspection", id=18474, SKIP - (null)
incidents.solution: When upgrading from FortiOS 7.4 to 7.6, the default protocol changes from TCP/UDP/SCTP to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP. To match this logic, a 7.6 ADOM should be used in FortiManager. However, it might appear that after upgrading the ADOM, "firewall service custom" objects fail to be installed. When drilling down to the object, it can be observed that the UUID of the object is set to ZERO, which is causing the issue during the installation: To resolve this problem and generate a correct UUID, it is possible to add the comment to the object, click the "Ok" button to update the object, and verify that a new UUID was generated. However, it may be challenging if it requires updating a bunch of such objects. To address this situation, use a script: Step 1: First, print a list of all objects to check how many have a ZERO UUID. execute fmpolic print-adom-object 167 +all Step 2: Take note of all affected objects and create a script. config firewall service custom edit "Jitsi_TCP_4443" unset uuid end Step 3: Run the script against the "Policy Package or ADOM DB". Step 4: Verify the object has a new, updated UUID and the installation runs without an error

incidents.title: Unable to delete a VDOM from FortiManager when its management VDOM is in a different ADOM
incidents.summary: Description How to delete the VDOM using FortiManager when the management VDOM is not present in the same ADOM as the target VDOM. Scope FortiManager. Solution FortiManager enforces a device/VDOM model constraint that prevents deleting a VDOM while its management VDOM resides in a different ADOM. This article explains the constraint and provides two practical workarounds. FortiManager's ADOM (Administrative Domain) architecture determines how VDOMs are assigned and managed.
incidents.symptom: How to delete the VDOM using FortiManager when the management VDOM is not present in the same ADOM as the target VDOM
incidents.solution: FortiManager enforces a device/VDOM model constraint that prevents deleting a VDOM while its management VDOM resides in a different ADOM. This article explains the constraint and provides two practical workarounds. FortiManager's ADOM (Administrative Domain) architecture determines how VDOMs are assigned and managed. In Normal Device Mode, all VDOMs from a single FortiGate must be placed in the same ADOM. In Advanced Device Mode, individual VDOMs from the same FortiGate can be assigned to separate ADOMs, enabling multi-tenant management. The deletion restriction occurs because FortiManager's device database tracks the management VDOM's ADOM assignment. When the management VDOM is in a different ADOM than the target VDOM, FortiManager cannot process the deletion through its normal device database operations. This is consistent with expected behavior where FortiManager displays errors when the management VDOM is not in the current ADOM for example, the error 'The management VDOM for device xxxxxx is not in the current advanced ADOM' Contournement : 1: Move the VDOM to the Same ADOM. Temporarily move the non-management VDOM so that both the management VDOM and the target VDOM reside in the same ADOM, then delete the VDOM. Workaround 2: Delete Directly on the FortiGate and Resync. Delete the VDOM directly on the FortiGate (bypassing FortiManager's ADOM restriction), then resynchronize the FortiGate on FortiManager. Verify the VDOM is removed from FortiManager's device database. Note : If the VDOM was created in FortiManager's device database but not properly saved, you may encounter an "Internal error" (code -20001) when attempting deletion. In such cases, run the following command on FortiManager to fix the database: diagnose cdb upgrade check resync-dev-vdoms This resyncs and removes any missing VDOMs from the device database

incidents.title: Administrator SSO authentication fails after upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.8.SolutionAfter upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login…
incidents.symptom: After upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8, administrator SSO authentication fails. FortiOS access requires a local administrator or a RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ administrator account
incidents.solution: After upgrade, administrator SSO will fail with the error message "Single Sign-On Failed", without presenting any option to enter an SSO administrator credential.The following FortiOS login methods are confirmed affected by the issue:Administrator FortiCloud SSO.Administrator third-party SSO, for example see Technical Tip: Configuring SAML SSO login for FortiGate administrators with Entra ID acting as SAML IdP.Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP, for example see Configuring single-sign-on in the Security Fabric.Confirmed not affected:VPN user SSO authentication.Other FortiOS versions including FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2.Local administrator authentication.Remote administrator authentication using RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+.While access to the FortiGate from FortiManagement Cloud (FortiGate Cloud) is technically not affected, SSO authentication to the FortiGate is still not possible over this management path.Issue matching:To confirm the issue, check the FortiOS crashlog for a matching "FORTISM Violation" from the time of the access attempt. This can be done by accessing the FortiGate using a local administrator account and executing diagnose debug crashlog read | gr Contournement : At this time, the only available workaround is to use another administrator authentication method.If no suitable administrator account exists, console access to a physical device can be used to recover access, see Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console.If the device is centrally managed by FortiManager or a valid FortiManagement Cloud subscription, an administrator can be added. See Recover access to FortiGate via FortiManagement Cloud.Related article:Technical Tip: Create a 'break glass' admin account on the FortiGate as a backup for remote authentication/MFA (Recommendation)

incidents.symptom: The ipsengine daemon crashes frequently on FortiGate devices running FortiOS 7.4.x / 7.6.x when FortiSandBox scanning is enabled in AntiVirus profiles
incidents.solution: SymptomAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.x or 7.6.x, the ipsengine daemon has been observed to crash repeatedly.The crash logs indicate a segmentation fault (Signal 11). This behavior results in Intrusion Prevention System scanning failures, which may cause certain traffic sessions or websites to be blocked.The following command below allows you to check the latest ipsengine crashes that occurred:Note:When an AntiVirus profile is configured to use FortiSandBox scanning (either Cloud or On-Premises), this will trigger a crash in the ipsengine.diagnose debug crashlog read | grep ipsengine -A 1 15512: 2026-09-08 07:26:43 application ipsengine 07.004.604 15513: 2026-09-08 07:26:43 *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received *** ... 15587: 2026-09-08 07:30:26 application ipsengine 07.004.604 15588: 2026-09-08 07:30:26 *** signal 11 (Segmentation fault) received *** Contournement : Disable the FortiSandBox scanning feature within all AntiVirus profiles used in Firewall policies. This allows other security profiles, such as SSL Inspection, Web Filtering, and IPS, to continue functioning without crashing the engine.Log in to the FortiGate GUI.Select Security Fabric -> AntiVirus.Edit the AntiVirus profiles used in the firewall policies.Under the APT Protection Option, set Send files to FortiSandbox for inspection to disabled.Select OK to save the changes.Alternatively, use the Command Line Interface (CLI) to disable the feature:config antivirus profile edit " " config http set fortisandbox disable end config ftp set fortisandbox disable end config imap set fortisandbox disable end config pop3 set fortisandbox disable end config smtp set fortisandbox disable end next endThe permanent fix for this Known Issue is already included in FortiOS 7.4.13, 7.6.7, and 8.0.0.Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 7.4.13 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 7.6.7 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Resolved issues | FortiGate / FortiOS 8.0.0 | Fortinet Document Library - 1182611Related article: FortiGate / FortiOS - Administration Guide -

incidents.title: Technical Tip: FortiAuthenticator ZTNA tunnel failing due to 'Traffic denied because cert auth failed' error on FortiGate
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAuthenticator ZTNA certificate error on FortiGate. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate. Solution FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 introduced a Zero Trust Tunnel Feature, which is used to securely connect with an on-prem Active Directory Server(LDAP). Zero trust tunnels FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 This article assumes that the initial setup for this feature has been completed: Setting up a zero trust tunnel If the ZTNA tunnel is failing on the FortiGate, check the ZTNA traffic logs on FortiGate: Log…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAuthenticator ZTNA certificate error on FortiGate
incidents.solution: FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 introduced a Zero Trust Tunnel Feature, which is used to securely connect with an on-prem Active Directory Server(LDAP). Zero trust tunnels FortiAuthenticator v6.4.4 This article assumes that the initial setup for this feature has been completed: Setting up a zero trust tunnel If the ZTNA tunnel is failing on the FortiGate, check the ZTNA traffic logs on FortiGate: Log & Report -> ZTNA Traffic. In the screenshot above, the error 'Traffic denied because cert auth failed' shows up. To resolve this issue, ensure the ZTNA CA certificate has already been uploaded onto the FortiGate: If the CA certificate does not exist, import it and make sure to take note of the name after importing the CA certificate. In the screenshot above, the name is 'CA_Cert_2'. The FortiGate will need to use the CA certificate in order to trust the FortiAuthenticator certificate for the ZTNA tunnel. After confirming the CA certificate, configure the following option through the FortiGate CLI: config authentication setting set user-cert-ca end Note: The authentication rule and scheme settings should also be configured as described in the documentation below: Configuring certificate authe

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tips: Admin is logged out of the GUI immediately after login (login must be entered twice) on FortiGate version 7.6.7
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue on FortiOS version 7.6.7: some administrators are kicked back to the login page right after a successful GUI login; it is necessary to enter credentials a second time before the dashboard loads. In other cases, the first attempt shows a blank/white page, and a later attempt loads normally. The login may be recorded in the event log together with an HTTPS connection error, even though authentication itself succeeds.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.7.SolutionSymptoms:After entering the username and password, the login…
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue on FortiOS version 7.6.7: some administrators are kicked back to the login page right after a successful GUI login; it is necessary to enter credentials a second time before the dashboard loads. In other cases, the first attempt shows a blank/white page, and a later attempt loads normally. The login may be recorded in the event log together with an HTTPS connection error, even though authentication itself succeeds
incidents.solution: Symptoms:After entering the username and password, the login page reappears instead of the dashboard. Entering the credentials a second time succeeds and the GUI loads.The issue affects GUI (HTTPS) logins only, SSH sessions are not affected. It may be seen across Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, and sometimes in /private mode as well.An 'HTTPS connection error' may be logged in the event log.Root cause:When signing in through a web browser, the page loads a large number of small resources all at once (far more than in earlier releases). The web interface's activity monitor mistakes this normal burst of activity for a brief attack and interrupts the login, dropping back to the login page, even though the username and password were already accepted.This is why the login can appear in the event log as successful while the page still sends back: authentication succeeds, but the session is cut before the dashboard finishes loading.Related known issues in the 7.6.7 release notes:Bug ID 1300025 – Admin session termination (especially Chrome/Edge) Contournement : clear browser cache/cookies.Bug ID 1306049 – Blank page after upgrade to 7.6.7. Workaround involves disabling HTTP rate-limiter settings.Resolution:Fixed in FortiOS version 7.6.8 (and above version 8.0.1). The fix scopes the unauthenticated request-body monitor to body-carrying methods only, raises the unauthenticated request timeout from 1 s to 10 s, and reworks the rate-limiter token pricing and refund logic so a normal GUI bootstrap is not mistaken for an attack and killed.Upgrade to FortiOS version 7.6.8 or above to resolve the issue.Workaround (until upgrade):Until the upgrade can be performed, one of the following avoids the problem:Clear the browser cache and cookies associated with the FortiGate, then log in again.Access the GUI in the browser's Incognito/InPrivate mode.Simply log in a second time; the second attempt loads the dashboard normally.Diagnostic Commands:Useful while reproducing the issue:diagnose debug resetdiagnose debug console timestamp enablediagnose debug application httpsd -1diagnose debug application node -1diagnose debug application http_authd -1 # or http_authdiagnose debug enableStop with:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset

The fix scopes the unauthenticated request-body monitor to body-carrying methods only, raises the unauthenticated request timeout from 1 s to 10 s, and reworks the rate-limiter token pricing and refund logic so a normal GUI bootstrap is not mistaken for an attack and killed.Upgrade to FortiOS version 7.6.8 or above to resolve the issue.Workaround (until upgrade):Until the upgrade can be performed, one of the following avoids the problem:Clear the browser cache and cookies associated with the FortiGate, then log in again.Access the GUI in the browser's Incognito/InPrivate mode.Simply log in a second time; the second attempt loads the dashboard normally.Diagnostic Commands:Useful while reproducing the issue:diagnose debug resetdiagnose debug console timestamp enablediagnose debug application httpsd -1diagnose debug application node -1diagnose debug application http_authd -1 # or http_authdiagnose debug enableStop with:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset

incidents.title: FortiGate 30/31G Platform unable to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8 "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification."
incidents.summary: DescriptionInstructions to resolve the "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." error when upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionWhen upgrading from FortiOS 7.6.7 to 7.6.8, you may face an error stating "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." when the image has finished downloading (or uploading, if you are using the file upload function):This is a known issue with the 30/31G platform, and the solution is to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.7 STS build 8767 before proceeding.
incidents.symptom: Instructions to resolve the "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." error when upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8
incidents.solution: When upgrading from FortiOS 7.6.7 to 7.6.8, you may face an error stating "This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification." when the image has finished downloading (or uploading, if you are using the file upload function):This is a known issue with the 30/31G platform, and the solution is to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.7 STS build 8767 before proceeding. To get this build, open a TAC ticket. After upgrading to this build, it will be possible to upgrade to FortiOS 7.6.8 GA: FortiOS 7.6.7 GA -> 7.6.7 STS build8767 -> 7.6.8 GA.Useful:In the ticket, you will find attached the special build you should need for the upgrade :The upgrade path should be: Current FOS 7.6.7 GA -> Special build8767 -> 7.6.8 GAAlternatively, you can upgrade the device via FortiManager.Note: If during the upgrade procedure you get an error on the GUI stating: "Image upgrade fail device could not be rebooted" and via console cable:inflate() error: -3This is because the device does not have enough free RAM to proceed with the upgrade. As a workaround, change the number of IPS workers to 1:config ips global set engine-count 1 endReboot the unit and try again. If it still fails with the same error, disable UTM temp

incidents.title: Bypassing FortiCare registration when CLI configuration or off-network license uploading fails
incidents.summary: DescriptionInstructions to bypass FortiCare registration through BIOS.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionOn newer FortiGate models, FortiCare registration is required before accessing the GUI. After the first login, you will be automatically redirected to the registration page. Once the device is registered, you can proceed with the configuration.However, there are situations where internet connectivity cannot be established through the CLI, preventing FortiCare registration, or where the air-gapped deployment option does not function as expected.
incidents.symptom: Instructions to bypass FortiCare registration through BIOS
incidents.solution: On newer FortiGate models, FortiCare registration is required before accessing the GUI. After the first login, you will be automatically redirected to the registration page. Once the device is registered, you can proceed with the configuration.However, there are situations where internet connectivity cannot be established through the CLI, preventing FortiCare registration, or where the air-gapped deployment option does not function as expected. Please try this methods first before changing BIOS settings: Enforce FortiCare registration.Example 1: It is not possible to select the reseller because the device does not have an Internet connection configured and there is no other option to bypass registration:Example 2: Before FortiCare registration is completed, the FortiOS CLI is restricted to read-only access, with only a subset of network configuration commands permitted. In theory, these commands should allow customers to configure an Internet connection. However, some customers have reported that they are unable to use them as expected or not recognizing the commands at all.Solution The solution is to access the BIOS menu and manually set the FortiCare registration level to 1 as sh

incidents.summary: DescriptionA firmware upgrade behavior issue observed in a High Availability (HA) cluster. In an HA cluster, when the FGCP Multi-Version Cluster (MVC) upgrade mode is enabled using set uninterruptible-upgrade enable, the upgrade behavior will upgrade the Secondary unit first followed by the Primary unit.However, there are cases where the firmware upgrade may not proceed to the Primary unit even after the Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded.For example:The Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded to firmware version 7.6.7.However, the…
incidents.symptom: A firmware upgrade behavior issue observed in a High Availability (HA) cluster. In an HA cluster, when the FGCP Multi-Version Cluster (MVC) upgrade mode is enabled using set uninterruptible-upgrade enable, the upgrade behavior will upgrade the Secondary unit first followed by the Primary unit.However, there are cases where the firmware upgrade may not proceed to the Primary unit even after the Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded.For example:The Secondary unit has been successfully upgraded to firmware version 7.6.7.However, the Primary unit remains on firmware version 7.4.11
incidents.solution: Recommended action:Do not reboot the Primary unit or initiate a failover.Re-run the firmware upgrade from the Primary unit to trigger the upgrade process again.This approach will usually resolve the issue and allow the firmware upgrade to proceed as expected

incidents.title: FortiClient Web Filter browser extension fails to uninstall during an on-fabric to off-fabric transition
incidents.summary: DescriptionWhen the Web Filter extension is not uninstalled when the endpoint moves from on-fabric to off-fabric while 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled and 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering' is enabled.ScopeFortiClient Endpoint version 8.0.0, FortiClient Windows.SolutionIssue scenario: FortiClient v8.0.0.0103 GA.Enable the Web Filter profile.Disable 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric'.Enable 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering'.Verify the extension is installed while on-fabric.Move the endpoint to…
incidents.symptom: When the Web Filter extension is not uninstalled when the endpoint moves from on-fabric to off-fabric while 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled and 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering' is enabled
incidents.solution: Issue scenario: FortiClient v8.0.0.0103 GA.Enable the Web Filter profile.Disable 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric'.Enable 'Web Browser Plugin for HTTPS Web Filtering'.Verify the extension is installed while on-fabric.Move the endpoint to off-fabric and observe that the extension is not uninstalled. Issue resolved In: FortiClient version 8.0.1. Solution description:Fixed a bug where the policy watchdog unconditionally re-added the browser extension force-install policy. The fix ensures that when 'Keep Extension When Endpoint is Off-Fabric' is disabled, the policy is removed during the transition to an inactive filtering state (including on-fabric to off-fabric). Both the periodic policy-check and extended-keepalive-absence paths now respect the policy gate to prevent the extension from being resurrected. Additionally, SafeSearch hosts-file enforcement was updated to align with actual extension presence
