incidents.title: FortiGate Single Sign-On users logged off when Enforce Kerberos is enabled
incidents.summary: DescriptionUsers are automatically logged off from FortiGate Single Sign-On after enabling the Enforce Kerberos setting in the Collector Agent.ScopeFortiGate, FSSO Collector AgentSolutionA known issue exists where the workstation check fails when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled. Users are de-authenticated when the workstation check fails after the dead entry timeout.Upgrade the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent to version 5.0.0335 or later.
incidents.symptom: Users are automatically logged off from FortiGate Single Sign-On after enabling the Enforce Kerberos setting in the Collector Agent
incidents.solution: A known issue exists where the workstation check fails when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled. Users are de-authenticated when the workstation check fails after the dead entry timeout.Upgrade the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent to version 5.0.0335 or later. This version addresses WMI workstation check failures when "Enforce Kerberos" is enabled by adding reverse DNS lookup to resolve workstation IP addresses to hostnames.Download the FortiGate Single Sign-On Collector Agent version 5.0.0335 from the Fortinet Support Portal.Install the updated Collector Agent on the server.Enable the "Enforce Kerberos" setting in the Collector Agent configuration.Monitor the user sessions to verify that they are no longer automatically logged off after one hour.Related article:Technical Tip: FortiGate FSSO Collector Agent v5.0.0323 and earlier do not support Windows Server 2025 with default polling mode

incidents.title: FortiClient Endpoints fail to match assigned Entra ID group policies and fall into the default policy due to a synchronization issue between the user identity and the device object.
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiClient Endpoints that are members of a specific Entra ID group do not match the corresponding group policy in FortiClient EMS. These endpoints are assigned to the default policy.ScopeFortiClient EMS and FortiClient Endpoint.SolutionFortiClient EMS cannot correctly retrieve the Azure device object ID for certain users. This occurs when a mismatch or failure happens in the lookup process between the reported user identity and the Entra ID device object, resulting in a 404 Not Found error during the API call to Microsoft Graph.Error…
incidents.symptom: FortiClient Endpoints that are members of a specific Entra ID group do not match the corresponding group policy in FortiClient EMS. These endpoints are assigned to the default policy
incidents.solution: FortiClient EMS cannot correctly retrieve the Azure device object ID for certain users. This occurs when a mismatch or failure happens in the lookup process between the reported user identity and the Entra ID device object, resulting in a 404 Not Found error during the API call to Microsoft Graph.Error example:ERROR update/sysinfo.go:344 [TID:KiK5dhcVVQ][site:default][uid:A11E1B23714F48A4910032061E4E7122]: Could not get azure device object id: search for device object id: http.GET(https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/devices(deviceId='0e427e3a-5d65-40bb-bfa5-b1b72f940d1b')?%24select=id) return status: 404 Not FoundPermanent solution: Update FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.8 or above. This version includes the fix for the identity matching bug.If updating to version 7.4.8 is not immediately possible, use the following workaround:Create a new group in Entra ID.Add the computer accounts directly to this new group instead of adding user accounts.Assign the desired FortiClient EMS policy to this new computer-based group

incidents.title: rxqid default value was changed after upgrade
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter an upgrade from versions 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4 to versions 7.0.15, 7.2.9, and 7.4.5, the rxqid value was changed and may cause RX drops on the interface.ScopeFortiOS.SolutionSymptomsUnder system 'affinity-packet-redistribution ' is the rxqid setting. It is the ID of the receive queue on an interface used to perform packet redistribution across multiple CPU cores. The value is from to .In 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4, the default value is 0.
incidents.symptom: After an upgrade from versions 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4 to versions 7.0.15, 7.2.9, and 7.4.5, the rxqid value was changed and may cause RX drops on the interface
incidents.solution: SymptomsUnder system 'affinity-packet-redistribution ' is the rxqid setting. It is the ID of the receive queue on an interface used to perform packet redistribution across multiple CPU cores. The value is from to .In 7.0.14, 7.2.8, and 7.4.4, the default value is 0. After upgrading FortiOS to 7.0.15, 7.2.9, 7.4.5, and above, the default value is changed to 255. In some cases, it can cause an increase in interface RX drops.7.0.14 7.2.8 7.4.4:FGT # get system status | grep Version: Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.4,build2662,240514 (GA.F) FGT # show system affinity-packet-redistribution config system affinity-packet-redistribution edit 1 set interface "port2" set affinity-cpumask "0xff" next end FGT # show full system affinity-packet-redistribution config system affinity-packet-redistribution edit 1 set interface "port2" set rxqid 0 set round-robin disable set affinity-cpumask "0xff" next end7.0.15 7.2.9 7.4.5 and above:FGT # get system status | grep Version: Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.5,build2702,240916 (GA.M) FGT # show system affinity-packet-redistribution config system affinity-packet-redistribution edit 1 set interface "port2" set affinity-cpumask "0xff" next end FGT # sh

incidents.summary: DescriptionAn issue where the administrative web interface (httpsd) becomes unreachable when the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is down, such as an IPsec tunnel.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptomsThe FortiGate GUI is not reachable, and users receive a 500 error when attempting to load the administration page. The httpsd process may not be running or fails to start. This issue can affect both the primary and secondary units in a High Availability cluster.Root CauseThe FortiGate management web server (httpsd) hosts the ACME client…
incidents.symptom: An issue where the administrative web interface (httpsd) becomes unreachable when the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is down, such as an IPsec tunnel
incidents.solution: SymptomsThe FortiGate GUI is not reachable, and users receive a 500 error when attempting to load the administration page. The httpsd process may not be running or fails to start. This issue can affect both the primary and secondary units in a High Availability cluster.Root CauseThe FortiGate management web server (httpsd) hosts the ACME client used for Let's Encrypt certificate challenges. If the ACME client is configured to listen on an interface that is currently down (for example, an IPsec tunnel), the web server cannot bind its listener to that interface. This causes the httpsd process to shut down, which blocks all administrative web access, including access via the management port.Resolution Contournement : Remove the interface binding from the ACME configuration to allow the web server to start.Connect to the FortiGate via the Command Line Interface (CLI).Run the following commands to unset the ACME interface:config system acme unset interface endThe GUI should become accessible immediately after removing the interface setting.Permanent

incidents.title: CSRF validation error, SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains
incidents.summary: Description An issue where users encounter a CSRF validation error when authenticating via SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains, such as Microsoft 365. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution When a user attempts to authenticate using a federated domain (for example, Microsoft 365) via the FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP Proxy, the process fails. The user is redirected from the identity provider back to the FortiAuthenticator endpoint /saml-idp-proxy/ and receives the following error message: Request failed CSRF validation: CSRF cookie not set.
incidents.symptom: An issue where users encounter a CSRF validation error when authenticating via SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains, such as Microsoft 365
incidents.solution: When a user attempts to authenticate using a federated domain (for example, Microsoft 365) via the FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP Proxy, the process fails. The user is redirected from the identity provider back to the FortiAuthenticator endpoint /saml-idp-proxy/ and receives the following error message: Request failed CSRF validation: CSRF cookie not set. Refresh your browser and try again. This is a known issue in FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10 and 8.0.3 which causes the system to fail to set the required CSRF token cookie during the SAML redirection process. When the browser performs the subsequent POST request to the login endpoint, the validation fails because the expected CSRF cookie is missing from the request headers. Resolution is to upgrade FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.11, 8.0.4 or higher. This issue is resolved in firmware version 6.6.11 and 8.0.4. Internal engineering ticket ID is 1325777. incidents.title: FortiSASE secure edge tunnel stays down after a FortiOS upgrade because of a Diffie-Hellman group mismatch
incidents.summary: DescriptionFortiGate secure edge tunnel to FortiSASE stops negotiating after the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5, why the tunnel comes up when the Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups are set to 5 and 14 and then drops again with the groups back at 20 and 21, and how to fix the condition permanently.This article also explains why the tunnel settings on FortiManager are not the source of truth for this tunnel, and how to make the workaround persist on FortiOS builds that do not contain the code fix.ScopeFortiGate configured as a FortiSASE secure edge,…
incidents.symptom: FortiGate secure edge tunnel to FortiSASE stops negotiating after the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5, why the tunnel comes up when the Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups are set to 5 and 14 and then drops again with the groups back at 20 and 21, and how to fix the condition permanently.This article also explains why the tunnel settings on FortiManager are not the source of truth for this tunnel, and how to make the workaround persist on FortiOS builds that do not contain the code fix
incidents.solution: SymptomA FortiGate operating as a FortiSASE secure edge has a VDOM, commonly named SASE, configured for LAN extension. The tunnel to the FortiSASE edge service is not created by an administrator. FortiOS creates and maintains it automatically, under a phase 1 interface named with the prefix ul-, for example ul-npu0_vlink1, and the interface carries the description "[fgconn] Do NOT edit. Automatically generated by extension controller".After the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5 or 7.6.6, the tunnel no longer establishes. The VPN logs show a large number of IKEv2 phase 1 proposals sent to the FortiSASE peer with no answer, each cycle ending in a negotiation timeout. The responder cookie in those log entries is all zeroes, which means the peer never replied. FortiOS creates and maintains it automatically, under a phase 1 interface named with the prefix ul-, for example ul-npu0_vlink1, and the interface carries the description "[fgconn] Do NOT edit. Automatically generated by extension controller".After the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5 or 7.6.6, the tunnel no longer establishes. incidents.title: High packet drops occur during traffic bursts on a FortiGate VM hosted in Google Cloud Platform
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the case when a FortiGate VM hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experiences significant packet loss and latency during high bursts of traffic. While interface-level counters do not show RX drops, the internal RX queue statistics indicate drops.ScopeFortiGate VM, GCP.SolutionThe issue is caused by RX queue buffer exhaustion. When the GCP instance presents only one RX queue, the ring buffer descriptors are exhausted during traffic bursts, leading to packet drops.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the case when a FortiGate VM hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experiences significant packet loss and latency during high bursts of traffic. While interface-level counters do not show RX drops, the internal RX queue statistics indicate drops
incidents.solution: The issue is caused by RX queue buffer exhaustion. When the GCP instance presents only one RX queue, the ring buffer descriptors are exhausted during traffic bursts, leading to packet drops. This occurs even if the CPU utilization is not high, as the bottleneck is at the NIC descriptor level rather than the CPU processing level.The following command will list the interface counters. incidents.title: FortiManager user session disconnection issues when using Cloudflare ZTNA
incidents.summary: Description When administrators access the FortiManager GUI via Cloudflare ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access), the login session may automatically terminate or disconnect roughly 30 seconds after logging in. This typically occurs because proxy routing, load-balancing, or edge POP switches cause minor fluctuations in the client's apparent source IP address, triggering session security validation failures on the FortiManager side.
incidents.symptom: When administrators access the FortiManager GUI via Cloudflare ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access), the login session may automatically terminate or disconnect roughly 30 seconds after logging in. This typically occurs because proxy routing, load-balancing, or edge POP switches cause minor fluctuations in the client's apparent source IP address, triggering session security validation failures on the FortiManager side
incidents.solution: To resolve this issue, you need to configure FortiManager to bypass strict source IP validation checks for active sessions. Log in to the FortiManager CLI as an administrator and execute the following commands: config system global set skip-ip-check-in-session enable end Once this setting is enabled, FortiManager will ignore intermediate source IP modifications or fluctuations during an active session, allowing Cloudflare ZTNA users to maintain a stable, uninterrupted connection to the GUI. incidents.title: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number
incidents.summary: Description FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices. Scope FortiPAM, FortiClient EMS. Solution Devices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number.
incidents.symptom: FortiPAM retrieves an incorrect FortiClient EMS serial number for synchronized tags, preventing ZTNA access for tagged devices
incidents.solution: Devices with assigned tags in FortiClient EMS cannot access FortiPAM via ZTNA. The tags synchronized from FortiClient EMS to FortiPAM are associated with an incorrect serial number that does not match the actual FortiClient EMS console serial number. Root Cause FortiPAM retrieves the default tenant serial number instead of the specific tenant serial number in multi-tenant FortiClient EMS environments. This is identified as BUG 1343587. Permanent Fix Update FortiClient EMS to version 7.4.9 or later Contournement : Perform the following steps to clear the invalid tags and refresh the synchronization: Clear the invalid tags associated with the incorrect serial number by running the following command on FortiPAM: diagnose endpoint tags remove-by-sn Restart the fabric connector daemon to refresh the data: diag test app fcnacd 99 Verify that the tags are synchronized with the correct serial number using the following commands: diagnose test application fcnacd 2 diagnose test application fcnacd 7 Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? incidents.title: Unable to delete the default admin account after migration to AHV
incidents.summary: Description An issue where the default admin account cannot be deleted from FortiManager after migration to a Nutanix AHV environment. incidents.title: Slow dynamic VLAN assignment when using 802.1X and MAC authentication bypass
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a delay in transitioning a FortiSwitch port to the configured Guest VLAN after a RADIUS server rejects an authentication request. Changing the authentication priority in the 802.1X security policy can help reduce the delay
incidents.solution: SymptomsWhen a device connects to a FortiSwitch port configured for 802.1X and MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB), the port may take approximately one minute to transition from the default VLAN to the configured Guest VLAN after the RADIUS server returns an Access-Reject response.In comparison, when the RADIUS server returns an Access-Accept response, authentication and network access are typically completed much faster.Root CauseThe delay may be related to the authentication priority configured in the 802.1X security policy. When the priority is set to "legacy", the switch may take longer to process the authentication sequence and transition to the Guest VLAN following an authentication failure.ResolutionStep 1: Update the Authentication Priority.Log in to the FortiGate CLI and change the authentication priority from "legacy" to "dot1x-mab" in the applicable 802.1X security policy.config switch-controller security-policy 802-1X edit " " set auth-priority dot1x-mab next endReplace with the name of the applicable 802.1X security policy.This setting prioritizes 802.1X and MAB authentication according to the configured authentication sequence and may reduce the time required to transitio

incidents.title: RADIUS attributes of users cleared during CSV file import
incidents.summary: Description Importing users via a CSV file with the 'Keep existing user accounts' option enabled may clear RADIUS attributes of existing accounts and prevent user authentication. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution RADIUS attributes of users that are not in the CSV file are deleted after importing a new CSV file. When performing a bulk user import via CSV in FortiAuthenticator, selecting Advanced Options -> Keep existing user accounts clears the 'Certificate Binding' attribute for some existing user accounts.
incidents.symptom: Importing users via a CSV file with the 'Keep existing user accounts' option enabled may clear RADIUS attributes of existing accounts and prevent user authentication
incidents.solution: RADIUS attributes of users that are not in the CSV file are deleted after importing a new CSV file. When performing a bulk user import via CSV in FortiAuthenticator, selecting Advanced Options -> Keep existing user accounts clears the 'Certificate Binding' attribute for some existing user accounts. Affected users lose authentication access. Issue 1-a: Importing a local user CSV file wipes user-bound RADIUS attributes. Issue 1-b: Certificates of users that are not in the CSV file are deleted. Issue 2: CSV Export does not include certificates of type 'Trusted CA'. Issue 3: CSV Export confuses local and remote users with the same ID. These are known issues tracked under the engineering ticket ID 1208720. See: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 Release Notes . Reported firmware version: 6.6.6 Resolution: Upgrade FortiAuthenticator to a version where the issue is resolved. The fix is available in the following versions: FortiAuthenticator 6.6.8 FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2

incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a known issue affecting FortiGate G-Series devices where downgrading or upgrading from v8.0.1 to v8.0.x via the GUI fails, displaying the error status 'Upgrade Failed'.ScopeFortiGate G-Series devices running FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245.SolutionExample error: During the firmware upgrade attempt, the device status may display the following:Steps to replicate the issue: Log in to a FortiGate G-Series device running FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245 (Feature).Attempt to upgrade the firmware to FortiOS v8.0.2 using the online…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue affecting FortiGate G-Series devices where downgrading or upgrading from v8.0.1 to v8.0.x via the GUI fails, displaying the error status 'Upgrade Failed'
incidents.solution: Example error: During the firmware upgrade attempt, the device status may display the following:Steps to replicate the issue: Log in to a FortiGate G-Series device running FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245 (Feature).Attempt to upgrade the firmware to FortiOS v8.0.2 using the online upgrade method via FortiGate Cloud or the GUI.Observe that the firmware upgrade fails. The device status displays 'Online - Upgrade failed', and the Upgrade Status displays 'Upgrade failed'. In some instances, the device status may show 'Rebooting with new firmware', while the Upgrade Status displays 'Firmware info unavailable'.Check the console output and observe the following messages:Image verification OK! Failed to get the image encryption key!Retry the firmware upgrade by manually uploading the FortiOS v8.0.2 firmware image through the GUI. The upgrade fails again.Verify that the device remains on FortiOS v8.0.1 build 0245 Contournement : Upgrade the firmware using TFTP via the CLI. Refer to the following guide for the upgrade procedure:Technical Tip: FortiGate TFTP Upgrade Permanent fix:This issue is scheduled to be fixed in FortiOS v8.0.3 build 0270

incidents.title: FortiManager policy package import error "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device". Scope FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following: The Download Import Report shows as following: "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)"…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot and fix an import error issue when it shows "Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device"
incidents.solution: When FortiManager import policy package from FortiGate shows fails as following: The Download Import Report shows as following: "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-IP-BlockList1, oid=2634, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" "system external-resource",FAIL,"(name=TL-BlockURL_IP_Group1, oid=2636, reason=invalid value. object: sys_external_resource. detail: Can not copy password attribute password from private key encrypted device)" What happened is FortiManager being unable to copy the password from system external-resource due to it being encrypted. To solve the issue, disable the "private-data-encrytion" in Device Manager -> Device & Groups -> select the FortiGate -> CLI Configurations -> System -> Global. After changing the setting, FortiManager's Import Configuration does not fail anymore. incidents.title: FortiGate 201G upgrade from FortiOS version 8.0.1 to FortiOS version 8.0.2 fails during reboot

incidents.title: Copilot is not usable after an upgrade to version 7.6.8 while the Explicit Proxy is in use
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.8+.SolutionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499.
incidents.symptom: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked
incidents.solution: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499. If on these versions, refer to this article instead:Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving Microsoft Copilot access issues with FortiGate inspecting traffic with a policy in proxy-mode and Application Control/IPS.If being on version 7.6.8 and have this issue, check the Forward Traffic logs filtered to the user's source IP. The following log may be visible:The traffic is being allowed by UTM, but denied by the proxy due to 'traffic denied because uri too long'. The maximum length of a request for an Explicit Proxy is defined by 'max-request-length', and this message will be seen when the proxy blocks the request due to exceeding this limit.The following commands can be used to change this limit:config web-proxy profile set max-request-length 64 endOnce this value is changed to the maximum, the traffic is allowed

incidents.title: FortiManager Policy Package install fails with verification error due to "antiphish: max-body-len" parameter
incidents.summary: Description An issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the " antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles. Scope FortiManager and FortiProxy 7.4.9 and higher, FortiProxy 7.6.1 and higher Solution When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification…
incidents.symptom: An issue where FortiManager Policy Package installation fails with a verification error due to the " antiphish: max-body-len" parameter under webfilter profiles
incidents.solution: When installing a Policy Package from FortiManager to FortiProxy 7.4.9, the installation fails with verification messages similar to the following: (vdom root: webfilter profile "monitor-all" antiphish:max-body-len) remote original: to be installed: 65536 <--- done generating verification report install failed The same message may be reported for multiple webfilter profiles. The root cause is a difference in the default value of the max-body-len parameter between FortiProxy and FortiManager. Starting with FortiProxy 7.4.9 and 7.6.1, the default value of max-body-len was changed from 65535 to 1024 . However, FortiManager continues to use 65535 as the default value for this parameter. This difference in default values can result in installation verification failure in FortiManager. To work around the issue, configure FortiManager to use the optimal installation verification mode: config system dm set verify-install optimal end Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? incidents.title: Upgrade firmware fails with 'New image is too big'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error 'New image is too big '. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer. Solution Typically, this error occurs during a FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager 8.0.X firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image. This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: "New image is too big”.
incidents.symptom: This article describes troubleshooting steps for issues related to the error 'New image is too big '
incidents.solution: Typically, this error occurs during a FortiAnalyzer or FortiManager 8.0.X firmware update when the target device lacks sufficient flash memory storage to accommodate the new firmware image. This is most commonly documented for FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer VM platforms, where the error message reads: "New image is too big”. This known issue, tracked with the ID 1329518 in the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer Known Issues , is not a bug but a system requirement to upgrade the products to the newest and bigger firmware releases Most common causes: Insufficient flash disk space : The flash partition does not have enough free space to store the new firmware image during the upgrade process. Small virtual disk allocation : The VM was originally provisioned with a flash disk that is too small for the target firmware version. Diagnostic steps: Take the firmware update from version 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 for FortiAnalyzer VM as an example. Check flash disk usage: Run the following command on the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer CLI to view the flash disk size and current usage: diagnose system flash list Example output showing the flash disk status: ImageName Version TotalSize(KB) Used(KB) Use% BootImage Running

incidents.title: FortiManager to FortiGate policy install fails with a custom protocol error
incidents.summary: Description Troubleshooting steps for a custom protocol error that occurs when performing a policy installation to FortiGate. Scope FortiManager. Solution The following issue may be encountered by users when performing policy installation to FortiGate v7.6 to a v7.4 ADOM in FortiManager. This issue occurs because the protocol types defined in the default firewall service objects differ between ADOM versions. For example, in v7.4, the default protocol for the DNS service is TCP/UDP/SCTP , whereas in v7.6, it has been updated to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP .
incidents.symptom: Troubleshooting steps for a custom protocol error that occurs when performing a policy installation to FortiGate
incidents.solution: The following issue may be encountered by users when performing policy installation to FortiGate v7.6 to a v7.4 ADOM in FortiManager. This issue occurs because the protocol types defined in the default firewall service objects differ between ADOM versions. For example, in v7.4, the default protocol for the DNS service is TCP/UDP/SCTP , whereas in v7.6, it has been updated to TCP/UDP/UDP-Lite/SCTP . To resolve this issue, upgrade the ADOM to v7.6 so that the default firewall service object definitions in FortiManager align with those on the FortiGate. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FSSO group lookup fails because of LDAP search 'Timed out' in 5 seconds, ignoring timeout settings
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a known issue in FortiAuthenticator where an LDAP search for users fails due to a 'Timed out' error within 5 seconds, regardless of configured timeout settings. For this reason, FortiAuthenticator fails to perform group lookup, and users are missing in FSSO sessions. Scope FortiAuthenticator, LDAP, FSSO. Solution This issue has occurred in cases where FSSO sessions are missing, and users were unable to access both internal and external resources because the firewall policies were configured based on user groups.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue in FortiAuthenticator where an LDAP search for users fails due to a 'Timed out' error within 5 seconds, regardless of configured timeout settings. For this reason, FortiAuthenticator fails to perform group lookup, and users are missing in FSSO sessions
incidents.solution: This issue has occurred in cases where FSSO sessions are missing, and users were unable to access both internal and external resources because the firewall policies were configured based on user groups. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCEP decryption failure with aes-256-cbc encryption
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the cause of SCEP decryption failures on FortiAuthenticator when receiving enrollment requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc from certain third-party devices. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiManager, FortiGate. Solution When a third-party device uses aes-256-cbc encryption for SCEP enrollment requests, FortiAuthenticator may fail to decrypt the PKCS#7 enveloped data. This results in a decryption failure during the SCEP process.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the cause of SCEP decryption failures on FortiAuthenticator when receiving enrollment requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc from certain third-party devices
incidents.solution: When a third-party device uses aes-256-cbc encryption for SCEP enrollment requests, FortiAuthenticator may fail to decrypt the PKCS#7 enveloped data. This results in a decryption failure during the SCEP process. Root cause: The issue is caused by a compatibility problem in how FortiAuthenticator handles SCEP requests encrypted with aes-256-cbc. While other encryption methods like des-ede3-cbc work correctly, requests using aes-256-cbc trigger a decryption error in the SCEP daemon. Symptoms: The following error messages appear in the FortiAuthenticator debug logs: PKCS7 message encrypted with aes-256-cbc (427) utils.cpp:386: decryption failed mo_pkcs7unwrap.cpp:526: cannot decrypt PKCS#7 enveloped data error:1C800064:Provider routines:ossl_cipher_unpadblock:bad decrypt Resolution: This is a known issue tracked under engineering ticket 1198353 and is expected to be resolved in an upcoming FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 GA release. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Intermediate CA cannot be exported as PKCS#12 on FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the reason why, on FortiAuthenticator 6.6.10, exporting an intermediate CA certificate with its private key in PKCS#12 format fails with the error 'Cannot export PKCS#12 certificate' . Scope FortiAuthenticator 6.6.10. Solution The issue occurs when an intermediate CA is created using a root CA that is hosted on the FortiAuthenticator. When attempting to export the intermediate CA together with its private key and a password in PKCS#12 format, the export fails.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the reason why, on FortiAuthenticator 6.6.10, exporting an intermediate CA certificate with its private key in PKCS#12 format fails with the error 'Cannot export PKCS#12 certificate'
incidents.solution: The issue occurs when an intermediate CA is created using a root CA that is hosted on the FortiAuthenticator. When attempting to export the intermediate CA together with its private key and a password in PKCS#12 format, the export fails. Cannot export PKCS#12 certificate: failed to extract enum CertificateOrPKCS12Certificate ('Certificate | PKCS12Certificate') - variant Certificate (Certificate): TypeError: failed to extract field CertificateOrPKCS12Certificate::Certificate.0, caused by TypeError: 'X509' object is not an instance of 'Certificate' - variant PKCS12Certificate (PKCS12Certificate): TypeError: failed to extract field CertificateOrPKCS12Certificate::PKCS12Certificate.0, caused by TypeError: 'X509' object is not an instance of 'PKCS12Certificate' This issue is tracked under engineering ticket 1322845 . The fix is expected to be included in the following FortiAuthenticator releases: FortiAuthenticator 6.6.11 FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 Upgrade FortiAuthenticator to a release containing the fix when available. incidents.title: Technical Tip: Unable to receive authentication code via SMS
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the procedure for sending an authentication code through SMS when the user reports that the authentication code message was not received. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If the SMS gateway message template is configured with the variable {{:token_code}} , but users receive a message without the OTP code, such as: "Your OTP login is . Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP." This indicates that the token code placeholder is not being substituted with the generated authentication code , resulting in a blank…
incidents.symptom: This article describes the procedure for sending an authentication code through SMS when the user reports that the authentication code message was not received
incidents.solution: If the SMS gateway message template is configured with the variable {{:token_code}} , but users receive a message without the OTP code, such as: "Your OTP login is . Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP." This indicates that the token code placeholder is not being substituted with the generated authentication code , resulting in a blank value in the SMS content. If the OTP code is missing when using the {{:token_code}} variable, modify the SMS gateway message template to: Your OTP login is {{:message}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. After updating the template, the authentication code will be included correctly in the SMS message delivered to the user. Configure the SMS gateway replacement message as shown below: Plain Text Your OTP login is {{:token_code}}. Valid for 3 minutes. Do not share the OTP. Show more lines The {{:token_code}} placeholder will be replaced with the generated OTP, ensuring that users receive the authentication code in the SMS message. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SCIM user and group synchronization failure between FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate
incidents.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve an issue where users and groups do not synchronize from FortiAuthenticator to FortiGate despite a successful TLS connection. Scope FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator. Solution When FortiAuthenticator acts as a SCIM client and FortiGate acts as a SCIM server, the synchronization of users and groups may fail if the base URL is configured incorrectly. Even if the TLS connection is established, the FortiGate SCIM daemon may fail to associate the incoming request with the configured SCIM client.
incidents.symptom: This article explains how to resolve an issue where users and groups do not synchronize from FortiAuthenticator to FortiGate despite a successful TLS connection
incidents.solution: When FortiAuthenticator acts as a SCIM client and FortiGate acts as a SCIM server, the synchronization of users and groups may fail if the base URL is configured incorrectly. Even if the TLS connection is established, the FortiGate SCIM daemon may fail to associate the incoming request with the configured SCIM client. The issue occurs when the base-url in the FortiGate SCIM configuration includes a port number. The base URI should typically consist of the protocol, domain name, and initial path. Including the port number in the base-url prevents the FortiGate from correctly identifying the SCIM client, resulting in the following debug error: diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application scim -1 diagnose debug enable url:https://10.5.146.127/scim/v2/Users/user_2 HTTP/1.1 used to find client:NULL. can't found client or client disabled. change state from wait_req to disconnect change state from disconnect to done change state from init to accepting change state from accepting to connect SSL_accept succeeded. Resolution Log in to the FortiGate command line interface. Verify the current SCIM configuration to check for a port number in the base-url: show user scim Remove the port numbe

incidents.title: Technical Tip: Clarification of the 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in FSSO debug log when Entra ID is being used
incidents.summary: Description This article clarifies the error log message 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in the FSSO debug log in the FortiAuthenticator when Entra ID is being used and remote LDAP is not configured. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution FortiAuthenticator FSSO supports logon events from native Microsoft Entra ID-joined workstations through the FortiClient SSOMA (FortiClient Single Sign-On Mobility Agent).
incidents.symptom: This article clarifies the error log message 'cannot get DNS name of domain x.x.x.x from Domain Manager' in the FSSO debug log in the FortiAuthenticator when Entra ID is being used and remote LDAP is not configured
incidents.solution: FortiAuthenticator FSSO supports logon events from native Microsoft Entra ID-joined workstations through the FortiClient SSOMA (FortiClient Single Sign-On Mobility Agent). For example, when an endpoint joined to Microsoft Entra ID connects to the network, FortiClient SSOMA sends the user identity and endpoint IP address to FortiAuthenticator. FortiAuthenticator then performs a group membership lookup against Microsoft Entra ID through the OAuth API and shares the retrieved Entra ID group membership information with the FortiGate. The configuration example can be found in the following document: FortiAuthenticator SSOMA for native Microsoft Entra ID joined workstation In a normal scenario, the following FSSO debug messages can be observed at 'https:// /debug/fsso-agent/' when FortiAuthenticator processes the SSOMA logon event and performs the Entra ID group membership lookup through the OAuth API: 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FortiClient connected: 2540D4605FDD4FB125FD1B532DECD268/192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] Received 1 event(s) from FCT: 192.168.1.20 08/05/2026 10:50:23 [9DC456C0] FCT LOGON 2026-02-10-10:50:23/1970-01-01-10:00:00 FortiClient (null):L2003.TESTDOMAIN

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Authentication Failure for Administrator Role Users After Upgrading FortiAuthenticator
incidents.summary: Description This article describes an issue where administrator role users are unable to authenticate after upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.6.2 to 6.6.10, while other users can log in successfully. The issue is related to CHAP authentication. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution If an administrator-role user is unable to authenticate through SSL VPN after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10, recreate the affected user account in FortiAuthenticator and reassign the FortiToken.
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue where administrator role users are unable to authenticate after upgrading FortiAuthenticator from version 6.6.2 to 6.6.10, while other users can log in successfully. The issue is related to CHAP authentication
incidents.solution: If an administrator-role user is unable to authenticate through SSL VPN after upgrading FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.10, recreate the affected user account in FortiAuthenticator and reassign the FortiToken. Perform the following steps: Delete the affected administrator user from FortiAuthenticator. Re-import the user from the configured LDAP server. Reassign the FortiToken to the newly imported user. Test SSL VPN authentication with the affected user. After completing these steps, the user should be able to authenticate successfully through SSL VPN. This procedure can be used as a workaround when only specific administrator-role users are affected following the FortiAuthenticator upgrade. incidents.title: Technical Tip: How to fix BdsDxe : failed to load Boot0001 UEFI NUTANUX VDISK in Nutanix Environment
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a failed deployment of a FortiAnalyzer instance when performing VM migrations from VMware (ESXi) to Nutanix. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution Error: Reason: Wrong boot mode selection: FortiAnalyzer firmware images have strict requirements regarding the hypervisor BIOS type. The boot disk is attached to the wrong bus: FortiAnalyzer images expect the virtual disk to be mapped correctly so the bootloader can initialize.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a failed deployment of a FortiAnalyzer instance when performing VM migrations from VMware (ESXi) to Nutanix
incidents.solution: Error: Reason: Wrong boot mode selection: FortiAnalyzer firmware images have strict requirements regarding the hypervisor BIOS type. The boot disk is attached to the wrong bus: FortiAnalyzer images expect the virtual disk to be mapped correctly so the bootloader can initialize. Missing or unassigned secondary data: DiskFortiAnalyzer is a logging and reporting tool; it cannot function or boot correctly without a dedicated storage partition. Resolution: Change the boot mode in the Nutanix Environment: In the Nutanix Prism console, go to Update VM -> Boot Configuration -> Change the boot mode from UEFI to Legacy BIOS (or Default) . Cloned .qcow2 boot image disk: Clone the image and explicitly attach it to the SCSI bus (e.g., SCSI Index 0). Add a new disk to the instance: Create a second, empty disk on the SCSI bus (e.g., 100 GB+ depending on licensing requirements) alongside the primary boot disk

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Incorrect VLAN assignment when using FortiAuthenticator dynamic VLANs
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot incorrect VLAN assignment when FortiAuthenticator is used to return dynamic VLAN attributes in RADIUS Access-Accept messages. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution Incorrect VLAN assignment may occur when FortiAuthenticator is configured for RADIUS Authentication if the same remote LDAP user or computer object is a member of more than one Active Directory or FortiAuthenticator user group, and when each group has a different RADIUS VLAN attribute configured.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot incorrect VLAN assignment when FortiAuthenticator is used to return dynamic VLAN attributes in RADIUS Access-Accept messages
incidents.solution: Incorrect VLAN assignment may occur when FortiAuthenticator is configured for RADIUS Authentication if the same remote LDAP user or computer object is a member of more than one Active Directory or FortiAuthenticator user group, and when each group has a different RADIUS VLAN attribute configured. For example, if a user or device is a member of both the Students and the Staff group, then the FortiAuthenticator will return both VLANs to the NAC (e.g., FortiGate). Since the NAC (Network Enforcement Device, e.g. a FortiGate) can only assign 1 x VLAN, the latter of the two will be assigned to the client device, which may or may not be correct, possibly resulting in a Student being placed in the Staff VLAN (or vice versa). To troubleshoot this behaviour, check the RADIUS Access-Accept message in FortiAuthenticator's RADIUS debug (i.e. https:// /debug/radius) and confirm whether more than one VLAN is being returned. Correct example (1 x PVID is returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLAN Problem example (2 x PVIDs are returned): Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Medium-Type += IEEE-802 Tunnel-Private-Group-Id += "58" Tunnel-Type += VLA

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Incorrect user triggered for push notification
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a known issue that push notification triggers for wrong user intermittently, FortiAuthenticator debug logs show a different username being matched. The user is able to log in using the token manually, but the push notification is not being received. Scope FortiAuthenticator, FortiAuthenticator Agent. Solution For example: The user 'Emerson' is getting incorrect random Fortitoken push triggers that appear to be originating from the user 'Emer'.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue that push notification triggers for wrong user intermittently, FortiAuthenticator debug logs show a different username being matched. The user is able to log in using the token manually, but the push notification is not being received
incidents.solution: For example: The user 'Emerson' is getting incorrect random Fortitoken push triggers that appear to be originating from the user 'Emer'. If the user 'Emerson' accepts the invalid push, the reply times out in the app. In FortiAuthenticator logs, when the issue happens: the 'Emer' user shows as 'Emerson', and 'Emerson' is also an active user. See the following log. It is meant to be an entry for the 'Emer' user, but it shows as 'Emerson': 2026-06-15T16:07:42.003325-04:00 HQFAC radiusd[6015]: (53417) facauth: Updated auth log 'lab.local/Emerson' for attempt from REST API: Remote LDAP user authentication from (null) with FortiToken failed: invalid token. The issue seems to happen randomly. The user 'Emer' is able to log in using manual token entry. This is a known issue with the id 1312120 and is resolved in firmware version 8.0.4. There is a special build on v8.0.3: contact Fortinet Support to get the special build. incidents.title: Technical Tip: EAP-TLS Authentication Fails with error 'Authentication failed for EAP method type 13'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the steps to troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator. The user is experiencing issues with EAP authentication, resulting in an error message indicating that authentication failed for EAP method type 13 (EAP-TLS). This message is generic and returned by the client/supplicant whenever the TLS handshake or certificate validation fails during EAP-TLS negotiation. The actual reason must be identified from FortiAuthenticator debug logs, client-side logs, or packet captures.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the steps to troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator. The user is experiencing issues with EAP authentication, resulting in an error message indicating that authentication failed for EAP method type 13 (EAP-TLS). This message is generic and returned by the client/supplicant whenever the TLS handshake or certificate validation fails during EAP-TLS negotiation. The actual reason must be identified from FortiAuthenticator debug logs, client-side logs, or packet captures
incidents.solution: To troubleshoot EAP authentication failure on FortiAuthenticator, follow these steps: Verify CA and certificate configuration Confirm that the CA certificate is correctly configured and has the appropriate Client Authentication or Server Authentication entries under its Key Usage / Extended Key Usage list. On the FortiGate CLI, run the following command to check the configured WiFi CA and server certificate: get system global | grep wifi This will show the 'wifi-ca-certificate' and 'wifi-certificate' currently in use, allowing to confirm the correct certificates are assigned. Check the certificate chain. Ensure that the Root CA and any Intermediate CA(s) that issued the client and/or server certificates are installed and trusted: On FortiAuthenticator: under Certificate Management -> Certificate Authorities -> Trusted CAs . On the client device: In the OS/device trusted root and intermediate certificate store. A missing intermediate CA is a common cause of TLS validation failure even when the leaf certificate is valid. Verify CRL/OCSP reachability: Verify that the client can reach the CRL/OCSP endpoints. If not required, consider disabling revocation checks for testing. Investigate

incidents.summary: Description This article describes a solution to an issue where the upgrade of FortiClientEMS fails due to a Grafana package error. The upgrade from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8 results in a failed upgrade. The error message observed: Setting up grafana (13.1.1) ... mv: cannot move '/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled' to '/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled': Directory not empty dpkg: error processing package grafana (--configure): installed grafana package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 Errors were encountered while…
incidents.symptom: This article describes a solution to an issue where the upgrade of FortiClientEMS fails due to a Grafana package error. The upgrade from version 7.4.7 to 7.4.8 results in a failed upgrade. The error message observed: Setting up grafana (13.1.1) ... mv: cannot move '/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled' to '/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled': Directory not empty dpkg: error processing package grafana (--configure): installed grafana package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 1 Errors were encountered while processing: grafana dpkg configure failed. Aborting
incidents.solution: The EMS v7.4.8 upgrade includes a Grafana package update (to v13.1.1 in this case). During the package installation, the post-installation script attempts to move the bundled plugins directory from the package's default location (/usr/share/grafana/data/plugins-bundled) to the runtime data directory (/var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled). The error Directory not empty means that /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled already existed and contained files when the mv command tried to move the new bundled plugins there. Note: This is a known issue with Grafana v13.1.1: Upgrade to Grafana 13.1.1 had errors . To resolve the EMS upgrade failure due to a Grafana package error, follow these steps: Run the command to rename the plugins-bundled directory. sudo mv /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled /var/lib/grafana/plugins-bundled.bak Run the command to configure the packages. sudo dpkg --configure -a Retry the upgrade process to complete the installation of FortiClient/EMS version 7.4.8. By following these steps, the upgrade failure due to the Grafana package error should be resolved, and the FortiClientEMS upgrade should complete successfully. forticlientems Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting. It also explains the difference between NTP synchronization on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData Main Host and the Security Event Manager Controller, and why the controller may generate significantly more NTP requests than the Main Host. Scope FortiAnalyzer-BigData.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot a FortiAnalyzer-BigData firmware upgrade that fails the NTP pre-upgrade check due to NTP server rate limiting. It also explains the difference between NTP synchronization on the FortiAnalyzer-BigData Main Host and the Security Event Manager Controller, and why the controller may generate significantly more NTP requests than the Main Host
incidents.solution: Starting from FortiAnalyzer-BigData v7.2.7 , the firmware upgrade process includes an NTP preflight validation. Accurate and consistent time synchronization is important for the distributed BigData cluster. If the configured NTP server cannot be successfully validated, the firmware upgrade is blocked. A typical symptom is that NTP synchronization on the Main Host appears healthy: diagnose system ntp status MS Name/IP address Stratum Poll Reach LastRx Last sample =============================================================================== ^* ntp-server.example.com 2 9 377 301 -92us[-123us] +/- 622us However, checking NTP from the Security Event Manager Controller may intermittently fail: fazbdadm check ntp ntpdate: rate limit response from server. ntpdate: no server suitable for synchronization found [ERR] NTP server ntp-server.example.com is not valid or not reachable Running the same command again may succeed: fazbdadm check ntp server , stratum 2, offset -0.000775, delay 0.02631 adjust time server offset -0.000775 sec NTP server ntp-server.example.com is valid~ This behavior can occur when the external NTP infrastructure applies rate limiting to the Security Event Manager Cont

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Getting error message 'Error resizing disk partition' in FortiClient EMS in AWS environment
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve the issue 'Error resizing disk partition' in FortiClient EMS in an AWS environment. Scope FortiClient EMS v7.4 onwards in an AWS environment. Solution When FortiClient EMS is deployed in an AWS environment, run the command below to expand disk space: execute lvm expand-disk --disk.name nvme0n1 It shows the error: 'Error resizing disk partition: exit status 5'. Solution : This is currently a known issue when FortiClient EMS is deployed in an AWS environment specifically.

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient EMS SAML Authentication Failure when FortiClient shows a 'Server encountered an error, please try again later' message
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot SAML authentication issues in FortiClient EMS when FortiClient shows a ' Server encountered an error, please try again later ' message during user authentication. In this scenario, users are unable to register FortiClient with FortiClient EMS using an invitation code because the SAML authentication process fails. Scope FortiClient EMS. FortiGate. Solution If users encounter a server error when authenticating with SAML, perform the following checks: In FortiClient EMS , navigate to User Management…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot SAML authentication issues in FortiClient EMS when FortiClient shows a ' Server encountered an error, please try again later ' message during user authentication. In this scenario, users are unable to register FortiClient with FortiClient EMS using an invitation code because the SAML authentication process fails
incidents.solution: If users encounter a server error when authenticating with SAML, perform the following checks: In FortiClient EMS , navigate to User Management -> SAML Configuration and edit the affected SAML profile. Verify the Service Provider (SP) certificate configured in the SAML profile. Ensure the certificate is a server certificate . Do not use a wildcard certificate, as it may prevent the SAML signing key from loading correctly. If necessary, temporarily remove the configured SP certificate and test the authentication again to determine whether the certificate is the source of the issue. Review the FortiClient EMS diagnostic logs for SAML-related errors. In particular, examine the following FortiClient EMS log file: python_logs/debug_ - - A common indication of this issue is the following error: xmlsec.Error: (1, 'cannot load key') This error typically indicates that FortiClient EMS is unable to load the private key associated with the configured SP certificate. After correcting the certificate configuration, retry the FortiClient registration using the invitation code. For additional information about configuring SAML authentication, refer to SAML Configuration . Like 2 Reply Follow Shar

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: 'error restore dbs' when restoring FortiClient EMS standalone database file (non-docker) to HA (docker)
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve the issue 'error restore dbs' when restoring the FortiClient EMS standalone database file (non-Docker) to HA (Docker). Scope FortiClient EMS v7.4 onwards. Current FortiClient EMS setup: Standalone, non-Docker. Target FortiClient EMS setup: FortiClient EMS HA setup with Docker. Solution Issue descriptions: Take a copy of the database file from a standalone FortiClient EMS non-Docker.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to resolve the issue 'error restore dbs' when restoring the FortiClient EMS standalone database file (non-Docker) to HA (Docker)
incidents.solution: Issue descriptions: Take a copy of the database file from a standalone FortiClient EMS non-Docker. Attempt to restore the database file to a FortiClient EMS HA setup with Docker. The restore process stopped exactly at 21% and then failed with the following error message: error restore dbs: restoreDB: restoring from dir: building filtered TOC: reading TOC from /opt/forticlientems/data/upload/dbbackup/sites/fcm_default: exit status 1 Solution : Go to the current FortiClient EMS dashboard -> Backup database . For Compression Type, make sure to select 'Database' type. Select the 'Back Up' button and save the backup file. Go to the target primary FortiClient EMS and restore the database file saved in step 3. The restore process will now continue after 21%, and should be successful. Note : In general, when taking a database backup file, always choose 'Database' compression type, unless it is explicitly requested by Fortinet TAC. forticlientems EMS FortiClient EMS fctems Like Reply Follow Share Powered by Gainsight Terms & Conditions Cookie settings Accessibility statement Sign up Already have an account? incidents.title: Technical Tip: Resolving an upgrade failed error during FortiClient EMS update caused by the Microsoft SQL Server Express database reaching size limit
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve the Setup Failed error 0x80070643 during a FortiClient EMS v7.2 upgrade. Scope FortiClient EMS v7.2 On-Premises using Microsoft SQL. Solution During the upgrade from FortiClient EMS v7.2.12 to v7.2.13 or v7.2.14, the installer may fail with the error Setup Failed and code 0x80070643. In the installer logs, the following SQL error may be observed: Could not allocate a new page for database 'FCM_default' because the 'PRIMARY' filegroup is full due to lack of storage space or database files reaching the…
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to resolve the Setup Failed error 0x80070643 during a FortiClient EMS v7.2 upgrade
incidents.solution: During the upgrade from FortiClient EMS v7.2.12 to v7.2.13 or v7.2.14, the installer may fail with the error Setup Failed and code 0x80070643. In the installer logs, the following SQL error may be observed: Could not allocate a new page for database 'FCM_default' because the 'PRIMARY' filegroup is full due to lack of storage space or database files reaching the maximum allowed size. This behavior is consistent with the Microsoft SQL Server Express database reaching its 10 GB size limit. To validate the database size, check the .mdf files in the following path: C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL12.FCEMS\MSSQL\DATA\ Before applying any change, create an EMS backup from EMS -> Dashboard -> Backup . incidents.title: Technical Tip: FortiGate unable to sending log to FortiAnalyzer when FIPS-CC enable
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the case where, when FIPS-CC mode is enabled on the FortiGate, the device is unable to send logs to FortiAnalyzer. Scope FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate, FIPS-CC. Solution When FortiGate enables FIPS-CC mode, the OFTP is unable to establish. From FortiGate, the connection status is UP. While from FortiAnalyzer, there is no authorized device pop-up notification. The packet capture showed that the FortiGate reset the connection.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the case where, when FIPS-CC mode is enabled on the FortiGate, the device is unable to send logs to FortiAnalyzer
incidents.solution: When FortiGate enables FIPS-CC mode, the OFTP is unable to establish. From FortiGate, the connection status is UP. While from FortiAnalyzer, there is no authorized device pop-up notification. The packet capture showed that the FortiGate reset the connection. To successfully send logs from a FIPS-CC-enabled FortiGate to FortiAnalyzer using OFTP, both devices must use custom certificates signed by the same Certificate Authority (CA). config system certificate oftp set mode custom set certificate set private key end However, there is another option that can be done from FortiAnalyzer, which is to enable the FIPS-CC mode. To enable the FIPS-CC mode: config system fips set status enable set entropy-token enable end Enabling the FIPS-CC mode would delete all the config and logs; the command must be run at the console. Once the FIPS-CC has been enabled from the FortiAnalyzer side, the new FortiGate needs to be authorized to enable the FIPS-CC mode. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Maps not loading in FortiAnalyzer GUI and returning 'Internal Server Error'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a possible reason for the Google Maps frames in FortiAnalyzer not loading and instead returning 'Internal Server Error'. The example below is from Device Manager, but the same can occur in FortiView and other pages using Google Maps overlays. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution As mentioned in the article Technical Tip: How to resolve map server connectivity issue , FortiAnalyzer requires access to mapserver.fortinet.com .
incidents.symptom: This article describes a possible reason for the Google Maps frames in FortiAnalyzer not loading and instead returning 'Internal Server Error'. The example below is from Device Manager, but the same can occur in FortiView and other pages using Google Maps overlays
incidents.solution: As mentioned in the article Technical Tip: How to resolve map server connectivity issue , FortiAnalyzer requires access to mapserver.fortinet.com . To allow the communication, the map server requires the FortiAnalyzer to present a Fortinet-issued embedded certificate, having a CN value matching the FortiAnalyzer Serial Number. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Cannot restore backup from one FortiClient EMS server to another FortiClient EMS server migration in version 7.2
incidents.summary: Description This article describes Issues that can be faced when migrating from one windows server 2016 to another windows server 2022 using FortiClient EMS on-premise for version 7.2. Scope FortiClient EMS on-premise. Solution When loading FortiClient EMS on-premise backup database to a new server (backup from windows server 2016 to windows server 2022 ) the restore may failed. This issue can be related to FCM logical name may already be incorrect, It’s something Microsoft SQL Server creates automatically during a restore, and it usually signals a…
incidents.symptom: This article describes Issues that can be faced when migrating from one windows server 2016 to another windows server 2022 using FortiClient EMS on-premise for version 7.2
incidents.solution: When loading FortiClient EMS on-premise backup database to a new server (backup from windows server 2016 to windows server 2022 ) the restore may failed. This issue can be related to FCM logical name may already be incorrect, It’s something Microsoft SQL Server creates automatically during a restore, and it usually signals a file/filegroup conflict. To avoid database restore issues, it is recommended restart the FCEMS_Monitor service after waiting for 10 minutes after the restore is finished on the new windows server. If issues persist, get a database backup from an old server (windows server 2016 for example) and open a ticket (see Customer Service Tip: How to create a ticket for Fortinet TAC ) for further troubleshooting. incidents.title: Technical Tip: FortiClient EMS cannot generate a digitally self-signed FortiClient exe installer
incidents.summary: Description This article describes why FortiClient EMS cannot generate a digitally self-signed FortiClient exe installer. Scope FortiClient EMS v7.4 onwards Solution When the end user manually runs a FortiClient exe installer in an attempt to upgrade FortiClient version, Windows Microsoft Defender SmartScreen will pop-up below message: The user will have to select 'Run anyway ' to upgrade FortiClient. Below is the reason why FortiClient EMS can never self-sign a FortiClient exe installer: Private key security risk.
incidents.symptom: This article describes why FortiClient EMS cannot generate a digitally self-signed FortiClient exe installer
incidents.solution: When the end user manually runs a FortiClient exe installer in an attempt to upgrade FortiClient version, Windows Microsoft Defender SmartScreen will pop-up below message: The user will have to select 'Run anyway ' to upgrade FortiClient. Below is the reason why FortiClient EMS can never self-sign a FortiClient exe installer: Private key security risk. The signing certificate private key must be stored on the FortiClient EMS server. In the event where the server itself is compromised, the bad actor will be able to obtain the software's private key and use it to sign their malware as 'trusted and made by Fortinet'. To avoid this pop-up message from appearing, it is possible to upload the company's own digital certificate to sign the FortiClient EMS-packaged FortiClient exe installer. Go to System Settings -> EMS Settings -> Sign Software Packages -> toggle ON. Input the timestamp server FQDN or IP, upload the Certificate -> Save . For the existing FortiClient installer, edit the installer in any way to repackage it. The repackaged installer will be signed by the certificate uploaded in step 3. aiReview.solution: Lorsqu'un utilisateur exécute manuellement le programme d'installation pour mettre à niveau FortiClient, Microsoft Defender SmartScreen affiche un message nécessitant de sélectionner 'Exécuter quand même'. Cela est dû au risque lié à la clé privée, qui doit être stockée sur le serveur FortiClient EMS. Pour éviter cet affichage, il est possible de charger le certificat numérique de l'entreprise pour signer le paquet : aller dans Paramètres système -> Paramètres EMS -> Signer les paquets logiciels -> activer, saisir le FQDN ou l'IP du serveur d'horodatage, charger le certificat puis enregistrer.

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiAnalyzer log retention days showing incorrect value
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a situation where the FortiAnalyzer log retention days show an incorrect value. Scope FortiAnalyzer. Solution Context : Despite being configured to retain logs for 365 days, the user experiences an issue where the FortiAnalyzer is showing a higher number of retention days than expected. Currently, the days of archive files retained is 492 and the configured days in-policy are 365 days.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a situation where the FortiAnalyzer log retention days show an incorrect value
incidents.solution: Context : Despite being configured to retain logs for 365 days, the user experiences an issue where the FortiAnalyzer is showing a higher number of retention days than expected. Currently, the days of archive files retained is 492 and the configured days in-policy are 365 days. Configured days in retention policy: To resolve the issue of incorrect log retention days on the FortiAnalyzer, follow these steps: Go to System Settings -> ADOMs -> View Storage Info to check the current log retention settings. Check the logview -> logs -> Logbrowse section to see if there are any logs that are older than the configured retention period. Use the logbrowse feature to filter logs by date and identify any logs that are causing the incorrect retention days to be displayed. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to solve the problem on FortiAnalyzer when PostgresSQL stuck during upgrade
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to solve the problem during FortiAnalyzer upgrade. Scope FortiAnalyzer v7.2.x, v7.4x, v7.6.x. Solution When trying to upgrade FortiAnalyzer, PostgresSQL maybe stuck at 41% with a console alert 'fail to upgrade postgres'. diagnose sql status upgrade-db Upgrading log SQL database 41%, stage: [Upgrade] started at: Tue Jul 1 17:09:18 2025 This is happening when trying to upgrade FortiAnalyzer without an upgrade path.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to solve the problem during FortiAnalyzer upgrade
incidents.solution: When trying to upgrade FortiAnalyzer, PostgresSQL maybe stuck at 41% with a console alert 'fail to upgrade postgres'. diagnose sql status upgrade-db Upgrading log SQL database 41%, stage: [Upgrade] started at: Tue Jul 1 17:09:18 2025 This is happening when trying to upgrade FortiAnalyzer without an upgrade path. Check the upgrade path in the link: Upgrade Path Tool Run the command below on the FortiAnalyzer that is having the issue and try to rebuild the database again: execute sql-local rebuild-db This command will cause the FortiAnalyzer to reboot, purge the analytics database, and start inserting the archive logs into the PostgreSQL/ClickHouse database. Although this procedure does not remove any log files, it is highly recommended to take a VM snapshot and/or back up the system configuration and log files to an external FTP server. Since this will rebuild the SQL database for all ADOMs, it may take a long time to complete, depending on the volume of logs stored and the current system resources available. There is no way to speed up this process

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Cannot access FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer via the GUI after upgrade
incidents.summary: Description This article describes a general fix for situations where the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer GUI is inaccessible after a firmware upgrade. The user is unable to access the GUI, and the service is not running, resulting in a defunct state. Scope FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer. Solution Context: In this scenario, the user has encountered problems accessing FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer through the GUI after a firmware upgrade.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a general fix for situations where the FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer GUI is inaccessible after a firmware upgrade. The user is unable to access the GUI, and the service is not running, resulting in a defunct state
incidents.solution: Context: In this scenario, the user has encountered problems accessing FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer through the GUI after a firmware upgrade. The message received in the browser is 'Connection_refused'. Access is established via the CLI, and the user ensures the device is working properly after the upgrade. Validation process: Check the current administrator settings and confirm no changes were made, and that HTTPS access continues using port 443 and HTTP 80. Enable a packet capture in FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer using port 443 and confirm the packets are received to eliminate the possibility of a network issue. Verify that the correct upgrade path was applied correctly (from the latest 7.2 version to v7.4.10) (run diagnose cdb upgrade summary ). Confirm there were no crashes related to the HTTP service ( run diagnose debug crash read ). Validate the current process list and status in process execution. In the current execution process, httpd is tagged as defunct, and checking the current process list shows httpd in a zombie status. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiAnalyzer prompts 'command fail. Return code 256' when executing 'execute sensor list'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to troubleshoot the 'command fail. Return code 256' prompt in FortiAnalyzer after executing the CLI command 'execute sensor list'. Scope FortiAnalyzer ,FortiManager Solution Ensure the affected FortiAnalyzer/FortiManager model comes with IPMI ( The Intelligent Platform Management Interface). For more information, see Technical Tip: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer models that support monitoring of sensor readings .
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to troubleshoot the 'command fail. Return code 256' prompt in FortiAnalyzer after executing the CLI command 'execute sensor list'
incidents.solution: Ensure the affected FortiAnalyzer/FortiManager model comes with IPMI ( The Intelligent Platform Management Interface). For more information, see Technical Tip: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer models that support monitoring of sensor readings . Perform the troubleshooting steps below: Gracefully shut down the FortiAnalyzer. It is necessary to keep integrity of the file system and DB: exec shutdown Unplug power cords and follow the next step while all power cords are disconnected: Press down the system power button (front-top-right) and hold it down for 30 seconds. Release the power button (after 30sec) Reconnect all power cords. Power up the device by pressing the power button. Once FortiAnalyzer boots up, run the command again. exec sensor list FortiAnalyzer should be able to display the output of 'exec sensor list'. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: How to resolve FortiAnalyzer 7.6 version showing Rebuilding SQL database status stuck at 99% for long time
incidents.summary: Description This article explains how to resolve FortiAnalyzer 7.6 version GUI alert showing rebuilding SQL database stuck at 99% for long time and not proceeding further. Scope FortiAnalyzer v7.6.0 and later. Solution The FortiAnalyzer database upgrade from PostgreSQL (PSQL) to ClickHouse is an automatic background process that occurs when the FortiAnalyzer firmware is upgraded to version 7.6.0 or later. The database upgrade takes long time depending on the log database in FortiAnalyzer.
incidents.symptom: This article explains how to resolve FortiAnalyzer 7.6 version GUI alert showing rebuilding SQL database stuck at 99% for long time and not proceeding further
incidents.solution: The FortiAnalyzer database upgrade from PostgreSQL (PSQL) to ClickHouse is an automatic background process that occurs when the FortiAnalyzer firmware is upgraded to version 7.6.0 or later. The database upgrade takes long time depending on the log database in FortiAnalyzer. Sometimes the rebuilding database gets finished however the status shows stuck at 99% during the completion stage and it does not proceed further. FortiAnalyzer GUI shows an alert saying Rebuilding SQL database showing progress of 99% with a short estimated remaining time and not moving forward. To confirm the database upgrade is finished perform the following two steps, Run ' diagnose sql show db-size ' multiple times and verify the size of the database is not increasing. incidents.title: Technical Tip: FortiAnalyzer rejects the FGFM/OFTP connection attempts with error 'No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled/LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id'
incidents.summary: Description This article describes how to resolve a communication issue between FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer with the error 'No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled/LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id'. Scope FortiAnalyzer, FortiGate VM. Solution It is possible that after an upgrade to firmware branch v7.4 on FortiGate (v7.4.9) and FortiAnalyzer (v7.4.8), the connection between the devices is lost.
incidents.symptom: This article describes how to resolve a communication issue between FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer with the error 'No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled/LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id'
incidents.solution: It is possible that after an upgrade to firmware branch v7.4 on FortiGate (v7.4.9) and FortiAnalyzer (v7.4.8), the connection between the devices is lost. If the FortiGate is removed from the FortiAnalyzer at this point, it might not be possible to re-add the device anymore, with the error 'No devices are available for approval.'. On FortiGate, when trying to set up the connection again, the connection status may show as 'Unauthorized'. When testing connectivity from FortiGate-VM CLI, it shows the error below: FGT-VM# execute log fortianalyzer test-connectivity Testing connectivity to fortianalyzer ... Failed to get FAZ's status. oftp_connect(global-faz) failed: oftp failed to authenticate. Steps to troubleshoot connectivity issues between FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer may be found in this article: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiGate to FortiAnalyzer connectivity . However, the following error may be encountered on FortiAnalyzer when trying to re-establish the connection: Error No legal SN found in cert and legacy auth mode disabled LOGIN_REQUEST_LEGACY error: invalid device id. incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Internal error when viewing FortiMail log via FortiAnalyzer supervisor
incidents.summary: Description This article describes the steps to resolve the internal error that occurs when trying to view FortiMail log via FortiAnalyzer supervisor. Scope FortiMail, FortiAnalyzer, FortiSandbox. Solution When using FortiAnalyzer supervisor, selecting Log View -> Logs -> All and then filtering by FortiMail, FortiSandbox (Or any device other than FortiGate), the error message 'Internal error: failed to start fof log search ' is displayed, as shown below: This is happening because the user is accessing 'LogView - All', which are SIEM logs.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the steps to resolve the internal error that occurs when trying to view FortiMail log via FortiAnalyzer supervisor
incidents.solution: When using FortiAnalyzer supervisor, selecting Log View -> Logs -> All and then filtering by FortiMail, FortiSandbox (Or any device other than FortiGate), the error message 'Internal error: failed to start fof log search ' is displayed, as shown below: This is happening because the user is accessing 'LogView - All', which are SIEM logs. The device filter in Supervisor is member/ADOM level, so when a user selects 'FortiMail' in the device list, it visits the member's default FortiMail ADOM SIEM logs. But the default FortiMail ADOM does not support SIEM logs, hence the request is failing.
